Establishing cardiovascular safety of the small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist orforglipron in type 2 diabetes.
Rising Obesity-Driven Cardiac Mortality Among Young Adults in the United States: A 25-Year Retrospective Analysis (1999-2023).
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity is a growing risk factor for cardiovascular disease and mortality in the United States, particularly among younger adults. METHODS: Using the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple Cause of Death database, we retrospectively analyzed trends and disparities in obesity-related cardiac mortality among US individuals aged 15 to 44 years from 1999 to 2023, stratified by sex, race, urbanization, and census region. Deaths were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes for obesity and cardiac conditions, including ischemic heart disease, sudden cardiac death, arrhythmias, and heart failure. Age-adjusted mortality rates were calculated using joinpoint regression and expressed as annual percentage change with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2023, 51 860 obesity-related cardiac deaths were recorded. The age-adjusted mortality rates increased from 0.9 (95% CI, 0.8-0.9) to 2.5 (95% CI, 2.4-2.6) per 100 000. Mortality was highest during the COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2021). Men consistently had higher age-adjusted mortality rates than women. Black or African American and American Indian/Alaska Native individuals showed the highest racial disparities. The South and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest regional mortality, with Alaska recording the highest state-level age-adjusted mortality rate in 2023 (6.0 per 100 000). Mortality largely returned to baseline across most groups from 2021 to 2023. CONCLUSIONS: Obesity-related cardiac mortality has risen in the United States over the past 2 decades with notable disparities across sex, race, region, and urbanization. These findings underscore the need for targeted public health interventions in high-risk populations to reduce premature cardiovascular deaths and reverse this trend.

recs.title: Beyond the Gradient: Patient-Reported Outcomes with Aficamten in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
Glycosylated Fibronectin Compared With sFlt-1/PlGF Ratio for Preeclampsia Assessment.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The ratio of sFlt-1 (soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1) to PlGF (placental growth factor) is an established biomarker for preeclampsia diagnostic triage. GlyFn (glycosylated fibronectin) measured by point-of-care testing is an alternative rapid assessment from finger-stick blood samples. This study was designed to test the hypothesis that the sensitivity of GlyFn is noninferior to that of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio in women with suspected preeclampsia. METHODS: This prospective observational study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of both tests for preeclampsia in high-risk participants presenting between 24+0 and 36+6 weeks of gestation at 5 hospitals from January 2024 to July 2025. Participants underwent simultaneous point-of-care GlyFn testing (Lumella) and laboratory sFlt-1/PlGF ratio measurements. The primary outcome was birth for preeclampsia within 28 days of testing. Thresholds were set at GlyFn ≥350 μg/mL and sFlt-1/PlGF ratio ≥38. The noninferiority margin was predefined at 5%. RESULTS: Among 397 participants, 59 (14.9%) had an indicated birth for preeclampsia within 28 days. GlyFn showed a sensitivity of 86.44% (95% CI, 75.02%-93.96%) compared with sFlt-1/PlGF 84.75% (95% CI, 73.01%-92.78%). Although sensitivities were numerically similar (P=0.79), the CI around the difference was too wide to establish noninferiority at the 5% margin. Negative predictive values were 96.40% and 96.59%, respectively. However, GlyFn had a lower specificity (63.31% versus 75.44%, P<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Point-of-care GlyFn testing showed similar sensitivity and negative predictive value to the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio for predicting an indicated birth for preeclampsia within 28 days. The point-of-care nature of the GlyFn test may facilitate immediate clinical decision-making in diverse healthcare settings. REGISTRATION: URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN13430018; Unique identifier: ISRCTN13430018.

recs.title: Altered Intersubject Variability of Morphological Connectivity in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease and Its Associations With Gene Expression and Cell Types.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a heterogeneous disorder; however, interindividual variability in morphometric brain connectivity remains unclear, as does its association with gene expression. METHODS: We enrolled 65 patients with CSVD and 35 healthy controls. Individual-level morphometric brain networks were constructed from T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, and intersubject variability of morphometric connectivity (IVMC) was quantified using a Kullback-Leibler divergence-based gray matter similarity measure. Group differences in IVMC and its associations with cognitive and clinical measures were examined. Partial least squares regression was applied to Allen Human Brain Atlas data to relate IVMC to gene expression, cell-type specificity, and biological functions. RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with CSVD showed globally increased IVMC (P<0.001) and significant differences across multiple functional networks (all PFalse Discovery Rate<0.05). IVMC in the sensorimotor and ventral attention networks was associated with poorer Auditory-Verbal Learning Test performance. Partial least squares regression analysis revealed that IVMC-related genes were enriched in neurodevelopmental and metabolic processes, whereas negatively weighted genes were associated with synaptic structure and glutamatergic signaling. Cell-type analyses linked IVMC alterations primarily to neuronal and glial transcriptional signatures. CONCLUSIONS: CSVD is associated with elevated IVMC across multiple functional networks, with changes in specific networks linked to memory impairment. These alterations may be associated with genes involved in neurodevelopment, synaptic function, and diverse neuronal and glial cell types, providing new insights into the interindividual variability of brain networks and the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying CSVD.

recs.title: 1-Year Outcomes of Early Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
Effectiveness of Individualized Physical Exercise in COVID-19-Induced Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is common in post-COVID-19 condition and is associated with high symptom burden and reduced quality of life. Although physical exercise is recommended for POTS, evidence of its effectiveness remains limited. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to evaluate the effectiveness of tailored exercise on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), upright time, physical function, and symptom burden in individuals with COVID-19-induced POTS. METHODS: Adults with COVID-19-induced POTS were randomized to standard care or standard care plus tailored exercise with weekly supervision. Assessments were conducted at baseline and 16 weeks. Primary outcomes were HRQoL and upright time. Secondary outcomes included daily steps, sedentary time, orthostatic autonomic response, muscle strength, physical capacity, patient-reported activity limitations, mental health, and symptom burden. Analyses used mixed models. RESULTS: Data were analyzed from sixty participants (85% females, mean age 37 years). No time-by-group interaction effects were observed for HRQoL. Upright time was reduced in the intervention group compared with controls, with an estimated between-group difference of -31 min/day, (95% CI -57 to -6). For secondary outcomes, daily steps were reduced in the intervention group, whereas both groups improved in POTS symptoms, activity limitations, and physical capacity, with a trend toward reduced postexertional malaise. No other secondary outcomes showed significant effects. CONCLUSIONS: Tailored exercise did not outperform standard care in HRQoL and was associated with reduced upright time, whereas improvements in several secondary outcomes were observed in both groups. Heterogeneity supports an individualized approach to exercise, integrated with pharmacological and multimodal management strategies.

recs.title: Cardiovascular Complications of Chronic Liver Disease.
recs.abstract: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms-including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation-that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.

GDMT is Associated with Reduced Loop Diuretic Requirements, Whereas Diuretic Dose Does Not Modify GDMT Benefit in Heart Failure: STRONG-HF.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Loop diuretics (LD) are the cornerstone of congestion management in heart failure (HF), but whether their requirement can be reduced by optimizing disease-modifying therapy is unknown. METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of STRONG-HF (n=1,075 with post-randomization LD data), we assessed whether up-titration of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) lowers LD demand, and whether LD dose reflects HF severity, predicts outcome, or modifies the benefit of high-intensity care. Patients were grouped by furosemide-equivalent dose; change at day 90 was compared by achievement of 100% target GDMT doses. RESULTS: Higher LD doses marked more severe HF. Achieving 100% of target doses of all GDMT classes (RASi, beta-blocker, MRA) translated into a substantially lower diuretic requirement: furosemide-equivalent dose at day 90 fell by -21.94 (SD 52.46) mg versus -1.55 (SD 49.886) mg in those not reaching targets (p<0.001); beta-blockers showed the largest effect of any single class -18.42 (SD 49.61) mg, (p<0.001). LD dose category was not independently associated with the primary endpoint (all-cause death or HF rehospitalization at 180 days) or its components; only LD dose doubling was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.47, 95% CI 1.04-2.09), without association with the primary endpoint or rehospitalization (both p>0.05). The benefit of high-intensity care was consistent across LD dose groups (no treatment-by-dose interaction). CONCLUSIONS: GDMT optimization acted as diuretic-sparing therapy: reaching target doses, particularly of all three classes, was associated with markedly lower LD requirement. LD dose mirrored HF severity but neither consistently predicted outcome nor modified the benefit of up-titration.

recs.title: High-Potency P2Y12 Inhibitors Among Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI: An Analysis From the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical practice guidelines recommend the use of clopidogrel among patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The frequency of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, such as ticagrelor or prasugrel, in this setting is not well known. METHODS: Using the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI registry, we analyzed patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention from April 2018 to June 2024, excluding those discharged on oral anticoagulants. Temporal trends in high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription were examined. A mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression model with a random intercept for hospital was used to identify patient-, procedural-, and institutional-level factors associated with high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription while accounting for within-hospital clustering. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio. RESULTS: Among 783 977 patients across 1815 hospitals, 35% were prescribed a high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor at discharge. The use of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors declined from 35% in 2018 to 31% in 2024 (P-trend=0.019), driven by a reduction in ticagrelor (from 29% to 23%, P-trend <0.001) despite a modest increase in prasugrel use (from 6.2% to 8%, P-trend=0.10). Male sex, prior myocardial infarction, and markers of procedural complexity (high-complexity/type C lesions, left main coronary artery, proximal left anterior descending artery, or use of mechanical circulatory support) were associated with higher odds of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription. In contrast, older age (≥75 years), prior stroke/transient ischemic attack, prior coronary artery bypass graft, severe renal dysfunction, and chronic total occlusion were associated with lower odds. University hospitals had lower odds of prescribing high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with considerable variability in prescription patterns among institutions (median odds ratio, 2.59). CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-third of chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were discharged on high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with decreasing trends over time. Practice patterns reflected perceived ischemic versus bleeding risk and significant institutional variation, underscoring opportunities for quality improvement and guideline alignment.

recs.title: Anthocyanin and Blueberry Intake, Lipids, C-Reactive Protein, and the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in Women.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anthocyanins and anthocyanin-rich berries have demonstrated lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory effects; however, associations with cardiovascular disease remain mixed. We therefore examined anthocyanin and blueberry intake for prospective associations with cardiovascular disease risk and cross-sectional associations with lipids and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) in the WHS (Women's Health Study). METHODS: Among 38 088 women who completed a baseline semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire in 1992 to 1995, we estimated intake of total anthocyanins, 6 anthocyanin subclasses, and blueberries. Multivariable hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated for confirmed major adverse cardiovascular events, including nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and cardiovascular disease death. In a subset of 26 912 women with baseline blood samples, multivariable odds ratios were calculated for adverse lipid and hs-CRP levels. RESULTS: During a median 28.0-year follow-up, 2752 major adverse cardiovascular event cases occurred. Age-, energy-, and WHS treatment-adjusted HRs across quintiles of total anthocyanin intake were 1.00 (reference), 0.87 (95% CI, 0.78-0.98), 0.79 (95% CI, 0.70-0.89), 0.81 (95% CI, 0.72-0.91), and 0.88 (95% CI, 0.79-0.99) (P-trend=0.23). Further adjustment for clinical, lifestyle, and dietary factors showed no significant associations with major adverse cardiovascular events or their components, with similar null findings observed for anthocyanin subclasses and blueberries. In cross-sectional analyses, higher total anthocyanins and anthocyanin subclasses, except pelargonidin, were significantly associated with lower multivariable-adjusted odds of adverse high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides (all other P-trend<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In the WHS, anthocyanin and blueberry intake were not significantly associated with cardiovascular disease risk. However, higher anthocyanin intake was cross-sectionally associated with lower odds of adverse high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides.

recs.title: Long-Term Safety and Procedural Performance of an Interatrial Shunt for Heart Failure According to Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term device durability and phenotype-specific safety outcomes after interatrial shunting require further characterization. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the procedural success, device durability, and heart failure (HF) phenotype-specific safety outcomes of an interatrial shunt in the RELIEVE-HF trial. METHODS: Randomized patients were assigned 1:1 to shunt or sham control with prespecified stratification by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (LVEF ≤40%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF >40%). Procedural performance, device durability, serious adverse events (SAEs), major adverse cardiovascular or neurological events (MACNE), major bleeding, and renal outcomes were assessed through 2 years. RESULTS: Among 605 enrolled patients (508 randomized; 97 roll-in), shunt implantation was attempted in 370 and was successful in 369 (99.7%). Among implanted patients with follow-up (n = 348), no device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). Prespecified LVEF-stratified analyses demonstrated divergent safety profiles. In HFrEF, shunt therapy was not associated with excess all-cause MACNE, major bleeding, or renal decline and was associated with lower SAE burden. In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline. CONCLUSIONS: Interatrial shunt implantation was mechanically reliable and durable through 2 years. Safety outcomes differed by HF phenotype, with no evidence of excess clinical safety events in HFrEF but increased adverse events in HFpEF. These findings support phenotype-specific evaluation of interatrial shunt therapy. (REducing Lung congestion symptoms using the v-wavE shunt in adVancEd Heart Failure [RELIEVE-HF]; NCT03499236).

recs.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
recs.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

recs.title: Nuclear magnetic resonance-derived lipoprotein profile and risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation: a case-cohort design within the PREDIMAR trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lipoproteins could be potential biomarkers of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence (TAR) after catheter ablation; however, their association remains inconclusive and based exclusively on routine lipid measurements. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) enables detailed lipoprotein characterization beyond conventional assays. OBJECTIVE: To identify a baseline NMR-derived lipoprotein profile associated with the risk of TAR after catheter ablation. METHODS: We conducted a case-cohort study (212 cases and 238 participants in a random sub-cohort, with 93 overlapping cases) nested in the PREDIMAR (PRevención con DIeta Mediterránea de Arritmias Recurrentes) trial. Conventional lipoprotein profiles were measured using the Pentra C-200 and advanced lipoprotein profiles were assessed by NMR. Lipoprotein values were normalized and scaled to one standard deviation using Blom's inverse normal transformation. Cox models were used to assess the associations between baseline lipoproteins and TAR. Additionally, a cholesteryl ester transfer (CETP)-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was constructed and evaluated. RESULTS: After 18-month follow-up, higher baseline remnant cholesterol (hazard ratio = 1.26, 95% confidence interval= 1.06-1.51, per SD), higher cholesterol and triglyceride content in very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.22, 95% confidence interval= 1.03-1.46) or in intermediate-density lipoproteins (IDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.29, 95% confidence interval= 1.09-1.52), showed increased risks of TAR. Higher triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio was directly associated, and higher triglyceride-to-VLDL cholesterol and triglyceride-to-IDL cholesterol ratios were inversely associated with recurrence. A CETP-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was directly associated with recurrence. CONCLUSION: An atherogenic lipoprotein profile characterized by elevated remnant cholesterol is associated with a higher risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

recs.title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO. METHODS: The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed. RESULTS: Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P < 0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (4.9% vs 2.0% vs 1.3%; P < 0.001), and in-hospital cardiac arrest (6.1% vs 2.7% vs 1.6%; P < 0.001). Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001). Using a definition of ACO including TIMI flow grade 0 or 1, NSTEMI-ACO accounted for 216,054 presentations (24.4% of NSTEMI). In-hospital outcomes were similarly worse compared with NSTEMI-no-ACO and better compared with STEMI. CONCLUSIONS: ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

recs.title: Functional data for LDLR variant classification: comparative insights from high-content microscopy and flow cytometry assays.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: FH VCEP specifications for familial hypercholesterolemia variant interpretation assign a higher evidence weight to functional data from flow cytometry than microscopy assays. This restricts the use of microscopy assays for LDLR variant classification. We aimed to compare functional data obtained by both assays to determine whether microscopy-based assays could support a higher evidence level. METHODS: Fifty LDLR variants with available flow cytometry and microscopy data were compared for LDL uptake activity, including 21 newly characterized variants by microscopy. Variants were grouped by FH VCEP functional thresholds and results integrated with UK Biobank data to assess associations with lipid traits. RESULTS: We validated our microscopy assay with FH VCEP-classified control variants and compared functional activities measured by microscopy and flow cytometry assays, which showed significant correlation (r = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.473-0.795, p = 1.45 × 10-7) and a close average agreement (Bland-Altman bias = -0.05, 95% LoA: -0.69 to +0.60). Functional FH VCEP variant groups for both assays resulted in fair categorical agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.018-0.479). Integration with UK Biobank data showed that carriers of variants with reduced LDLR activity (<70% and <50%) had higher LDL-C, total cholesterol, and ApoB levels compared to those with normal activity (>90%) for both microscopy and flow cytometry assays, with more pronounced differences observed at the <50% LDLR activity threshold. CONCLUSION: Microscopy assays show concordance with flow cytometry, consistent associations with lipid phenotypes and our OddsPath calculations support re-evaluation of evidence weights for microscopy assays.

recs.title: Assisted Reproductive Technology and Risk of Congenital Heart Defects in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: To date, >10 million children have been conceived via assisted reproductive technology (ART) globally. However, there are some concerns about potential adverse outcomes associated with ART-conceived pregnancies, including the risk of congenital heart defects (CHDs). This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between ART and the risk of major CHDs as well as their specific subtypes. METHODS: Major electronic databases were screened for studies comparing the incidence of CHD following ART-conceived pregnancies versus spontaneous conception. The primary end point was study-defined incidence of CHDs. Secondary end points included incidence of tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great arteries, aortic coarctation, ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, pulmonary valve atresia, tricuspid valve atresia, and hypoplastic left heart. Pairwise meta-analyses were performed using frequentist random-effect models to calculate risk ratios and 95% CIs. RESULTS: Thirteen studies, encompassing a total of 45 916 925 subjects (4986 conceived via ART), were included in the quantitative synthesis. ART was significantly associated with a higher risk of major CHD compared with natural pregnancy (risk ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.68-3.28]), with significant heterogeneity across the studies. An increased risk of tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect following ART-conceived pregnancies was found, while no difference was found on other CHDs. Prespecified sensitivity analyses were in line with the primary findings of the meta-analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Our meta-analysis shows a potential link between ART and increased risk of major CHDs, particularly on tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect.

Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Detection and Management of Physiological Instability in Heart Failure: Results of the Randomized LINK-HF2 Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled wearable monitoring can detect individualized physiological deviations preceding heart failure (HF) decompensation, but whether these signals can be translated into improved outcomes remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility of integrating AI-generated notifications with a structured clinician response algorithm into postdischarge HF care and to explore their association with HF events following hospitalization. METHODS: LINK-HF2 (Detection of Physiological Anomaly Using Artificial Intelligence and Prevention of Heart Failure Hospitalization) was a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint study conducted at 5 Veterans Affairs medical centers. Adults hospitalized for acute HF were enrolled at discharge and assigned to AI-guided monitoring with clinician notification or to standard care. All participants wore a continuous multisensor patch for up to 90 days. A personalized similarity-based model detected deviations in cardiorespiratory and activity signals and generated notifications. Implementation outcomes included feasibility, acceptability, and usability. The main exploratory clinical endpoint was HF rehospitalization. Secondary exploratory clinical endpoints included the composite outcome of all-cause unplanned rehospitalizations, emergency department visits, and all-cause mortality. All clinical endpoints were compared through Cox proportional hazards models over the follow-up period. RESULTS: Among 171 analyzed participants, 80 (46.8%) were assigned to intervention and 91 (53.2%) to control. Median monitoring adherence was 72.4% of follow-up days; clinicians responded to communicated notifications within a median of 1 day (range: 1-5 days), and qualitative analysis demonstrated high patient acceptance and clinician engagement, whereas identifying workflow integration and response uncertainty as the primary barriers to implementation. In exploratory analyses, HF rehospitalization occurred in 13 (16.3%) patients in the intervention group and 17 (18.7%) in the control group (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.43-1.84; P = 0.76). The composite clinical endpoint also did not differ between groups (HR 1.03; 95% CI: 0.63-1.70; P = 0.89). The intervention group had a lower rate of AI-detected physiological instability than controls (HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.60-0.97; P = 0.025). CONCLUSIONS: AI-enabled continuous physiological monitoring was feasible and reduced AI-detected physiological instability. Although this feasibility study did not demonstrate a reduction in exploratory clinical events, these findings highlight that accurate physiological risk detection alone may be insufficient to modify clinical risk without mechanistically aligned and trusted therapeutic responses. (Detection of Physiological Anomaly Using Artificial Intelligence and Prevention of Heart Failure Hospitalization [LINK-HF2]; NCT04502563).

recs.title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. OBJECTIVE: To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. RESULTS: Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

recs.title: Sex-Based Differences in Chronic Heart Failure: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-based disparities in patient enrollment and treatment effects in heart failure (HF) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been reported. We aim to systematically analyze sex-based enrollment and treatment effect differences in HF RCTs over time. METHODS: RCTs enrolling patients with chronic HF were systematically searched on PubMed-MEDLINE. Eligible trials included pharmacological or device-based interventions with a hard primary endpoint (mortality and hospitalization) and reporting enrollment of women. Sex-specific treatment effects (HR or RR) were extracted. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, and pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 56 RCTs (39 drug, 17 device) were included. The pooled proportion of women enrollment was 27.0% (95%CI: 22.0% to 32.4%) in drug trials and 25.3% (95%CI: 21.0% to 29.9%) in device trials. Women were more underrepresented in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) than in HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) trials (21.0% vs 49.6%, p < 0.001). Among drug trials reporting sex-specific effects, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 0.94 (95%CI 0.89-1.01) and RR was 0.81 (95%CI 0.68-0.96), suggesting potentially greater benefit for women. No interaction was observed between HFrEF and HFpEF trials (HR: p = 0.44; RR: p = 0.95). The pooled interaction estimate on event counts was 0.90 (95%CI 0.84-0.96). For devices, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 1.05 (95%CI 0.90-1.22) and RR was 0.68 (95%CI 0.50-0.93). CONCLUSION: Women remain underrepresented in HF RCTs. Sex-stratified analyses suggest a potentially greater relative benefit of drug intervention in women, which might inform future RCTs. Further studies are required to investigate the mechanisms of these differences.

recs.title: Nonlinear 24-Hour Blood Pressure Dynamics in Cognitive Impairment and Dementia.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In cognitive impairment and dementia, where biological functions are disrupted, nonlinear dynamics may reflect dysregulation of blood pressure (BP) that might not be captured by linear variability. We investigated whether nonlinear dynamics of 24-hour BP variability are associated with cognitive impairment and dementia. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 4854 participants from 3 population-based studies. Raw 24-hour ambulatory BP recordings were structured as time series to quantify nonlinear variability using sample entropy, detrended fluctuation analysis, and Poincaré measures. High entropy and Poincaré values with low detrended fluctuation analysis suggest irregular dynamics, whereas the opposite pattern indicates a predictable BP system. Neurological outcomes included Mini-Mental State Examination, mild cognitive impairment (n=212), and dementia (n=111). RESULTS: The mean age was 67.6±7.89 years (61.0% women). Higher 24-hour systolic BP entropy and Poincaré measures were associated with lower Mini-Mental State Examination; adjusted-mean Mini-Mental State Examination estimates ranged from -0.119 (95% CI, -0.184 to -0.053) to -0.035 (95% CI, -0.060 to -0.010). These measures were also associated with higher odds for prevalent mild cognitive impairment (odds ratios [OR] ≥1.41) and dementia (ORs ranged from 1.32 [95% CI, 1.08-1.60] to 2.36 [95% CI, 1.49-3.74]). Lower detrended fluctuation analysis was related to dementia (OR, 1.64 [95% CI, 1.01-2.68]). Sex, antihypertensive medication, and measures of linear variability did not modify the association between nonlinear variability and cognitive outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Nonlinear 24-hour BP dynamics were associated with cognitive impairment and dementia. Nonlinear patterns of irregular 24-hour variability may represent a form of BP dysregulation relevant to dementia.

recs.title: "Baseline Characteristics and Utilization of Medical Therapies in Acute Hospitalized and Chronic Heart Failure Patients Enrolled in GRASP-HF: Differences Between ICARe-HF and Non-ICARe-HF Centres".
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Global Registries and Surveys Programme-Heart Failure (GRASP-HF) is a prospective, multicentre, international observational study assessing implementation of the 2021/2023 ESC-HF-Guidelines. GRASP-HF is aligned with the Improving Care through Accreditation and Recognition in Heart Failure (ICARe-HF) programme, which links centre-characteristics with guideline-implementation performance. AIMS: To compare baseline characteristics, guideline-directed-medical-therapy (GDMT) implementation, and in-hospital outcomes between GRASP-HF patients managed in centres participating or not participating in the ICARe-HF programme. METHODS: GRASP-HF patients were stratified by ICARe-HF participation, clinical settings, acute (AHF) vs chronic HF (CHF) and ejection fraction (EF) subtypes. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models evaluated associations with quadruple therapy implementation and in-hospital mortality. RESULTS: Among 10,936 patients (63.3% CHF, 36.7% AHF), patients from ICARe-HF participating centres (51.3%) were older, more comorbid but with less severe congestion. In both CHF and AHF, ICARe-HF centres demonstrated greater GDMT utilization, particularly angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors and sodium-glucose-cotransporter-2 inhibitors. In HFrEF, quadruple therapy was more frequently implemented (47% vs 40% in CHF; 27% vs 24% at AHF discharge) and remained associated with ICARe-HF participation after adjustment, Odd Ratio (OR) =1.73, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) :1.17-2.55. Target doses remained suboptimal, particularly after AHF. Although crude in-hospital mortality was lower in ICARe-HF centres (2.3% vs 5.5%), this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (OR=0.87, 95% CI:0.48-1.56). CONCLUSIONS: Participation in the ICARe-HF programme was associated with more comprehensive implementation of contemporary GDMT, particularly in HFrEF. The association with in-hospital mortality was attenuated after adjustment and should be considered exploratory.

recs.title: Should Valve-to-Coronary Volume Incorporate Leaflet Burden?
AI-assisted scoping review of code sharing in clinical prediction model research.
recs.abstract: Clinical prediction models are increasingly deployed to support diagnostic and prognostic decisions, making reproducibility essential for assessing their reliability and generalizability. Analytical code supports independent assessment of these processes, yet its availability in the literature remains limited. This scoping review quantifies current practices in sharing analytical code to inform the development of TRIPOD-Code, a reporting guideline for code availability and reproducibility. Here a large-language-model-assisted pipeline was developed to screen articles citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI, extract repository links and assess retrieved repositories against 14 predefined reproducibility-related features. Among 3,967 articles, 482 (12.2%) included code-sharing statements. Sharing prevalence varied widely by journal and country. Repository assessment showed substantial heterogeneity in reproducibility features. These findings underscore the need for clearer expectations beyond code availability, including documentation, dependency specification and executable structure. Strengthening these practices may improve the usability of clinical prediction model studies and support their deployment in real-world clinical settings.

recs.title: Plasma Glutamine and Glutamate in Relation to Clinical Outcomes After Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter Prospective Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glutamine (Gln) and glutamate (Glu) have been suggested to play a pivotal role in neuronal homeostasis and metabolic regulation, showing potential as prognostic biomarkers for stroke. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of plasma Gln, Glu, and glutamine-to-glutamate ratio (GGR) with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke. METHODS: This secondary analysis of the multicenter CATIS (China Antihypertensive Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke) included 3499 participants with ischemic stroke. Plasma Gln and Glu levels were measured within 24 hours of hospital admission using ultraperformance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. The primary outcome was unfavorable functional outcome (death or major disability) at 3 months after ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes included major disability, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular events. Risk discrimination and reclassification of Glu metabolites were assessed. RESULTS: Compared with the lowest quartiles, multivariable-adjusted odds ratios of the primary outcome in the highest quartiles were 0.37 (95% CI, 0.28-0.47) for Gln, 2.05 (95% CI, 1.60-2.62) for Glu, and 0.37 (95% CI, 0.29-0.48) for GGR (all P for trend <0.001). Approximately 9% of the associations of Glu metabolites and unfavorable functional outcome were mediated by the composite marker of inflammation and insulin resistance. Incorporating Gln, Glu, and GGR into conventional risk factor models improved risk discrimination and stratification for unfavorable functional outcome, with increases in C statistics (from 0.831 to 0.842-0.848), net reclassification indices (22.9%-31.0%), and integrated discrimination improvements (1.1%-1.6%) (all P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Plasma Gln, Glu, and GGR were associated with adverse clinical outcomes, providing prognostic significance in patients with ischemic stroke. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01840072.

recs.title: Thoracic Intermuscular Adiposity, Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction, and Prognosis After Cardiac Surgery.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Body mass index is a widely-used yet imprecise measure of adiposity. Thoracic intermuscular adiposity is reported to be related with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), but their prognostic implications after cardiac surgery are not clear. This study aimed to investigate whether computed tomography-derived thoracic intermuscular adiposity and CMD provide better prognostic information than body mass index in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. METHODS: This study consecutively enrolled 666 patients undergoing elective surgery from 3 centers. Using computed tomography at the T12 vertebral level, we quantified the cross-sectional areas (cm2) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, and intermuscular adipose tissue. Intermuscular fat fraction was calculated as intermuscular adipose tissue/(intermuscular adipose tissue+skeletal muscle)×100%. CMD was defined by a coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance >25. The primary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and rehospitalization for heart failure. RESULTS: A total of 63 MACEs (9.5%) occurred during a median 17-month follow-up. Obesity defined by body mass index (10.7% of patients) was not associated with MACE (P=0.187). Each 1% increase in intermuscular fat fraction was significantly associated with CMD (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.14-1.31]; P<0.001), whereas body mass index showed no such correlation (P=0.964). CMD independently predicted MACE (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.03; [95% CI: 1.15-3.61]; P = 0.015), whereas intermuscular fat fraction did not (P=0.516). The annualized MACE rate was significantly higher in patients with CMD (11.0% versus 5.2%, P=0.004). CONCLUSIONS: Computed tomography-derived intermuscular adiposity correlated strongly with CMD, and preprocedural CMD was associated with a higher risk of MACE after cardiac surgery. External validation and prospective studies are warranted.

recs.title: Sex Differences in the Prevalence, Medical Therapy, and Outcomes in Heart Failure With Improved Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with improved ejection fraction (HFimpEF) is a rapidly growing clinical entity. There is little understanding of how sex relates to the epidemiology, predictors, and trajectory of HFimpEF. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to describe sex-based differences in the epidemiology, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use, and clinical outcomes among patients with HFimpEF within a large, diverse health care system. METHODS: The authors identified adults with incident heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction ≤40%) between 2013 and 2022. HFimpEF was defined as a subsequent ejection fraction measurement >40% within the following 12 months. Sex was based on self-report. Among patients with HFimpEF, the authors examined GDMT use at the time of incident HFrEF, HFimpEF, and 1 year following HFimpEF, stratified by sex. They examined the incidence of worsening heart failure (WHF) events and all-cause death 1 year postincident HFrEF. We compared event rates between patients with HFimpEF and persistent HFrEF, adjusted for demographic and clinical characteristics. RESULTS: Among 28,292 patients with incident HFrEF (females: 34.8%), 35.2% experienced HFimpEF. Females were more likely to experience HFimpEF in the 12 months following HFrEF than males (36.5% vs 34.5%, P < 0.0001). Among patients with HFimpEF, GDMT use was similar among females and males and declined after incident HFimpEF in both sexes. Compared with patients with persistent HFrEF, patients with HFimpEF had better WHF outcomes and all-cause death outcomes, which was consistent by sex. However, females with HFimpEF had higher rates of WHF compared with males with HFimpEF, even when adjusted for clinical covariates. CONCLUSIONS: HFimpEF is associated with improved outcomes for both females and males. However, females with HFimpEF have higher rates of WHF events compared with males.

recs.title: Timing of Nonculprit PCI for STEMI and Multivessel Disease.
Practical Approaches to Coronary Venous Ethanol Ablation for Refractory Ventricular Arrhythmias: Technique Selection and Clinical Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary venous ethanol ablation (CVEA) is a promising alternative for refractory ventricular arrhythmias (VAs); however, it has limited availability, lacks guideline support, and comprises heterogeneous procedural techniques. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the acute efficacy, safety, and long-term outcomes of CVEA in refractory VAs and outline practical techniques of CVEA. METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing VA ablation at our center between December 2017 and December 2025 were screened; CVEA was performed after unsuccessful endocardial RFA. We performed CVEA using either tip injection, conventional double-balloon, or modified double-balloon techniques based on venous anatomy. RESULTS: Among 204 consecutive patients undergoing VA ablation, 55 had VAs refractory to endocardial RFA. Of these, 42 with a coronary venous electrogram preceding VA onset by >20 ms underwent CVEA, including 33 with premature ventricular contraction (PVC) and 9 with ventricular tachycardia (VT). Acute success was achieved in 32/33 patients with PVC and all patients with VT. During a median follow-up of 1,024 days, long-term success was achieved in 22 patients with PVC and 5 with VT. No association was observed between intraprocedural findings and long-term recurrence. CVEA-related procedural complications occurred in 13 patients, with no fatal events reported. Exploratory analyses suggested favorable outcomes for the modified double-balloon technique in anatomically selected cases and an association between higher ethanol volume and ethanol-related complications. CONCLUSION: In patients with VAs refractory to endocardial RFA, CVEA was associated with favorable acute and long-term outcomes, with no fatal complications. Technique selection should be tailored to the venous anatomy, with judicious ethanol volume adjustment.

recs.title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
recs.abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

recs.title: Rescue TAVR After Ozaki Procedure.
Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial. METHODS: Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients. CONCLUSIONS: OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

recs.title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD. METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

recs.title: Trends in Use of Coronary Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Over a Decade in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass graft are among the most commonly performed procedures globally. The influence of recent scientific evidence on national-level temporal trends remains poorly explored. METHODS: The frequency, characteristics, and outcomes of elective and nonelective coronary angiography, PCI, and coronary artery bypass graft were described using the French National Hospitalization Database from 2014 to 2023 (covering a population of 67.0 million inhabitants), totaling 6 290 951 coronary interventions among 2 985 822 patients (mean age, 67.8±12.2 years; 69.9% men). RESULTS: Over 10 years, the annual number of coronary interventions increased by 33%, driven by a rise in coronary angiography (+32%) and PCI (+40%), while coronary artery bypass graft decreased (-8%). The growth in PCI was predominantly related to an increase in elective procedures (from 53.5% to 56.9%, P<0.001), particularly among older patients (+73%), and in multivessel disease (from 16.7% in 2014-2015 to 19.0% in 2022-2023, P<0.001). Attempts to recanalize chronic total coronary occlusion doubled (from 1.9% to 3.3%, P<0.001). In-hospital death after PCI decreased (from 2.05% in 2014 to 1.58% in 2023, P for trend<0.001), with the most notable improvements observed in nonelective PCI. Similarly, in-hospital death after coronary artery bypass graft declined (from 3.5% to 2.9%, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore a significant increase in both coronary angiography and PCI over the past decade in France, particularly in procedures classified as elective among older patients. This trend raises questions about the influence of recent scientific evidence and guidelines on clinical practice in this country.

recs.title: Under Pressure: Right Ventricular Obstruction by Pericardial Cyst.
Making every vial count: fractional dosing of yellow fever vaccine.
Opportunities to Address Barriers to Enrollment in Food is Medicine Programs: Lessons Learned From the SUPeRFOOD Trial.
Minimally Invasive Versus Sternotomy in Redo Mitral Valve Surgery: Short- and Long-Term Outcomes with Meta-Regression and Time-to-Event Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Redo mitral valve surgery carries substantial risk, and the relative benefits of minimally invasive (MI-MVS) versus sternotomy MVS, particularly regarding long-term survival, remain uncertain. METHODS: Electronic databases were searched for studies comparing MI-MVS with sternotomy MVS in adult redo MVS. Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized to reconstruct individual patient data for time-to-event analysis, with study-level hazard ratios (HR) generated using a Cox frailty model. Perioperative outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses evaluated propensity-matched cohorts, endoscopic/video-assisted minithoracotomy, and direct-vision minithoracotomy. Meta-regression explored the impact of study-level covariates on mortality. RESULTS: Fifteen studies including 3457 patients were analyzed. MI-MVS was associated with lower perioperative mortality compared with sternotomy MVS (odds ratio [OR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.23-0.48]; P<0.001), reduced incidence of reoperation (OR, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.44-0.98]; P=0.04), and acute kidney injury (OR, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.39-0.87]; P=0.008); rates of stroke and arrhythmia were similar. The direction and magnitude of the mortality effect consistently favored MI-MVS in the subgroup analyses. Time-to-event analysis demonstrated improved survival with MI-MVS (HR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.62-0.89]; P=0.001), but this was attenuated in the propensity-matched analysis. Meta-regression showed that sex distribution, mean age, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction did not significantly moderate mortality effects. CONCLUSIONS: In redo MVS, MI-MVS is associated with improved perioperative outcomes without compromising long-term survival; however, attenuation of the survival difference after propensity matching suggests that this long-term advantage may reflect baseline risk rather than procedural effect.

recs.title: Patient Characteristics and Outcomes Associated With Home-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Referrals to and participation in cardiac rehabilitation programs remain suboptimal. We examined factors associated with home-based cardiac rehabilitation (HBCR) referral and participation and associations of referral and participation with outcomes. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included adults ≥18 years of age from Kaiser Permanente Southern California with a HBCR-qualifying event or procedure between January 2021 and September 2024. HBCR referral and, separately, participation was identified within 90 days. Outcomes included 30-, 180-, and 365-day hospitalizations and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Among 44 468 adults, 13 164 (29.6%) received a referral within 90 days. Those receiving versus not receiving a referral were younger (mean age 65.6 versus 70.6 years) and more often male (71.4% versus 59.5%). Referral was associated with a lower likelihood of 180-day all-cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (prevalence ratio [PR], 0.86 [95% CI, 0.82-0.91] and PR, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.66-0.82]), and 365-day all-cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (PR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.79-0.86] and PR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.66-0.75]). Participation was associated with a lower likelihood of 30-day all-cause hospitalization (PR, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.66-0.92]), 180-day all-cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (PR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.75-0.91] and PR, 0.85 [95% CI, 0.74-0.98]), and 365-day all-cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (PR, 0.89 [95% CI, 0.82-0.96] and PR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.98]). CONCLUSIONS: Older adults and women had lower HBCR referral highlighting persistent gaps. Lower hospitalization risk associated with timely HBCR referral and participation underscores the importance of appropriate patient screening to improve outcomes.

recs.title: Outcomes in patients with diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and heart failure treated with tirzepatide or dulaglutide: SURPASS-CVOT analysis.
recs.abstract: AIMS: The impact of tirzepatide and dulaglutide on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and heart failure (HF) outcomes according to HF status is unknown. METHODS AND RESULTS: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were treated with tirzepatide up to 15 mg or dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly (average 4 years). The incidence of MACE-3 [cardiovascular (CV) death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke], MACE-4 (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization) and composite of all-cause or CV death and hospitalization or urgent visits for HF were analysed in patients with and without a history of HF. A history of HF (20.3%) was associated with more coronary artery disease and prior MI. Incidences of event categories were higher in the HF group. The hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause death or hospitalization or urgent visits for HF on tirzepatide vs. dulaglutide was 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.70-0.99] in patients with HF and 0.88 (95%CI 0.78-1.00) without HF. The HR for CV death or hospitalization or urgent visits for HF was 0.85 (95%CI 0.70-1.03) and 0.96 (95%CI 0.83-1.12), for MACE-3 0.90 (95%CI 0.76-1.08) and 0.93 (95%CI 0.83-1.04), and for MACE-4 0.81 (95%CI 0.69-0.95) and 0.91 (95%CI 0.83-1.00) in patients with and without HF, respectively. The patient-reported outcomes of APPADL and EQ-5D-5L visual analogue scores improved and were higher on tirzepatide in both groups. CONCLUSION: With overall non-inferiority established, this exploratory analysis revealed lower rates of the composite of all-cause death or HF events, or MACE-4 among patients with T2D and HF treated with tirzepatide compared with dulaglutide.

recs.title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) presents with variable risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. Genetic diagnosis guides sudden death prevention strategies, but risk magnitude for arrhythmogenic genes remains unknown. This study leveraged the international Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe) to address this gap and improve risk stratification. METHODS: Effects of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in genes associated with DCM and ventricular arrhythmia on clinical events were analysed in DCM-SHaRe patients. Patients were stratified by presence of a P/LP variant in a high-arrhythmogenic risk gene (LMNA, DSP, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, SCN5A, DES, TMEM43), a low-arrhythmogenic risk gene (TTN, TNNT2, MYH7, others), or gene-elusive. Outcomes included age-, sex-, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-adjusted risk of major ventricular arrhythmia (MVA), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), death, and their composite. RESULTS: Among 2660 genotyped adults with DCM (mean diagnosis age 47 ± 15 years, 39.8% female), 434 (16%) had P/LP variants in high-arrhythmogenic genes, 451 (17%) in low-arrhythmogenic genes, and 1775 (67%) were gene-elusive. Compared with gene-elusive patients, patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants showed increased MVA [hazard ratio (HR) 3.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.63-4.01], AF (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.96-2.98), HF (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.89-3.19), and composite (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.69-2.29) risk, which remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, and LVEF. Patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants and LVEF ≥ 50% maintained increased MVA (HR 2.36, 95% CI 1.59-3.51) and composite (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.25-2.12) risk. CONCLUSIONS: Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

recs.title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). RESULTS: After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I2 = 0%; τ2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

recs.title: Left Ventricular End-Diastolic Diameter Predicts Clinical Outcomes in Patients Supported With Surgically Implanted Microaxial Flow Pump.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study sought to determine the impact of left ventricular size on clinical outcomes after a microaxial flow pump was surgically implanted. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included patients who received a surgical microaxial left ventricular assist device from May 2020 to February 2024 at 2 high-volume centers in the United States. Patients were categorized into 2 groups based on their preimplant left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD): "small LVEDD," defined as LVEDD ≤5.5 cm, and "large LVEDD," defined as LVEDD >5.5 cm, respectively. End points were all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation, in-hospital death, death 30-days after discharge, and survival at 30-month follow-up. RESULTS: Two-hundred sixty-two patients received an Impella 5.5. Preimplant LVEDD was documented in 194 (74%) patients, where 50 patients had LVEDD ≤5.5 cm and 144 patients had LVEDD >5.5 cm. Patients with a small LVEDD had a higher rate of all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation (32% versus 11.8%, P=0.002), in-hospital death (42% versus 20.1%, P=0.004), and death 30 days after discharge (44% versus 20.8%, P=0.003). In adjusted analyses, patients with a greater LVEDD had 62% decreased risk of long-term death (hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.19-0.76]; P=0.001), compared with patients with a smaller LVEDD. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, all-comer study, we found that patients with reduced left ventricular dimension who required an Impella 5.5 had worse outcomes. Further research is warranted to recapitulate our observations across more centers.

recs.title: Arrhythmic Risk in Titin Cardiomyopathy: More Than a Question of Phenotype.
Permissive Cardiotoxicity: An Evolving Paradigm.
recs.abstract: Permissive cardiotoxicity is an evolving clinical practice pattern that balances the management of cancer treatment-associated cardiotoxicities with the risk of interrupting lifesaving or life-extending cancer treatments. This paradigm shift has been catalyzed by advancements in the diagnostic and therapeutic tools available to treating clinicians, as well as a recognition of the consequences of withholding or delaying cancer therapy. Permissive cardiotoxicity has become a central tenet in the practice of cardio-oncologists; however, recognition and confidence in managing cardiotoxicity is also crucial for the general cardiologist and oncologist due to the growing population of patients with cancer. This review aims to (1) highlight the philosophy of permissive cardiotoxicity, (2) provide a framework for risk stratification of cardiovascular toxicities, (3) describe systems of care considerations for successful implementation of permissive cardiotoxicity, and (4) review the existing literature and guideline recommendations for specific cardiovascular toxicity mitigation.

recs.title: Bending the Curve: Revealing Population Risk With Quantitative Atherosclerotic Plaque.
Classification and Outcomes of Coronary Microvascular Disease in Myocardial Infarction and Angina With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCAs) and angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCAs) present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We assessed the frequency of coronary microvascular disease (CMD) and its subtypes in MINOCA compared with ANOCA and evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: Patients with nonobstructive coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary function testing from 2012 to 2022 were prospectively enrolled and retrospectively classified as MINOCA or ANOCA (reference group). Myocardial infarction due to atherothrombosis, myocarditis, and Takotsubo syndrome were excluded. Invasive provocation testing was performed. CMD was classified as endothelium-independent (coronary flow reserve <2.5 with adenosine) and endothelium-dependent (<50% increase in coronary blood flow with acetylcholine). Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, urgent revascularization, stroke) were recorded over 8 years. RESULTS: Of 622 patients, 73 (12%) had MINOCA (69% female, median age 56 years) and 549 (88%) ANOCA (72% female, median age 53 years). CMD was common in both groups (71% versus 64%; P=0.271), while endothelium-independent CMD was more frequent in MINOCA (41% versus 21%; P<0.001). Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred more often in MINOCA (40% versus 11%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.4; P=0.001). CMD predicted higher major adverse cardiovascular events in both MINOCA (hazard ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-12.0]; P=0.038) and ANOCA (hazard ratio, 7.9 [95% CI, 2.9-21.8]; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: CMD is common in both MINOCA and ANOCA. The higher prevalence of endothelium-independent CMD in MINOCA suggests a potential mechanistic role in infarction. Patients with MINOCA have a worse prognosis than ANOCA, particularly when CMD is present.

recs.title: Implementation and outcomes of a regional cardiogenic shock network in the UK.
Palmitic acid promotes hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes via KDM5A/H3K4me3.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Palmitic acid (PA), the most abundant saturated fatty acid (SFA), is positively associated with heart failure (HF) risk. However, its role and mechanism underlying HF remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of a PA-enriched diet and potential therapeutic targets in HF. METHODS: The association between plasma SFAs and HF was investigated in a cohort of 232 592 UK Biobank participants. Mice were randomly categorized into three groups, where they were fed a PA-enriched, olive oil-enriched, or control diet for 4 weeks, followed by a 4-week dietary adaptation period on the control diet. A pressure overload model was established by transverse aortic constriction in these mice and cardiac-specific lysine demethylase 5A (Kdm5A)-knockout mice. RESULTS: The UK Biobank database revealed an association between high plasma SFA levels and increased HF risk. Our in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that short-term PA treatment promoted cardiac hypertrophy and HF without further exposure to high levels of PA, indicating a pro-hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes. Mechanistically, PA promoted palmitoylation-driven KDM5A degradation via the ubiquitination pathway, thereby up-regulating histone 3 lysine 4 tri-methylation (H3K4me3). KDM5A/H3K4me3 promoted a pro-hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes, thus causing cardiac hypertrophy via a monocarboxylate transporter 4 (MCT4)-induced metabolic imbalance. Furthermore, KDM5A agonist D18 ameliorated this PA-mediated cardiac hypertrophy and HF. CONCLUSIONS: A PA-enriched diet promotes pro-hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes, cardiac hypertrophy, and HF via KDM5A/H3K4me3/MCT4. The application of D18 may represent a promising therapeutic approach for PA-mediated cardiac hypertrophy and HF.

recs.title: Four Distinct Morphologies of Bundle Branch Reentrant Ventricular Tachycardia Eliminated by Right Bundle Branch Ablation.
Durability and Safety of Superior Vena Cava Isolation With a Lattice-Tip Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter: Focal Versus Circumferential Lesion Sets.

Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study.
recs.abstract: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings.
