Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.

recs.title: Evolution of Tined Leadless Pacemaker Implantation: Patient Selection, Implant Volume, Center Characteristics, and Safety Trends.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: As leadless pacing approaches a decade in clinical practice, we sought to assess how device complications have changed over time, and how variations in patient, implanter volume, and facility characteristics are associated with these changes. OBJECTIVE: To examine rates of cardiac perforations after leadless pacemaker implantation over time, and the associations between patient, implanter volume, and facility characteristics with these outcomes, including the extent of variation attributable to implanters and facilities. METHODS: Medicare claims linked to a manufacturer's device registration data were used to identify patients implanted with a tined leadless pacemaker from 2017 to 2024. Patient selection across implanters and facilities was evaluated by examining differences in patient characteristics and their impact on patient-adjusted model estimates. Random-intercept models were fitted to estimate variation attributable to implanters and facilities. RESULTS: Among 46,698 implants, 19,446 (41.6%) were Micra AV; patients had a mean age of 80.4 years and a high Charlson Comorbidity Index (4.7±3.4). Cardiac perforation rates declined over time (adjusted Coefficient -0.13, 95% CI -0.19 - -0.06, p-value<0.01). Higher implanter volume was associated with fewer perforations (OR 0.93 per additional 10 implants, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p-value<0.01). Differences in patient characteristics across providers and facilities were observed; however, adjustment for these differences did not materially alter the associations between implanters and facility and perforation rates. CONCLUSION: In Medicare patients with tined leadless pacemakers, cardiac perforation rates declined over time and were lower in those implanted by more experienced implanters. Variation in outcomes was more closely associated with implanters than facilities.

recs.title: Quantitative Proteomics of Plasma-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Reveals a Plasminogen-Centered Protein Network in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognosis of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR) remains poor; this is primarily due to late diagnosis, when irreversible damage has already occurred. Circulating levels of transthyretin or other plasma markers have little value for diagnosis. Although extracellular vesicles (EVs) (key mediators of intercellular communication) may reflect disease-specific molecular changes, their protein cargo has not yet been explored in the context of ATTR cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether cardiac amyloidosis alters the proteome of circulating EVs and assessed whether these changes define signature of ATTR. METHODS: Plasma EVs were prospectively isolated by ultracentrifugation from 41 patients with confirmed ATTR-CM (ATTR+ group; wild-type ATTR and variant ATTR) and 24 frequency-matched patients with nonamyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR- group), all referred to the Referral Center for Cardiac Amyloidosis (Henri Mondor Hospital, Créteil, France). EVs were characterized by flow cytometry and analyzed by quantitative liquid chromatography mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry proteomics. RESULTS: ATTR+ patients had a distinct signature enriched in proteins associated with vascular homeostasis, coagulation, and inflammation. At least 18 of these proteins formed an interconnected network centered on plasmin/plasminogen. Notably, EV levels of transthyretin and plasminogen were elevated, whereas the level of alpha2-antiplasmin (plasmin's primary inhibitor) was low. This imbalance is particularly relevant because plasmin is known to promote amyloidogenesis via transthyretin cleavage. CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory findings highlight a plasmin/plasminogen-centered protein network linking fibrinolysis, complement activation, and vascular inflammation to ATTR pathophysiology, and suggest that plasma EV proteomics warrant further evaluation as a minimally invasive approach for disease monitoring and biomarker discovery in ATTR-CM.

recs.title: Statins and non-cardiac surgery: continuation, not initiation.
Physical activity, atrial fibrillation and the dose-response relationship: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Regular physical activity (PA) may reduce atrial fibrillation (AF) risk in the general population, however, contemporary data suggests individuals engaging in the highest levels of PA may exhibit a paradoxical rise in AF risk. The point at which the dose-response curve reverses remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the association between PA and AF across the full continuum of PA exposure. METHODS: Four databases were searched (from January 1990 to June 2025). Eligible studies included those that reported PA exposure compared against a sedentary control group and assessed AF incidence or prevalence. PA exposures were standardised to metabolic equivalent of task hours per week (MET-hr/wk). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using a weighted random-effects model. A weighted restricted cubic spline model of logarithmic odds was used to produce a dose-response curve. RESULTS: 37 studies were included (n = 1,298,291 individuals). In the general population, PA was associated with a reduction in odds of AF by 22% (22 studies; OR 0.78; 95% CI 0.68, 0.89). Athlete status was associated with an increase in the odds of AF (15 studies; OR 2.74; 95% CI 1.72, 4.39). Dose-response analysis (26 studies; n = 1,022,790 individuals) showed 26 MET-hr/wk of PA was associated with the greatest reduction in odds of AF, with doses beyond 78 MET-hr/wk associated with increased odds of AF; the equivalent of 6-7 hours per week of endurance training. CONCLUSION: PA and AF demonstrate a U-shaped relationship whereby beyond a quantitative dose threshold of 78 MET-hr/wk, the protective effect of exercise may reverse.

recs.title: Temporal trends of heart failure epidemic in the Rotterdam Study over three decades.
recs.abstract: AIM: There is limited information on the heart failure (HF) epidemic and its temporal changes. Current research aimed to report the HF epidemic over the past three decades in the Rotterdam Study, covering the prevalence and incidence of HF, comorbidities and risk determinants. METHODS: Using data from the population-based Rotterdam cohort, three Epoch groups [Epoch 1990s (1989-1993, N=7,983), Epoch 2000s (1997-2001, N=7,738), and Epoch 2010s (2009-2014, N=6,170)] were identified, with a mean age of nearly 70 years. For each Epoch group, point prevalence at baseline and 5-year HF incidence rate, comorbidities at baseline, and HF risk determinants (using Cox proportional hazards models) were calculated. RESULTS: Point prevalence of HF was 3.3% in Epoch 1990s, 6.0% in Epoch 2000s, and 4.8% in Epoch 2010s, with an increase from the 1990s to 2000s followed by a decline in the 2010s, yielding an overall statistically significant upward trend (p<0.001). 5-year incidence of HF per 1,000 person-years was 16.3 (95%CI: 15.0 to 17.8), 10.3 (95%CI: 9.2 to 11.4) and 7.9 (95%CI: 6.9 to 9.0) in respective epochs, with a downward trend. Hypertension was the most common comorbidity in HF patients, followed by dyslipidemia and kidney dysfunction. The association of hypertension and diabetes with risk of incident HF decreased over time. Coronary heart disease (CHD), atrial fibrillation (AF) and stroke all showed increasing hazard ratios across groups. CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of HF increased during the past decades in a population-based setting, while HF incidence declined. Hypertension and diabetes tended to become less critical risk factors for new-onset HF nowadays, while CHD, AF, and stroke showed trends toward stronger associations with HF risk over time.

recs.title: Pathway-Guided and Patient-Centered Therapeutic Strategies in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), encompassing coronary artery disease (CAD), cerebrovascular disease (ischemic stroke, IS; and transient ischemic attack, TIA), and peripheral artery disease (PAD) of atherosclerotic origin, remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite major advances in prevention and treatment. Although atherosclerosis arises from the convergence of endothelial injury, lipid accumulation, inflammation, and thrombosis, the relative contribution of these pathogenic processes varies markedly among individuals, due to the effects of genetics, demographic, and racial factors, lifestyle behaviors and comorbidities, several of which are modifiable. The variability in the atherosclerosis underlying mechanisms results in substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Recently, ASCVD management has expanded beyond single-pathway intensification toward pathway-guided, patient-centered, multi-targeted therapeutic strategies. Over the past decade, we have witnessed the development of highly specific therapeutics, including small-molecule inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, and RNA-based therapies, while genome-editing approaches remain at an investigational stage. Contemporary Phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have demonstrated that several novel agents reduce cardiovascular (CV) risk, whereas others produce biological effects without improving outcomes, underscoring the need for outcome-based validation. Despite improved safety profiles and enhanced treatment adherence, the optimal integration of these therapies into clinical practice continues to evolve. In this narrative review, we evaluate evidence from established, emerging, and investigational therapeutic strategies for ASCVD prevention and treatment. We also describe the impact of endothelial-protective, lipid-lowering, anti-inflammatory, and antithrombotic, strategies on CV outcomes, with particular emphasis on differential efficacy across patient subgroups, vascular territories, and clinical settings. In addition to synthesizing evidence from contemporary clinical trials, this review proposes a novel pathway- and phenotype-based conceptual framework for individualized ASCVD management and secondary prevention. The framework integrates residual-risk phenotypes with clinical characteristics, comorbidities, vascular territory, and treatment-related considerations to support residual-risk-guided selection of complementary evidence-based therapies while balancing anticipated benefit, safety, treatment burden, and adherence.

recs.title: Smoke, spirits, and opioids-the cardiovascular toll of substance use.
Making Sarcopenic Obesity Actionable for Heart Failure Prevention.
Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

recs.title: Survivors of Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease.
Intravenous Vitamin C and Mortality and Organ Dysfunction in Severe Burn Injury-Reply.
A Proactive Digital Valve Care Pathway for Management of Severe Aortic Stenosis: The DETECT AS II Study.
Prevalence, Predictors, and Clinical Implications of Residual Shunt After Patent Foramen Ovale Percutaneous Closure.
Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and a COG5 Variant in Aortic Dissection.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. RESULTS: Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 near HLA-A and rs9276409 within HLA-DQA2) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in the COG5 gene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted TPM4, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. CONCLUSIONS: This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidate COG5 variant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

recs.title: Echocardiographic Assessment and Clinical Applications of the Left Atrial Stiffness Index in Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: The left atrial stiffness index is an emerging echocardiographic marker that integrates pressure-related burden and atrial reservoir deformation to provide a composite measure of left atrial pressure-deformation coupling. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis of left atrial stiffness, the methodological principles underlying echocardiographic left atrial stiffness index assessment, and the current evidence supporting its clinical applications across cardiovascular diseases. The strongest evidence is available in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, in which increased left atrial stiffness index has been associated with adverse hemodynamics, exercise intolerance, rhythm recurrence, and adverse clinical outcomes. In hypertension, cardiomyopathies, valvular heart disease, and congenital or aortic disorders, available data suggest potential clinical relevance, although the evidence remains more heterogeneous and less mature; by contrast, evidence in ischemic, inflammatory, and stroke-related settings is still preliminary. Despite its physiological appeal, broader clinical adoption remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, variable thresholds, limited invasive validation, and uncertain incremental value beyond its component measures. At present, left atrial stiffness index is best positioned as an adjunctive marker for phenotyping, hemodynamic assessment, and risk stratification, particularly in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, pending further methodological harmonization and prospective disease-specific validation.

recs.title: Allometric Scaling of Left Heart Structure and Function in Elite Cyclists: Development of Sport-Specific Prediction Equations.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Elite athletes frequently exceed conventional left ventricular (LV) and left atrial thresholds when guideline-recommended linear scaling for body size is applied, prompting unnecessary investigation. Few athlete-specific allometric equations yield percentage predicted values or Z scores. We aimed to develop allometric equations for LV and left atrial structure and function in elite cyclists, accounting for body size, sex, discipline, and heart rate, and to compare these with body surface area (BSA) indexing. METHODS: We evaluated 181 elite cyclists (105 male, 76 female; age 22.7±5.5 years; 128 endurance, 53 sprint) with normal preparticipation cardiac screening. Weighted least squares allometric regression determined optimal scaling exponents for height, weight, and BSA, with models advancing in complexity only when prediction accuracy significantly improved. Equations were externally validated in 62 independent elite male endurance cyclists. RESULTS: Men had larger BSA-scaled LV and left atrial size than women (both P<0.001). Many cyclists exceeded conventional thresholds (American Society of Echocardiography 2015: LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA 69.6%, LV end-systolic volume indexed to BSA 62.9%; British Society of Echocardiography 2020: LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA 50.8%, left atrial volume indexed to BSA 28.7%). Height provided superior allometric fit versus weight or BSA. Height, sex, discipline, and RR interval were key determinants. On external validation, only 6.5% exceeded the Z score threshold for LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA, compared with 90.3% classified abnormal by ASE guidelines. CONCLUSIONS: Height-based allometric scaling outperformed weight or BSA for cardiac dimensions and function in elite cyclists. These sport-specific equations, validated in an independent cohort, provide clinically usable percentage predicted values and Z scores that permit quantitative assessment rather than binary thresholds and may reduce misclassification of physiological adaptation as disease in preparticipation cardiac screening programs.

recs.title: Enhanced Early Risk Stratification in Cardiogenic Shock Using Machine Learning: A Hierarchical Clustering Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity, limiting the performance of conventional risk stratification tools like the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system. Machine learning (ML) has identified reproducible CS phenotypes that improve risk prediction, but their temporal consistency across the progression of shock remains incompletely described. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the temporal evolution of ML-derived CS phenotypes across the first 3 intensive care unit (ICU) days and determine whether phenotype trajectories enhance mortality stratification beyond SCAI staging. METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective registry of 2,906 adults with CS admitted to ICUs between 2016 and 2022, hierarchical agglomerative clustering was applied independently to clinical variables on ICU days 1, 2, and 3. RESULTS: On day 1, 3 phenotypes emerged: Cardiac (younger, acute myocardial infarction-predominant, preserved renal function; 15% mortality), Cardio-Renal (older, non-acute myocardial infarction-predominant, isolated renal extracardiac impairment, predominantly SCAI A and B on admission; 27% mortality), and Cardio-Metabolic (severe renal and tissue malperfusion, predominantly SCAI D and E on admission; 55% mortality). Similar phenotypes persisted on day 2 and day 3. These ML-derived phenotypes enhanced mortality stratification within each SCAI stage across days 1 to 3. CONCLUSIONS: Hierarchical clustering reproduced previously identified CS phenotypes that were consistent across the first 3 days of ICU stay, providing an enhanced framework for early risk stratification. Prospective validation is required for clinical implementation.

recs.title: Association of Lipoprotein(a) and Low-Attenuation Plaque Burden With Future Myocardial Infarction.
Treatment Discontinuation of Blood Pressure-Lowering Drugs-Reply.

Ethnicity does not equal region and patient-level evidence should always prevail over aggregate-data inference: the treatment effects of clopidogrel are consistent across Asian and non-Asian regions of enrolment.
Clinical trajectory and disease progression in patients with cardio-renal-metabolic syndrome: the CaReMap observational study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardio-renal-metabolic (CRM) syndrome describes the pathophysiological interconnection among diabetes mellitus (DM), atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and heart failure (HF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Limited studies simultaneously examine progression trajectories across all three conditions at the population level. We aimed to quantify the coexistence of CRM components, with a specific focus on patients with HF, and analyse survival and disease progression in a real-world setting. METHODS: CaReMap, an observational cohort study, analysed data from an Italian Regional Epidemiological Repository. The selection period spanned from 2017 to 2022. Incident patients had a first diagnosis of DM, HF, or CKD after January 1, 2017. Prevalent patients were classified based on their baseline morbidity status on January 1, 2017. Descriptive statistics, Kaplan-Meier survival estimates, and cumulative incidence curves for cause-specific events were reported. The CRM stage was further defined according to disease coexistence and severity. RESULTS: CaReMap included 71,694 adults with established CRM-related conditions (31.8% incident; 68.2% prevalent). Among incident patients, HF was associated with the highest probability of developing an additional diagnosis (60.4% at 6 years), while CKD showed the highest probability of death before a new diagnosis (43.3% at 6 years). In prevalent patients, the DM&HF group showed the highest cumulative incidence of further diagnoses (47.1% at 6 years). Across both incident and prevalent cohorts, HF and CKD patients experienced the steepest decline in overall survival. CONCLUSION: In this population-based Italian cohort, DM, HF, and CKD define distinct diagnostic trajectories with substantial competing risk of death. These findings provide real-world estimates of transition patterns and absolute risks that may inform risk stratification and integrated care pathways.

recs.title: Non-aneurysmal Left Sinus of Valsalva Thrombus with Myocardial Infarction and Scar: A Multimodal Imaging Diagnosis.
Photon-counting computed tomography depicts seven multifocal ulcer-like projections with jet-like blood flow in aortic dissection.
Atrial Septostomy and Left Ventricular Venting During Peripheral VA-ECMO.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral venoarterial (VA)-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, and therefore the risk of LV distension, pulmonary edema, and cardiac stasis. Balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) provides atrial-level unloading, but the durability of LV venting remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of BAS for LV venting in patients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock (CS). METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective study of consecutive adults with CS supported with peripheral VA-ECMO who underwent BAS for LV unloading at an academic center (2019-2024). The primary endpoint was LV venting failure, a composite of pulmonary edema, LV distension, spontaneous echocardiographic contrast, LV or aortic root thrombus, stroke due to ECMO, or escalation to additional mechanical support. RESULTS: A total of 28 patients were included in the study. BAS resulted in a significant reduction in mean left atrial pressure (20.5-13.5 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Durable LV venting was achieved in a subset of patients; however, LV venting failure occurred in 53.6%, driven primarily by pulmonary edema. Pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting-failure status (interaction P = 0.018). Model-estimated pulse pressure was higher at 48 hours (P = 0.010) and 72 hours (P = 0.031) among patients who ultimately did not experience venting failure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for CS, BAS achieves atrial-level decompression and may provide durable LV venting in select patients, although venting failure remains common. Observed arterial pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting failure status.

recs.title: Who We Recruit, Who We Miss: EARLY-HF and the Equity Gap in Heart Failure Research.
Extended DAPT for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease. Reply.
Clinical Characteristics and Transplacental Treatment of Fetal Ventricular Tachycardia: A Nationwide Survey in Japan.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fetal ventricular tachycardia (VT) is an ultra-rare form of tachyarrhythmia, and no established management strategy currently exists. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the current diagnostic and management approaches for fetal VT. METHODS: A nationwide survey of suspected fetal VT was conducted across 77 tertiary referral facilities in Japan between 2014 and 2023. RESULTS: In total, 24 fetal VT cases from 18 facilities were analyzed. Twenty cases were diagnosed based on atrioventricular dissociation. Four were initially diagnosed as supraventricular tachycardia. VT occurred by 32 6/7 weeks of gestation in all nine long QT syndrome (LQTS) cases (LQT 2 in six, LQT 3 in two, and other in one), whereas 8/15 non-LQTS cases occurred at term. Eight of 20 cases managed as fetal VT, and three of four cases managed as fetal supraventricular tachycardia received fetal treatment. Fetal treatments were effective in 9/11 cases overall and in 8/9 LQTS cases. Side effects were observed in 6/11 cases; however, no serious adverse events occurred, except one case of lidocaine toxicity. After birth, LQTS cases were more likely to be refractory to treatment than non-LQT cases (8/9 vs. 6/14), requiring multidisciplinary management. Neurodevelopmental delay was more frequent in LQTS cases than in non-LQTS cases (6/9 vs. 2/14). CONCLUSIONS: Transplacental treatment is highly recommended for preterm fetal VT. In particular, in cases of fetal VT diagnosed before 33 weeks of gestation, aggressive fetal treatment including magnesium sulfate and β-blockers should be considered with the possibility of LQT 2 or 3.

recs.title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

recs.title: Assessment of Severity of Chronic Aortic Regurgitation: Importance of a Hierarchical Approach to Echocardiogram Doppler Parameters.
Systemic Venous Excess in Acute Heart Failure: A Retrograde Signal of Right Ventricular Uncoupling.
Population-scale reconstruction of menopause dynamics reveals a physiological cliff at the final menstrual period.
recs.abstract: Menopause reshapes female physiology, yet current understanding is limited by small longitudinal cohorts that characterize it as a gradual transition. Large-scale biomedical datasets remain underutilized because the final menstrual period (FMP) age is rarely recorded. Here we present a computational framework, inspired by astronomy, that reconstructs FMP-anchored trajectories from cross-sectional data by removing the blurring caused by variation in FMP age across individuals. Applying this to two independent cohorts totaling 300 million laboratory tests revealed a step-like physiological cliff at the FMP including endocrine, skeletal, hepatic, renal and lipid systems. These discontinuities are absent in male individuals, are concordant across populations and appear markedly attenuated by menopausal hormone therapy. Dysregulation began more than a decade before FMP. These findings support a systemic, quantifiable view of menopause and provide a generalizable strategy for recovering hidden biological trajectories applicable to other transitions such as puberty or disease progression.

recs.title: Heart-specific T cell responses: from antigens to disease mechanisms.
recs.abstract: The field of immunology has transformed our understanding of myocardial cell biology and paved the way for new pathophysiological concepts in cardiology. Researchers have sought to elucidate the contributions of nonspecific inflammatory mechanisms to cardiac diseases, and an increasing number of clinical trials have explored anti-inflammatory approaches in cardiovascular disease. Moreover, adaptive immune mechanisms directed to cardiac proteins released by dying cardiomyocytes have been reported across a broad spectrum of conditions, including acute myocarditis, myocardial infarction and heart failure, and have gained increasing attention. This concept of antigen-specific cardio-immune crosstalk could pave the way for a deeper understanding of tissue-specific disease mechanisms and facilitate the development of targeted interventions. However, only a small number of cardiac antigens have been identified so far, and an immunological definition of heart specificity remains elusive. This Review revisits the molecular composition of the heart from the perspective of T cells to describe the most relevant cardiac antigens identified to date, thus defining a framework for identifying novel T cell reactivities in the injured heart. Going forward, these insights might pave the way for the development of new tools to track specific T cells across various cardiac diseases, in contexts ranging from model organisms to patients.

recs.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance derived myocardial strain: applications, acquisition techniques, analysis, and reporting.
recs.abstract: Myocardial strain imaging enables quantification of cardiac deformation. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) is well suited for strain assessment due to the ability to image in any given plane with high spatial and contrast resolution. CMR strain measures have incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility over conventional clinical imaging parameters across disease states. Routine integration of CMR strain assessment in clinical practice has been hindered by the lack of agreement on imaging protocols and analysis methods, variability due to noise sensitivity, and a paucity of robust normative age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges. In recognition of the expanding applications of strain techniques in clinical and research CMR, this joint SCMR/RSNA/EACVI scientific statement integrates data from original research studies, guidelines, and opinions from experts across the field to guide responsible and evidence-based utilization of CMR strain.

recs.title: Deus Ex Mechano: Hydrostatic Pressure in Pulmonary Hypertension.
Heart Transplant for Advanced Heart Failure: A Review.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Heart failure affects more than 6 million US adults; approximately 4% to 5% progress to advanced disease despite optimal therapy. Heart transplant is a class I guideline-recommended therapy for select individuals with advanced heart failure. OBSERVATIONS: Early referral for heart transplant is guided by the "I NEED HELP" mnemonic, a tool that identifies patients with advanced heart failure based on criteria such as use of inotropes, persistent symptoms (New York Heart Association class III or IV), end-organ dysfunction, left ventricular ejection fraction, defibrillator shocks, hospitalizations for heart failure, persistent edema or escalating use of diuretics, and low blood pressure. Each criterion is associated with higher risk of death or first heart failure hospitalization over a median follow-up of 260 days (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.19 [95% CI, 1.11-1.27] for each additional criterion). Typical absolute contraindications to heart transplant include active systemic infection, malignancy with limited life expectancy, severe and irreversible end-organ dysfunction (eg, cirrhosis, severe pulmonary hypertension), active substance use, major untreated psychiatric illness, inadequate social support, and severe frailty. Approximately 4600 heart transplants are performed annually in the US. The mortality rate was 8.5 deaths/100 patient-years for adults on the transplant waiting list in 2023. Leading causes of early death after transplant include primary graft dysfunction (39.5%), multiorgan failure (18.5%), and infection (13.9%). Among adults, contemporary survival rates after heart transplant are 91.5% at 1 year and 80.3% at 5 years. Lifelong maintenance immunosuppression typically combines a calcineurin inhibitor, antiproliferative agents (typically mycophenolate mofetil or azathioprine) and corticosteroids, with selective use of induction therapy (intensive immunosuppression immediately after transplant). Acute rejection requiring treatment occurs in 20% to 25% of recipients within a year, and may be treated with high-dose corticosteroids, antithymocyte globulin, and B-cell-targeted therapies (such as rituximab or bortezomib). Rejection surveillance with endomyocardial biopsies of the right ventricular septum is performed 5 to 10 times within the first year after transplant. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (chronic rejection that causes diffuse coronary narrowing) affects 29% of heart transplant recipients within 5 years and 46.8% by 10 years and is the leading cause of late mortality. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy is treated with statins, mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitors (such as sirolimus or everolimus), and retransplant for severe cases. Infections (62.5% are bacterial, 30.0% are viral, 6.7% are fungal, and 0.8% are parasitic) and malignancy (10.7% within 5 years after heart transplant) are other leading causes of late mortality. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Heart transplant is the definitive therapy for carefully selected patients with advanced heart failure despite receiving optimal, guideline-directed therapy. After heart transplant, lifelong multidisciplinary care is necessary to manage immunosuppression, prevent and treat rejection and cardiac allograft vasculopathy, and monitor for infection and malignancy.

recs.title: Thirty years of percutaneous epicardial access: reflections on the evolution of ventricular tachycardia substrate mapping and ablation.
Is the Sarcopenic Obesity Index a Pathophysiological Phenotype or Merely a Ratio?
Transcatheter mitral valve replacement using transcatheter aortic valve implants in the mitral position: a UK multicentre experience.
From the Paced QRS to Assessing the Mechanical Substrate for Achieving Cardiac Resynchronization: A Leap of Faith or the Ground Truth?
Polygenic Determinants of Arterial Stiffness: Implications for Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Components of arterial stiffness (structural stiffness from aging and load-dependent stiffness from high blood pressure [BP]) are markers for cardiovascular disease risk. We evaluated relationships between polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for BP and arterial stiffness. METHODS: Participants (n=5804) are from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) with measures of carotid ultrasound and genomic DNA. Carotid pulse wave velocity (PWV) was calculated from carotid ultrasound. Structural stiffness was calculated by adjusting carotid PWV to a 120/80 mm Hg BP with participant-specific models. Load-dependent stiffness was the difference of total and structural stiffness. BP PRSs were derived from genome-wide associations. Associations were assessed with multivariable-adjusted regression models. Mendelian randomization was performed with 2-stage least squares. RESULTS: Participants were aged 62.8±10.3 years. Systolic BP (SBP) was 133.5±20.5 mm Hg, diastolic BP (DBP) was 74.27±10.28 mm Hg, and pulse pressure was 59.22±16.17 mm Hg. Total carotid PWV was associated with the SBP PRS (β=0.10±0.02, P=5.25E-08) and the DBP PRS (β: 0.08±0.02, P=7.26E-07) but not pulse pressure PRS (P=0.05). Load-dependent carotid PWV was associated with the SBP PRS (β=0.09±0.01, P=7.93×10-30), the DBP PRS (β=0.09±0.01, P=4.92×10-34) and the pulse pressure PRS (β=0.03±0.01, P=8.18×10-5). Structural carotid PWV was not associated with any BP PRSs. With Mendelian randomization, SBP and DBP showed significant independent positive effects on load-dependent stiffness (P<0.001); only SBP was significant for total carotid PWV after accounting for DBP. CONCLUSIONS: There are key differences in the genetic underpinnings of the mechanistic components of arterial stiffness.

Connecting the dots in cardiovascular medicine: endometriosis, chronic inflammation, and venous thromboembolism.
Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.
recs.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

recs.title: Letter by Koliastasis and Kim Regarding Article, "Impact of Coronary Diameter Stenosis and Proximal Lesion Location on Outcomes Following PCI in Patients Undergoing TAVI: Prespecified NOTION-3 Substudy".
Genetics of poor medication adherence: revealing risks and novel therapeutic targets.
Left Ventricular Unloading and Procedural Intensification in CHIP-BCIS3.
USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown. METHODS: USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI. RESULTS: The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis. CONCLUSIONS: Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

recs.title: Adjunctive Low-Voltage Area Ablation Reduces Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Trial Sequential Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adjunctive low-voltage area ablation (LVAA) has been proposed as a substrate modification strategy to improve outcomes of catheter ablation in persistent atrial fibrillation (AF); however, randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating LVAA have yielded inconsistent findings. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analysis sought to evaluate the efficacy of LVAA in addition to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) compared with PVI alone in patients with persistent AF. METHODS: Electronic databases were searched from inception to September 2026 for eligible RCTs. The primary endpoint was recurrent AF/atrial tachyarrhythmia ≥12 months after index ablation. Secondary endpoints included major periprocedural complications and procedural durations. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models. Trial sequential analysis was performed to assess the robustness of cumulative evidence. RESULTS: Seven RCTs comprising 1,487 participants (weighted mean age 68 years, 60% male) were included. Compared with PVI alone, PVI + LVAA was associated with significantly lower recurrence of AF/atrial tachyarrhythmia (HR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.50-0.88; I2 = 55%; P = 0.004). Trial sequential analysis demonstrated that the cumulative Z-curve crossed the monitoring boundary for benefit, supporting the robustness of the observed treatment effect. Adjunctive LVAA increased total procedure duration (mean difference: 30.5 minutes; 95% CI: 5.8-55.2; P = 0.02) and radiofrequency ablation duration (mean difference: 12.3 minutes; 95% CI: 5.4-19.1; P < 0.001) without increasing fluoroscopy time or major periprocedural complications (relative risk: 1.12; 95% CI: 0.60-2.10; P = 0.7). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with persistent AF, adjunctive LVAA in addition to PVI significantly reduces recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmia compared with PVI alone. These findings support electroanatomically guided substrate modification as a promising individualized ablation strategy in persistent AF.

recs.title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH). METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization. RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious. CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

recs.title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

recs.title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

recs.title: Machine Learning of Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Myocardial Radiomics for Identification of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an important cause of heart failure (HF) with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness that can be challenging to distinguish from other LV hypertrophic processes. Echocardiographic myocardial radiomic texture analysis may identify imperceptible amyloid-induced structural changes. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to develop and validate an echocardiography-based machine learning model using myocardial radiomics to identify ATTR-CM. METHODS: In this retrospective and prospective multicenter study, 854 echocardiographic scans were analyzed. Conventional and novel radiomic features were extracted from parasternal short-axis views at basal, mid, and apical LV levels, with incorporated age and sex from echocardiogram metadata. A machine learning pipeline was developed using a balanced training set (150 ATTR-CM, 150 nonamyloid HF). Performance was evaluated on an independent internal validation set (50 ATTR-CM, 399 nonamyloid HF) and an external validation set (10 ATTR-CM, 10 immunoglobulin light-chain-amyloid, 10 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, 75 nonamyloid HF). RESULTS: In internal validation, the model achieved 86% sensitivity (95% CI: 73.8%-93%), 92% specificity (95% CI: 88.9%-94.3%), 57.3% positive predictive value (95% CI: 46.1%-67.9%), 98.1% negative predictive value (NPV) (95% CI: 96.2%-99.1%), and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve 0.938 (95% CI: 0.891-0.985). Performance was consistent in the external validation (100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity, 33.3% positive predictive value, 100% NPV, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve of 0.917). The model correctly classified 77.3% of nonamyloid HF, 70% of AL-amyloid cases, and 100% of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cases as non-ATTR in subgroup analysis. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an echocardiographic radiomics-based tool to identify ATTR-CM with excellent discrimination and very high NPV in a cohort that approximates clinical experience. These preliminary findings require validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

recs.title: Immune-inflammatory profiles, coronary artery disease, and peripheral artery disease in people with HIV.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: People with HIV (PWH) have high risk of coronary (CAD) and peripheral (PAD) artery disease independent of traditional risk factors. Single immune-inflammatory biomarkers provide limited insight into disease risk and phenotypes, whereas integrative profiling may reveal novel mechanisms. Here we investigated associations between immune-inflammatory profiles, CAD, and PAD in PWH. METHODS: We included PWH from the Copenhagen Comorbidity in HIV Infection (COCOMO) Study with undetectable HIV RNA and measurements of 25 immune-inflammatory biomarkers. Participants underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements to assess for CAD and PAD. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering on principal components grouped participants by immune-inflammatory clusters, and we assessed their associations with CAD and PAD. RESULTS: Among 651 PWH, we identified three immune-inflammatory clusters: one with low senescent T cell proportions; one with low concentrations of inflammation, innate activation, and endothelial dysfunction markers (reference cluster); and one with high senescent T cell proportions and concentrations of inflammation, innate activation, and endothelial dysfunction markers (high inflammation cluster). The high inflammation cluster was associated with obstructive CAD (adjusted OR 2.42 [95% CI: 1.06; 5.33]), higher lipid-rich plaque volumes (adjusted β = 8.47 [95% 0.84; 16.1] μL), and lower ABI (adjusted β = -0.07 [95% CI: -0.13;-0.01]) among those with PAD compared to the reference cluster, after adjustment for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidaemia. CONCLUSIONS: An immune-inflammatory profile characterised by T cell senescence, inflammation, innate activation, and endothelial dysfunction was associated with high-risk CAD severity, highlighting immunopathogenic pathways associated with atherosclerosis in PWH.

recs.title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

recs.title: Prevalence of Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Established Cardiovascular Disease Among All of Us Participants: Benchmarking Against National Estimates.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The AoU (All of Us) Research Program aims to accelerate precision-medicine research. To provide context for the generalizability of findings we benchmarked cardiovascular risk factors and established cardiovascular disease prevalence in AoU against nationally representative estimates. METHODS: We included AoU participants enrolled between May 2017 and June 2022 and the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) 2017 to March 2020 cycle. The AoU Survey cohort included participants who completed the Personal and Family Health History survey (N=185 232). AoU EHR included participants with linked electronic health record (EHR) (N=287 012). We identified cardiovascular risk factors and cardiovascular disease through survey questions in AoU Survey and NHANES, and Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine codes for AoU EHR. RESULTS: AoU Survey and AoU EHR were older than NHANES (56.1±17 years and 57.6±17 years versus 47.5±18 years) with more female participants (64% and 60% versus 51.8%). Black participants were underrepresented in AoU Survey (9.1%) and overrepresented in AoU EHR (19.9%); 11.5% in NHANES. Prevalence of cardiovascular comorbidities in AoU Survey and NHANES were similar but lower in AoU Survey when age adjusted (eg, hypertension 31.7% in NHANES versus 19.7% in AoU Survey, diabetes 11.3% versus 8%). Black participants had higher unadjusted rates of hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease and congestive heart failure than NHANES. AoU EHR with its code-based identification had higher unadjusted prevalence of most cardiovascular comorbidities; differences attenuated with age-adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: AoU includes more historically underrepresented groups, but representation varies by whether cohorts are defined by survey versus EHR availability. Further, disease prevalence can change based on how conditions are ascertained.

recs.title: Duration of antibiotic treatment for infective endocarditis: should we move towards tailored therapy?
Combined ischaemia and vulnerable plaque percutaneous coronary intervention to reduce cardiovascular events: design and rationale of the COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial.
recs.abstract: Fractional flow reserve (FFR) assessment represents the most widely used revascularisation strategy of the last two decades. However, many FFR (+) lesions, particularly those in the grey zone, can be safely treated medically, while other lesions carrying vulnerable plaque (VP) features can cause future events despite the absence of ischaemia. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) can identify lesions with VP morphology. The objective of this study is to determine whether a combined revascularisation strategy - targeting only severely ischaemic lesions (FFR ≤0.75) and extending treatment to OCT-assessed VP, even in the absence of ischaemia (FFR>0.80) - could reduce future adverse events compared with the current revascularisation practice based exclusively on the presence of ischaemia (FFR ≤0.80). The COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial is a global, prospective, randomised, single-blinded, sham-controlled, superiority trial. A total of 1,223 all-comer patients with multivessel disease (≥2 lesions with a diameter of stenosis ≥50%) will be randomised 1:1 to revascularisation if the FFR is ≤0.75 or a VP is present (experimental arm) versus FFR ≤0.80 in the comparative arm. The primary endpoint is a composite of cardiac death, any myocardial infarction, or any clinically driven revascularisation within 24 months. The trial has already completed enrolment in 50 centres worldwide. COMBINE-INTERVENE is the first trial evaluating the impact of a revascularisation strategy that targets lesions that are either severely ischaemic or carry an OCT-assessed VP versus revascularisation based on ischaemia alone. The trial is powered for superiority. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05333068).

recs.title: The Vanishing Occluder.
Genetic Variants in Cardiomyopathy Genes Are Associated With Right Ventricular Dysfunction in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
Electrophysiologic Phenotype Outperforms Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction for Mortality Prediction in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis carries mortality rates approaching 50%. Risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), yet many fatal cases occur despite preserved systolic function. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to compare the prognostic value of electrophysiologic involvement vs LVEF in ICI-associated myocarditis. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed for ICI-associated myocarditis cases with extractable patient-level data. Electrophysiologic phenotype (EP) was defined by clinically significant conduction disease or ventricular arrhythmia, including high-grade atrioventricular block, ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, or cardiac arrest. LVEF was dichotomized at ≤35%. Cluster-robust logistic regression was used to assess associations with mortality. RESULTS: From 242 publications, 319 cases were extracted; 180 with complete data comprised the analytical cohort (77 deaths; 42.8% mortality). EP involvement (66.7% of cases) was associated with significantly higher mortality vs EP-negative cases (55.0% vs 18.3%; risk ratio: 3.00; 95% CI: 1.72-5.24; P < 0.001). LVEF ≤35% was not significantly associated with mortality (50.7% vs 38.1%; P = 0.125). Among patients with an LVEF >35%, EP involvement was associated with markedly higher mortality (55.1% vs 11.4%; P < 0.001). In adjusted models, EP remained associated with mortality on both the odds-ratio scale (OR: 5.27; 95% CI: 2.29-12.13; P < 0.001) and risk-ratio scale (RR: 2.94; 95% CI: 1.54-5.59; P < 0.001), whereas LVEF ≤35% was not independently associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Electrophysiologic involvement is a dominant prognostic marker in ICI-associated myocarditis, particularly for risk stratification among patients with an LVEF >35%. Risk stratification should prioritize cardiac rhythm monitoring and identification of conduction abnormalities over reliance on LVEF alone.

recs.title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort. METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes. RESULTS: Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures, P<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (P=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.

recs.title: Outcomes of leadless pacing with the Micra VR beyond 10 years.
Machine Learning Integration of Ablation Quality Metrics for Predicting Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence: A Multicenter Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current prediction models for atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after ablation rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical characteristics, demonstrating limited predictive accuracy and offering little guidance for intraprocedural decision-making and outcome optimization. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a machine learning model that integrated clinical characteristics with ablation quality metrics to individually predict AF recurrence. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing their first AF ablation in 14 hospitals from mainland China. Patients aged 18 to 80 years were enrolled, and data on clinical characteristics and quality metrics were collected. An XGBoost model was developed using 7 selected features to predict 1-year AF recurrence. The model was developed using 5-fold cross-validation for internal validation and was further externally validated on data from 2 independent hospitals. RESULTS: Among 1,782 patients enrolled between December 2021 and December 2023, 294 (16.5%) experienced AF recurrence within 1 year. The final XGBoost model achieved strong discrimination in internal validation (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.918, 95% CI: 0.874-0.962). In feature-combination analyses, model performance improved from an AUC of 0.588 using clinical features alone to 0.918 after incorporating ablation quality metrics. In 2 independent external validation centers (n = 239), the model showed good discrimination, with AUCs of 0.992 and 0.951 and precision-recall AUCs of 0.960 and 0.815, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ablation quality metrics yielded an validated model that showed strong discrimination for 1-year AF recurrence, outperforming clinical features alone. This approach highlights the prognostic value of intraprocedural quality assessment and may support personalized patient management.

recs.title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR. METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed. RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

recs.title: Partitioning ApoB in the context of Lipoprotein(a) concentrations: A Necessary but Incomplete Step Toward Defining Plaque Phenotype.
Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted P<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn/. Unique identifier: ChiCTR2300074640.

recs.title: Association of epicardial adipose tissue with myocardial stiffness and postoperative outcomes in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergoing transapical beating-heart septal myectomy.
Cell Village Captures Populational Heterogeneity of Sunitinib Cardiotoxicity.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: TKIs (tyrosine kinase inhibitors) have transformed cancer therapy; however, cardiotoxicity remains a frequent adverse effect with variable susceptibility among patients. For sunitinib, a commonly prescribed TKI, the molecular programs and functional features underlying this variability are not well defined, and clinically actionable predictors of cardiotoxicity risk remain lacking. METHODS: To investigate interindividual variability in sunitinib-induced cardiotoxic responses, we implemented the Cell Village platform consisting of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes from 20 healthy donors. Pooled iPSCs were differentiated into cardiomyocytes, treated with sunitinib for 72 hours, followed by harvesting for single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Donor identity was determined using single nucleotide polymorphism-based demultiplexing. Additionally, individual line-specific transcriptomic responses to sunitinib were integrated with quantitative functional phenotyping (including contractility, electrophysiology, and recovery efficacy following tocotrienol treatment) in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes differentiated from a subset of 10 lines. RESULTS: Sunitinib induced a robust global transcriptional response characterized by dysregulation of tyrosine kinase signaling, cytoskeletal organization, ion channels, and calcium-handling pathways. Although the pathway-level changes were shared, individual donor lines displayed heterogeneity in both gene expression patterns and functional impairment. Across functional parameters, relaxation velocity was the most consistently correlated with toxicity severity. Integration of each iPSC line's functional data with the corresponding transcriptomic signatures identified gene modules related to calcium handling and structural organization strongly correlated with donor-specific toxicity and recovery indices. Pharmacological validation using tocotrienol demonstrated partial, donor-dependent improvement of sunitinib-related iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte impairments. CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study establishes a scalable, donor-resolved platform that links pooled transcriptomic profiling with functional toxicity and recovery phenotypes in human cardiomyocytes. By linking molecular perturbations to functional outcomes across genetically diverse backgrounds, this approach provides a framework for dissecting interindividual variability in TKI-associated cardiotoxicity. More broadly, it provides a foundation for extending population-scale cardiotoxicity assessment to additional drugs and protective interventions.

recs.title: Body Mass Index, Valsartan, and Myocardial Remodeling in Early-Stage Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Secondary Analysis of the Randomized VANISH Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with adverse outcomes in overt hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the prevalence and impact of elevated body mass index (BMI) in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the randomized VANISH (Valsartan for Attenuating Disease Evolution in Early Sarcomeric Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy) trial, participants were categorized according to baseline BMI (nonelevated or elevated [≥85th percentile if age <18 years; ≥25 kg/m2 if age ≥18 years]). Exercise capacity (peak oxygen uptake [milliliters per kilogram per minute]) and cardiac imaging parameters were evaluated by baseline BMI and 2-year change in BMI. RESULTS: Among 171 (96%) participants (mean age, 23±10 years; 39% female sex; 97% White), 82 (48%) had nonelevated BMI and 89 (52%) had an elevated BMI. After covariate adjustment, higher baseline BMI was associated with lower peak oxygen uptake; lower left ventricular systolic and diastolic function; higher left ventricular mass; and higher atrial, ventricular, and extracellular volumes. Similarly, greater 2-year increases in BMI were associated with greater declines in peak oxygen uptake and greater increases in left ventricular mass. Participants with elevated BMI were more likely to develop late gadolinium enhancement over 2 years (adjusted odds ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-11.9]; P=0.033). Valsartan appeared to modestly attenuate 2-year increases in body weight versus placebo (adjusted mean difference, -3.1% [95% CI, -6.2 to -0.1%]; P=0.042). Baseline BMI did not appear to modify the effect of valsartan on cardiac remodeling (Pinteraction=0.96). CONCLUSIONS: Elevated BMI was common and associated with greater hypertrophic, eccentric, and fibrotic remodeling in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Two-year increases in BMI were associated with greater phenotypic progression. These findings suggest prevention and treatment of elevated BMI may attenuate hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01912534.

recs.title: Building Zanzibar's first cardiac catheterization lab: closing the chain of survival.
Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation.
