METHODS AND RESULTS: Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences. CONCLUSION: Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

recs.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037). CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

recs.title: Early Uptake of Oral Semaglutide for Obesity Treatment After Regulatory Approval.
Can a Wrist-Worn Stimulator Improve the Results of an AF Ablation?
Survivors of Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease-In Reply.
Use of the wearable cardioverter-defibrillator in Spain: the first 300 patients.
Real-Life Psychological Experiences and Cardiac Autonomic Physiology Among Survivors of a Myocardial Infarction in Midlife.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Young and middle-aged women with ischemic heart disease have a higher burden of psychosocial factors compared with male counterparts. They also have worse morbidity and mortality, despite less atherosclerotic burden. Data on daily life stress and autonomic physiology could help guide targeted interventions. METHODS: We studied 302 individuals ≤61 years of age recently hospitalized for a myocardial infarction. All underwent a 7-day home monitoring of mood and stress using ecological momentary assessments, with concomitant Holter monitoring for autonomic physiology. Deceleration capacity, a prognostic marker of parasympathetic activity, was the primary autonomic outcome; heart rate variability was also examined. RESULTS: The sample was 43% women with mean age of 51 years (SD, 7 years). Across the week of monitoring, women reported higher levels of negative mood and stress than men. Women also exhibited significantly lower parasympathetic activity (daily average of deceleration capacity) than men; heart rate variability was also lower. Among women, daily negative mood was inversely associated with lower deceleration capacity: for each 1-log unit higher daily negative mood score, deceleration capacity declined 4.5% in women, but among men, the difference was close to zero: 0.5% (P=0.02 for interaction). Adjustment for other risk factors did not materially affect the associations. A similar pattern of results was observed for heart rate variability metrics. CONCLUSIONS: Young and middle-aged women who recently survived a myocardial infarction have more parasympathetic withdrawal than men in daily life, especially during moments of negative mood. These results underscore the need for greater attention to psychosocial management in women after myocardial infarction.

recs.title: Cardiogenic shock networks: breaking the link between geography and survival?
ANOCA Patients With Prior Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease and PCI Have Higher Odds of Epicardial Spasm.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of patients undergoing coronary angiography have angina with no obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Among ANOCA patients, 2 distinct groups exist: patients with and without a history of prior obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate associations between history of prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI and coronary microvascular and vasomotor dysfunction endotypes in ANOCA patients. METHODS: A prospective Coronary Microvascular and Vasomotor Dysfunction Registry of consecutive ANOCA patients undergoing invasive coronary functional testing (ICFT). RESULTS: Among 624 ANOCA patients undergoing ICFT, 11% had prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI. ANOCA patients with prior obstructive CAD had a higher prevalence of males, were older, and had higher rates of cardiovascular risk factors. Prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI was associated with an 11-point lower Seattle Angina Questionnaire 7 summary score in unadjusted (β -11.0; 95% CI: -17.0 to -4.4; P = 0.001) and adjusted models. Patients with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had a higher prevalence of epicardial spasm by angiographic criteria (70% vs 34%; P < 0.001) and 4.55-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm in unadjusted (OR: 4.55; 95% CI: 2.65-8.07; P < 0.001) and adjusted models, with similar odds of coronary microvascular dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: Among ANOCA patients, those with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had over a 4-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive ICFT in ANOCA patients with prior PCI.

recs.title: Cellular consequences of non-ablative radiotherapy, a novel approach to ventricular tachycardias.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiotherapy (RT) with a single application of ionizing radiation (STAR) has been suggested as a non-invasive alternative to radiofrequency in ablating ventricular tachycardia (VT). Emerging data reveal that STAR may suppress VT without substrate destruction, by enhancing impulse conduction instead, through increased expression of NaV1.5 channels and connexin 43. The study aims to investigate electrophysiology and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics in cardiomyocytes (CMs) from mice subjected to in-vivo RT. The emerging data led us to evaluate biochemical changes potentially linking electrophysiological response to ionizing irradiation. METHODS: CMs isolated 2 weeks after RT with low-dose (15 Gy) or high-dose (25 Gy) were compared to those of sham-treated mice (CTRL). We evaluated: i) the properties of the transient (INaT) and sustained (INasus) components of INa; ii) AP parameters, including the prevalence of Early After-Depolarizations (EADs); iii) intracellular Ca2+ dynamics; iv) CaMKII phosphorylation and v) ROS content. RESULTS: 25 Gy RT i) increased INaT and, to a larger extent, INasus (increased INasus/INaT ratio); ii) increased AP amplitude, +dV/dtMAX and duration (APD) and facilitated EADs; iii) depressed intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. 15 Gy RT had similar but smaller effects (dose-dependency). 25 Gy RT reduced CaMKII phosphorylation but increased cell ROS content, thus providing a mechanism for the late component of INa (INaL) enhancement. CONCLUSIONS: The results support the view that STAR may supress VT by increasing conduction velocity, with APD prolongation providing an additional mechanism. On the other hand, INasus enhancement and Ca2+ handling depression may impair electrical stability and contractility in the irradiated region.

recs.title: Splicing the Hypertrophic Heart: MBNL2, Tropomyosin, and Mitochondrial Stress.
Associations of Mild or Trace Valvular Abnormalities With Cardiac Remodeling in Older Adults: The ARIC Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The impact of mild/trace valvular abnormalities on cardiac remodeling is not well understood, despite their association with poor cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: Using data from 4684 participants in the ARIC (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) Study (2011-2013), aged 66 to 90 years, we examined cross-sectional associations of mild/trace valvular abnormalities (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, and mitral regurgitation) with cardiac parameters using multivariable linear regression models. Cardiac parameters included cardiac structure (eg, left ventricular mass index), systolic function (eg, ejection fraction), diastolic function, and biomarkers (eg, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T). RESULTS: The prevalence was 4.3% for mild aortic stenosis, 10.9% for mild/trace aortic regurgitation, and 44.7% for mild/trace mitral regurgitation. Mitral regurgitation showed the most consistent associations with cardiac measures (left ventricular mass index 5.48 g/m2 [95% CI, 4.38-6.57 g/m2]; ejection fraction -1.92% [95% CI, -2.29% to -1.54%]; high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.08 log ng/L [95% CI, 0.05-0.12 log ng/L]). Aortic stenosis was associated with impaired ventricular filling (Ratio of early transmitral flow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e') lateral ratio 2.00 [95% CI, 1.48-2.53]) and elevated biomarkers (high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.17 ng/L [95% CI, 0.09-0.25 ng/L]), whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsened cardiac structure (left ventricular mass index 3.52 [95% CI, 1.76-5.28] g/m2) and systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction -1.54% [95% CI, -2.14% to -0.94%]). A dose-response relationship was also observed between the number of total abnormalities and all cardiac parameters examined. CONCLUSIONS: Mild/trace mitral regurgitation was most consistently associated with all cardiac parameters examined. Aortic stenosis was associated with elevated E/e' lateral ratio and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsening in cardiac structure and ejection fraction. Our study supports the possibility of pathophysiological contributions of these mild/trace valvular abnormalities.

recs.title: Correction to: Development and Validation of the American Heart Association's PREVENT Equations.
Pulsed Field Ablation as First-Line Therapy for the Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation: a FARADISE Sub-Analysis.
Effects of Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter Ablation of Ventricular Arrhythmias on Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Performance.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Sphere-9 lattice-tip catheter (Affera, Medtronic) enables delivery of both radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and pulsed field ablation (PFA) for ventricular arrhythmia (VA) ablation. Data on its impact on cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) are limited. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate changes in CIED function following VA ablation using the Sphere-9 catheter. METHODS: We reviewed 65 consecutive patients (median age 71 years, 94% male, 63% ischemic cardiomyopathy, median left ventricular ejection fraction 31%) with pre-existing CIEDs who underwent VA ablation (62 ventricular tachycardia [95%], 3 premature ventricular contraction [5%]) using the Sphere-9 catheter (combined RFA/PFA (53 [82%]), RFA alone (6 [9%]), PFA alone (6 [9%])). Device interrogation was performed within 30 days preprocedure, within 7 days postprocedure, and at 3-month (+/- 30 days) follow-up. RESULTS: At 3-months, right ventricular leads demonstrated reduced sensing amplitude (11.7-10.0 mV, P = 0.04), pacing impedance (441-422 Ω, P < 0.001), shock impedance (64-59 Ω, P = 0.01), and increased capture threshold (0.9-1.0 V at 0.4-0.5 milliseconds, P = 0.03). Left ventricular (LV) leads demonstrated reduced pacing impedance (544-475 Ω, P = 0.04), whereas LV capture threshold remained elevated (1.0-1.4 V, P = 0.08). Right atrial lead parameters remained stable. No patient required CIED revision. One patient experienced cardiac resynchronization therapy-D pulse generator failure during PFA delivery 7.5 mm from an LV lead tip electrode, requiring generator replacement. CONCLUSIONS: Ventricular arrhythmia ablation using the Sphere-9 dual-energy lattice-tip catheter was associated with small but persistent changes in right and left ventricular lead parameters. Serious CIED interactions were uncommon, and further studies are needed to better understand the underlying mechanisms.

recs.title: Association of beta-blocker therapy with outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction stratified by GRACE risk score: A nationwide registry analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Associations between beta-blocker use following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and clinical outcomes remain uncertain in the contemporary era of near-universal early revascularization and drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly for patients with preserved left ventricular function. We sought to determine whether associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied across Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) risk strata. METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of 11,866 STEMI survivors from two prospective nationwide Korean registries who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with second-generation DES. Patients were categorized by beta-blocker prescription at discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at one year; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability treatment weighting were employed to mitigate confounding. Variation in associations was examined across the continuous GRACE risk spectrum, categorized into low-risk (GRACE <85), intermediate-risk (GRACE 85-179), and high-risk (GRACE ≥180) strata. RESULTS: Beta-blockers were prescribed to 83.8% of the cohort. After propensity matching, beta-blocker use was associated with lower one-year all-cause mortality (2.7% vs. 4.2%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.91) and MACE (6.0% vs. 8.3%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.55-0.92). These associations attenuated by three years. The GRACE 2.0 score exhibited robust discrimination for mortality (AUC = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.76-0.82). Continuous interaction analyses showed small model-estimated absolute risk differences in low-risk patients (GRACE <85), whereas the largest model-estimated absolute risk difference was observed in intermediate-risk individuals (GRACE 85-179). CONCLUSIONS: Among STEMI survivors treated with contemporary PCI, associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied according to baseline GRACE risk. No statistically significant association was observed in low-risk individuals (GRACE <85), whereas the association with lower mortality was most evident in the intermediate-risk group (GRACE 85-179). These hypothesis-generating findings warrant evaluation in randomized trials before being used to guide treatment decisions.

recs.title: Psychological Stress and the Diurnal Patterns of Sodium Excretion and Blood Pressure: Results From the SABRE Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological stress is associated with reduced blood pressure (BP) dipping, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study examined the associations among stress-induced sodium excretion, diurnal sodium excretion, and BP dipping. METHODS: Apparently healthy adult participants underwent a laboratory session during which urinary sodium excretion was measured before and after mental stress tasks. Participants then completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring and separate awake and asleep urine collections. The change in urinary sodium excretion rate with stress was defined as the difference in urinary sodium excretion rate before and after stress. The awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate and systolic BP dipping were calculated from the 24-hour urine and BP measurements. RESULTS: In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, mean systolic BP, mean diastolic BP, parental history of hypertension, fasting glucose, and 24-hour creatinine clearance, a smaller stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of urinary sodium excretion rate (n=180, B=0.2253 [95% CI, 0.0490-0.4016]). In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, current smoking, alcohol use, fasting glucose, 24-hour sodium excretion, 24-hour potassium excretion, 24-hour creatinine clearance, and fractional excretion of sodium, a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with lower systolic BP dipping (n=175, B=1.0127 [95% CI, 0.0599-1.9656]). CONCLUSIONS: A lower stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a worse diurnal pattern of urinary sodium excretion, which was associated with lower systolic BP dipping. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT03636490.

recs.title: Failure to Prevent Heart Failure is not a Failure -A Heart Failure Prevention Service facilitates early heart failure diagnosis.
Oscillatory Epicardial Delayed Potentials and Associated Unipolar Voltage Gradients in Brugada Syndrome.
Improved patient value after implementing same day discharge for patients undergoing pulmonary vein isolation.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is an effective intervention to treat atrial fibrillation, which is increasingly prevalent. Same-day discharge (SDD) is a strategic approach to limit procedure-related costs. This study aimed to compare healthcare utilization, costs, and clinical outcomes before and after implementation of an SDD protocol. METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study included 2987 patients undergoing PVI between 1 January 2016 and 1 April 2021. Baseline characteristics, pre-, peri-, and post-procedure healthcare utilization and clinical outcomes were compared before (cohort A; n = 1379) and after (Cohort B; n = 1608) implementation of the SDD protocol using bivariate and multivariate analyses. show that cohort B vs. cohort A had lower all-cause 90-day mortality (0% vs. 0.3%, P = 0.031), no differences in re-ablation < 1 year (P = 0.286), as well as in complications: bleedings (P = 0.177), tamponade < 30 days (P = 0.157), phrenic nerve injury (P = 0.984), thromboembolic complication < 72 h (P = 0.212), or vascular complications (P = 0.290). In terms of healthcare utilization and costs, cohort B had significantly less peri-procedure hospital admission costs (€721.52 vs. €1011.78, P < 0.001) and less total peri- and post-procedure costs (€840.37 vs. €1152.94, P < 0.001). Adjusted for all baseline characteristics, the post-implementation cohort showed on average €315 lower total costs per patient. CONCLUSION: The implementation of the SDD protocol was associated with comparable complication rates while significantly reducing both peri- and post-procedure healthcare utilization and costs, thereby enhancing patient value. This indicates a potential margin for further cost reductions and increased efficiency.

recs.title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE. METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO. RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield. CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

recs.title: Cardiac Myosin-Binding Protein C for Diagnosis of Myocardial Infarction in Patients With Prior Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diagnosing myocardial infarction in patients with prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains challenging, primarily because of lower diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn). cMyC (cardiac myosin-binding protein C), because of its faster release kinetics and greater abundance, may offer improved diagnostic performance in this population. METHODS: The diagnostic accuracy of cMyC was directly compared with that of hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI in a prospective, international, multicenter, diagnostic study enrolling adult patients presenting to the emergency department with acute chest discomfort. Final diagnoses were centrally adjudicated by 2 independent cardiologists using all available clinical and study-specific data, including imaging and serial hs-cTnT measurements. Patients were stratified according to the presence or absence of prior CABG. RESULTS: Among 4752 patients, 387 (8%) had prior CABG (median age, 75 years; 86% men). The incidence of myocardial infarction was significantly higher in patients with prior CABG (38% versus 16%; P<0.001). In the CABG group, the diagnostic accuracy of cMyC as quantified by the area under the curve was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.85-0.92), which was comparable but not superior to that of hs-cTnT (0.89 [95% CI, 0.86-0.92]) and hs-cTnI (0.88 [95% CI, 0.84-0.91]). These findings were consistent across alternative high-sensitivity cMyC assays. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior CABG, cMyC demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for myocardial infarction, but not superior to established hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI assays. REGISTRATION: URL: clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT00470587.

recs.title: Self-Monitoring of Blood Pressure: A Qualitative Study From Iraqi and Syrian Refugees.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) monitoring improves long-term blood pressure (BP) outcomes, but evidence on the acceptability and feasibility of SMBP in refugee populations is limited. Refugees face high cardiovascular risk due to poorly controlled BP. METHODS: We recruited Iraqi and Syrian refugees living in San Diego, California, through the Family Health Centers of San Diego and enrolled them in a 6-week single-arm pilot acceptability and feasibility trial of SMBP with telemonitoring protocol modeled after the TASMIN (Telemonitoring and Self-Management in Hypertension) SMBP trial in the United Kingdom. Postintervention interviews assessed barriers and facilitators of the intervention. Inductive thematic analysis was performed, and results were organized using the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. Quantitative participant data were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: A total of 101 refugees participated (80% Iraqi individuals; mean age, 64±9.7; 49% men). Participants generally favored having their BP readings telemonitored and transmitted to their BP providers' office over completing the physical diary. Facilitators of SMBP included increased self-autonomy, device user friendliness, increased participant confidence, and family support. Barriers included device malfunction, old age, comorbidities, everyday life obligations, diary complexity, and forgetfulness. Participants emphasized for future interventions to promote autonomy, family engagement, and include a streamlined BP tracking method while also integrating provider-patient decision making. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study of SMBP among refugees. The intervention was found to be acceptable and feasible. Participants felt valued, self-autonomous, and confident in SMBP. Future interventions that use technology, family support, team-based care, and user-friendly devices may improve BP control in this population.

recs.title: Association of Air Pollution Exposure and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consistent evidence indicates that air pollution negatively impacts cardiovascular health. However, the relationship between air pollution and atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear, and exposure measurement error has been a significant concern for prior studies. OBJECTIVE: This prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the association of chronic air pollution exposure and risk of AF. METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, a community-based cohort study conducted in 6 U.S. metropolitan areas. Concentrations of 4 pollutants (PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and O3) were assessed from 2000-2018 using hierarchical spatiotemporal models that incorporated cohort-specific monitoring to estimate ambient exposure at participants' residences. In Cox regression models, pollution estimates were represented as time-varying exposures, with 2-year rolling averages updated every 30 days. In our primary model, we adjusted for demographics and health behaviors. RESULTS: Our study included 6618 participants (mean age 62; 53% female). Over 16.5 years median follow-up, we identified 1055 AF events. In our primary model, an interquartile range increment of NO2 (13.5 ppb) was associated with 29% higher risk of AF (hazard ratio 95% CI: 1.00, 1.67). Associations with PM2.5, NOx, and O3 were weaker but also directionally consistent with higher risk. CONCLUSION: We found evidence linking air pollution exposure to risk of incident AF. These results can be used to inform policy and other public health efforts aimed at alleviating the burden of AF, especially given that NO2 exposure estimates (median 17.3 ppb) fell well below the current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency annual standard of 53 ppb.

recs.title: Early Introduction and Prolonged Full-Dose Anakinra Reduce Recurrence Risk After Discontinuation in Recurrent Pericarditis: An International Multicenter Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anakinra is effective in recurrent pericarditis, yet optimal treatment duration and strategies for safe drug discontinuation remain uncertain. Identifying predictors of sustained remission after discontinuation is important for clinical management. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 185 consecutive adult patients with corticosteroid-dependent and colchicine-resistant refractory recurrent pericarditis across 16 international referral centers, who permanently discontinued therapy after clinical remission. The primary end point was pericarditis recurrence after drug discontinuation. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify demographic, clinical, and therapeutic predictors of postdiscontinuation relapse. RESULTS: Among 185 patients who discontinued anakinra (58.4% women, mean age 50.4±17.8 years, 77% idiopathic cause), treatment was initiated a median of 10 months (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-19.5) after the first episode and continued at 100 mg/d for a median of 6 months (IQR, 4-12). Over a median follow-up of 7.2 months (IQR, 1.5-23.3) after discontinuation, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 2.1 months (IQR, 0.7-8.5). Initiation within 12 months from the first pericarditis episode and maintenance of full-dose therapy (100 mg/d) for ≥6 months were independently associated with lower recurrence risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.18-0.66]; P=0.001 and HR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-0.86]; P=0.017; respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Early initiation of anakinra and maintenance of full-dose therapy for at least 6 months are associated with a significantly lower risk of relapse after discontinuation and may inform treatment duration and discontinuation strategies in recurrent pericarditis.

recs.title: The power of proteomics: predicting mortality in heart failure.
Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Physiology-Guided vs Angiography-Guided Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: From the FARGO Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) may reduce unnecessary grafts and improve outcomes. However, in the FARGO (Fractional Flow Reserve vs Angiography Randomization for Graft Optimization) trial, FFR was reduced significantly after 6 months in deferred lesions. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes after FFR-guided CABG compared to angiography-guided CABG. METHODS: In this multicenter randomized clinical trial, 100 patients were randomized to FFR-guided (n = 50) or angiography-guided CABG (n = 50). Patients underwent a 6-month follow-up coronary angiography with FFR in deferred lesions. In this extended long-term follow-up revascularization, myocardial infarction, stroke, death, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), a composite of the individual endpoints, were assessed. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 8.8 years (IQR: 8.3, 9.3), patients in the FFR-guided group had significantly more MACCE compared to the angiography-guided group, (26 [52%] vs 16 [32%], log-rank test P = 0.03). This difference was driven by significantly more long-term revascularization, FFR-guided CABG 32% vs angiography-guided 12%, log-rank test P = 0.01. The revascularization rate was significantly higher from 0 to 1 year (12 [24%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.01), whereas beyond 1 year, rates were similar (4 [8%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.47). Most patients had stable symptoms, and revascularization was symptom-driven. Myocardial infarction (6 [12%] vs 3 [6%]), death (10 [20%] vs 7 [14%]), and stroke (6 [12%] vs 6 [12%]) did not differ significantly between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: FFR-guided CABG was associated with a significantly higher rate of MACCE after CABG, driven by more revascularization within the first year.

recs.title: Myocardial Fibrosis as an Arrhythmogenic Substrate: Integrating Genetics, Imaging and Invasive Electrophysiology for Sudden Death Risk Stratification.
CMR-derived anatomical indices for arrhythmia risk stratification in Ebstein anomaly.
Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy: The Importance of Ring-Like Scar Architecture.
Lp(a)-Reducing Agent Pelacarsen Misses the Mark in Phase 3-Now What?
Lipoprotein(a) and long-term revascularization burden: a recurrent-event analysis of the UK Biobank.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To investigate whether elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with cumulative coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization burden in a primary prevention cohort. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 237 729 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry free of ASCVD at baseline, followed for a median of 14.1 years. Lp(a) was analysed using the ESC/EAS 2025 threshold of 105 nmol/L and continuously (per 50 nmol/L increment). The primary outcome was the total number of coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization procedures per person. Given the genetically determined, lifelong nature of Lp(a) exposure, to capture the full sequence of procedures over time, rather than time-to-first-event alone, we applied recurrent-event statistical models, including the Andersen-Gill model, negative binomial regression, and the Prentice-Williams-Peterson gap-time model. Overall, 10 731 revascularization procedures occurred in 237 729 participants. The proportion undergoing ≥1 procedure was higher with Lp(a) ≥ 105 vs. <105 nmol/L (4.36% vs. 2.96%), with larger differences for ≥2 (1.53% vs. 0.95%) and ≥3 procedures (0.36% vs. 0.18%). In Andersen-Gill analysis, Lp(a) ≥ 105 nmol/L was associated with a higher revascularization rate (HR 1.50, 1.42-1.60), with a 55% higher rate of revascularization procedures during follow-up by negative binomial regression (IRR 1.55, 1.45-1.65). The association was strongest for the first procedure (HR 1.48, 1.40-1.56), attenuated for the second (HR 1.28, 1.09-1.50), and non-significant for the third (HR 1.23, 0.94-1.62). Findings were consistent across coronary and peripheral territories. CONCLUSION: In this large primary prevention cohort, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with a higher long-term revascularization burden across multiple vascular territories. The association was robust for coronary, supportive for peripheral, and inconclusive for carotid revascularization owing to limited statistical power. These findings, derived from recurrent-event methodology, provide a more complete quantification of Lp(a)-associated cardiovascular procedural risk than time-to-first-event analyses alone.

recs.title: Interatrial Shunts for Heart Failure: Safe, But for Who?
Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Incident Cardiovascular Events and Death in Treated Serious Mental Illness, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity have elevated cardiovascular risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have established cardiometabolic benefits in the general population, but their effects in SMI are unclear. We evaluated whether GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death. METHODS: This was a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study of 218 043 adults with SMI, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and active antipsychotic or antidepressant medications in the TriNetX database (73 health care organizations). Outcomes were incident MI, HF, and all-cause death at 1 and 3 years. The primary exposure was GLP-1RA use versus nonuse; secondary analyses examined semaglutide or tirzepatide. Exploratory analyses evaluated sex, race, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use. RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death. Risk differences at 1 and 3 years were -0.007 and -0.010 for MI, -0.011 and -0.018 for HF, and -0.039 and -0.065 for death (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide use was also associated with lower risks of MI, HF, and death (all P<0.001). Findings were directionally consistent after accounting for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use. CONCLUSIONS: Adults with treated SMI, type 2 diabetes, and obesity using GLP-1RAs, particularly semaglutide or tirzepatide, had significantly reduced 1- and 3-year risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death versus nonusers. These pooled associations should be interpreted in the context of SMI's clinical heterogeneity and the limitations of administrative case ascertainment.

recs.title: Dual Control of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels by ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL8.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)-containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies. METHODS: We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr-/- mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8. RESULTS: Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr-/- mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition. CONCLUSIONS: A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase- and endothelial lipase-mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB-containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

recs.title: Look Beyond the Trabeculae: CMR-Substrate Predicts Risk.
Underserved communities at risk of heart failure: effectiveness of community-based recruitment strategies and burden of unrecognised cardiovascular disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients from socioeconomically deprived and ethnically diverse backgrounds are under-represented in cardiovascular research. EARLY-HF is a community-based pilot study designed to predict incident HF in primary care. We aimed to assess effectiveness of recruitment strategies for engaging underserved populations and quantify the burden of unrecognised CVD. METHODS: Prospective cohort study enrolling 550 adults aged ≥50 years with two or more cardiometabolic risk factors and no prior diagnosis of HF. Participants were recruited via: (i) targeted identification using electronic health records in eight primary care centres; (ii) digital advertising and targeted social media campaign; (iii) ten community outreach events; (iv) direct referral from family or friends. The baseline study visit included ECG, blood sampling, and imaging. RESULTS: 185 (34%) participants were from the most deprived Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) quintile and 97 (18%) were of non-White ethnicity. Primary care and digital advertising were the most effective recruitment strategies, enrolling 444 (81%) and 68 (12%) participants respectively, while maintaining diverse representation. The social media campaign generated 15,207 advertisement clicks and 1,012 expressions of interest at a cost of £5.93 per sign-up. Community outreach events enrolled 5 (1%) participants and were resource intensive. A substantial burden of previously unrecognised CVD was identified: 125 (23%) participants had clinically actionable cardiac abnormalities, including 46 (9%) with previously unrecognised myocardial infarction, 331 (60%) had uncontrolled blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg), and 162 (30%) had elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/ml). CONCLUSIONS: Primary care-embedded and digital recruitment strategies can effectively engage underserved communities at risk of HF, at scale and at low cost. This population has a very high burden of unrecognised CVD.

recs.title: Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Improves Atrial Function and Reverses Atrial Remodeling in Dyssynchrony Heart Failure Model.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing may reduce new-onset atrial fibrillation. However, its mechanism and the comparison of atrial reverse remodeling effect between left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) has not been elucidated. We aim to investigate reverse atrial remodeling by LBBP and LVSP in a canine model of rapid pacing-induced dyssynchronous heart failure (DHF). METHODS: Twenty-six beagles followed a 6-week protocol: controls (n=4), rapid atrial pacing (n=4), DHF (n=6), DHF+LBBP and DHF+LVSP (3 weeks DHF followed by 3 weeks LBBP or LVSP, both n=6). Atrial emptying fraction, functional, and electrophysiological parameters were dynamically assessed. Atrial fibrosis was analyzed in tissue samples. RESULTS: Within 3 weeks DHF increased atrial volumes and diminished RA and LA emptying fraction and strains significantly compared with baseline. Subsequent 3 weeks of LBBP increased emptying fraction and strains significantly. At week 6, P-wave duration was shorter in DHF+LBBP than in DHF. Atrial fibrillation was only inducible in DHF animals. Left atrial appendage levels of collagen I/III and α-SMA deposition and fibrosis were lower in DHF+LBBP compared with DHF animals. LBBP reversed atrial structural and electrical parameters to the levels in rapid atrial pacing animals. LVSP improved those parameters compared with those in DHF but did not normalize them to the levels in the rapid atrial pacing animals. CONCLUSIONS: LBBP significantly reverses DHF-induced functional, cellular, and molecular remodeling in the atria, while a smaller amelioration is achieved with LVSP. The findings may explain the reduction in new-onset atrial fibrillation after LBBP.

Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; P=0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; P=0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; P=0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

recs.title: Event-Weighted Desaturation Burden and Cardiovascular Mortality in Sleep Apnoea: Findings from a Large Community-Based Prospective Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obstructive sleep apnoea's prognostic value is limited by reliance on the apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI), which fails to capture physiological heterogeneity of respiratory events. We developed a composite metric, event-weighted desaturation burden (EWDB), integrating weighted respiratory event load, regularity of consecutive inter-event intervals, and cumulative desaturation area. We evaluated its association with cardiovascular mortality and its incremental prognostic value compared with AHI and established hypoxic metrics. METHODS: We analysed 4,904 adults from the Sleep Heart Health Study with baseline polysomnography and adjudicated follow-up. EWDB was derived by combining a respiratory weighted index, a distribution factor based on inter-event interval regularity, and event-linked hypoxic burden (HB). RESULTS: The primary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Over a median follow-up of approximately 11 years, 341 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In fully adjusted multivariable Cox models, higher EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality. However, AHI and HB associations were attenuated and lost statistical significance after full adjustment. EWDB (per 1-SD increase) remained robustly associated with cardiovascular mortality, whereas AHI did not. Incorporating EWDB into a comprehensive clinical model provided incremental risk stratification. Similar robust associations were observed for fatal coronary heart disease and incident heart failure. CONCLUSIONS: EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and provided incremental prognostic information beyond established clinical and sleep-related factors in this cohort. By integrating respiratory event intensity, cumulative burden, and inter-event interval regularity, EWDB may better characterize cardiovascular stress related to sleep-disordered breathing.

recs.title: Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave-corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves. RESULTS: Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m2, P<0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P<0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P<0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P<0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P<0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P=0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid-A wave PAWP (R2=0.96 versus R2=0.86, P<0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P<0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53-2.86]; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

recs.title: Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In hereditary angioedema, a rare bradykinin-mediated condition, oral on-demand treatments facilitating prompt administration and providing rapid, sustained relief and attack resolution remain scant. We investigated the efficacy and safety of deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks. METHODS: RAPIDe-3 was a phase 3, double-blind, 2 × 2 crossover trial in adolescent and adult participants (aged ≥12 to <18 years and aged ≥18 to ≤75 years, respectively) with hereditary angioedema, at 59 sites across 24 countries on six continents. Eligible participants had hereditary angioedema, including those with normal C1 inhibitor associated with a documented genetic variant, at least two attacks within the last 3 months before screening, and experience with effectively using conventional on-demand therapies for hereditary angioedema attacks. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two double-blind crossover sequences to treat two attacks with a 20 mg oral deucrictibant immediate-release capsule or placebo as either deucrictibant-placebo or placebo-deucrictibant, stratified by age and use of long-term prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was time to onset of symptom relief, defined as Patient Global Impression of Change rating of at least a little better. Safety was assessed in all participants who received any dose of study drug. RAPIDe-3 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06343779) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between April 4, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, 149 people were assessed for eligibility, and 134 eligible participants (ten [7%] adolescents and 124 [93%] adults) were randomly allocated. 58 (43%) were male and 76 (57%) were female, and the median age was 38·0 years (IQR 27·0-50·0). 113 participants treated 201 attacks. The primary efficacy analysis included 88 participants with paired treated attacks. Of these, 47 (53%) participants were female and 41 (47%) were male, and 60 (68%), 16 (18%), 4 (5%), and 1 (1%) were White, Asian, Black, and American Indian or Alaska Native, respectively. Onset of symptom relief occurred significantly faster with deucrictibant than placebo, with median times of 1·28 h (95% CI 1·05 to 1·52) and more than 12 h (5·82 to >12), respectively (p<0·0001). Fatigue was the only adverse event reported more than once within 3 days post-treatment: a single event was reported by two participants, one of which was deemed unrelated to treatment. Across the study, no treatment-related adverse events were assessed as severe or serious, and no adverse events led to treatment discontinuation. INTERPRETATION: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration. FUNDING: Pharvaris.

Guideline-Directed Treatment Eligibility and Burden of Untreated Stage-1 Hypertension Under the 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Hypertension Guideline: Insights From NHANES 2015 to 2020.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Adoption of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events risk model in the 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guideline may substantially alter the number and characteristics of adults with untreated stage 1 hypertension who are recommended for treatment. We aimed to quantify treatment-recommendation reclassification among adults with untreated stage 1 hypertension under the 2025 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based guideline compared with the 2017 pooled cohort equations-based guideline. METHODS: This cross-sectional, nationally representative study used data from NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) 2015 to March 2020. The study population included adults aged 30 to 79 years with stage 1 hypertension, focusing on untreated participants. The exposure was the guideline-endorse cardiovascular risk assessment framework, pooled cohort equations, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events, respectively. The primary outcome was recommendation for antihypertensive pharmacotherapy. RESULTS: Among 1926 adults with stage 1 hypertension (weighted 32.57 million), 59.59% (19.41 million) were untreated. Under the 2025 guideline, 13.84% (95% CI, 7.06%-20.63%) of untreated adults eligible under the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events threshold (0.42 million) became newly eligible for pharmacotherapy compared with the 2017 guideline. Newly eligible adults were older (mean±SE, 60.48 [0.77] years) and had higher diabetes prevalence (37.74% [95% CI, 15.45%-60.04%]) than those below the treatment threshold. CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association hypertension guideline recommendations were largely concordant with the prior guideline among adults with untreated stage 1 hypertension, while still newly identifying a subset of individuals with elevated cardiometabolic risk who may benefit from earlier intervention.

recs.title: The Unlucky Occlusion Patients Missed by the STEMI/NSTEMI Paradigm May Be Found by OMI/NOMI.
Cardiac Reverse Remodeling and Clinical Outcomes Following Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitor Therapy in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac reverse remodeling and associated clinical outcomes following angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) therapy in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (EF) remain unclear. We investigated differences in 1-year echocardiographic response after ARNI therapy and predictors of clinical outcomes. METHODS: This study involved patients with HF with reduced EF and ARNI therapy for more than 6 months, using data from a 2-center registry. Echocardiographic data were analyzed at baseline and 1 year after ARNI initiation. Responders were defined as patients with a ≥30% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume at 1 year; all others were nonresponders. The primary outcome was cardiovascular death, and secondary outcomes were hospitalization for HF and all-cause death. Time-by-group interactions in echocardiographic parameters were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: Among 1002 patients (mean age: 64.2±13.7 years; 70.8% men), 451 (45.0%) were responders and 551 (55.0%) were nonresponders. Responders had a lower baseline left ventricular EF but higher left ventricular EF at 1 year (27.0% [95% CI, 22.0-33.0] and 48.0% [95% CI, 42.0-55.0]). Both groups showed improvements in diastolic parameters, with more pronounced changes in responders. In multivariable analysis, nonresponders had a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for HF, and all-cause death (all P<0.001). Male sex and a higher baseline left ventricular EF were independent predictors of nonresponse, whereas systolic blood pressure ≥110 mm Hg and atrial fibrillation were associated with better outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac reverse remodeling after ARNI therapy varies among patients with HF with reduced EF. Positive responders to ARNI therapy at 1 year experienced more favorable clinical outcomes.

Development and external validation of a non-laboratory model to predict early-onset cardiovascular disease risk: a multicohort machine learning study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a questionnaire-based model for two related tasks in adults younger than 65 years: classification of incident early-onset cardiovascular disease (EOCVD) among participants without cardiovascular disease at baseline, and time-to-event prediction of all-cause mortality among participants with EOCVD at baseline. METHODS: Longitudinal data were obtained from CHARLS, HRS, KLoSA, ELSA, and SHARE. The incidence classification analysis included 37,082 participants, and the prognostic survival analysis included 19,478. Eighteen questionnaire or routinely obtainable predictors were used. No laboratory biomarker or imaging measurement was entered into either model, although reported diagnoses may have depended on earlier clinical testing. RESULTS: CatBoost achieved an AUROC of 0.6869, an AUPRC of 0.1438, a precision of 0.1105, and a recall of 0.6512 in the independent SHARE cohort. The Cox proportional hazards model achieved a test-set C-index of 0.7175; its 3-, 5-, and 7-year AUROCs were 0.7314, 0.7348, and 0.7350. CONCLUSIONS: P-EOCVD provides questionnaire-based risk stratification for incident EOCVD and subsequent mortality. Its low precision precludes diagnostic use. The model may support first-step screening where laboratory testing is not immediately available, but prospective validation and recalibration are required before use in under-resourced populations.

recs.title: A multiview video-text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography.
recs.abstract: Invasive coronary angiography is the reference standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, yet assessment is subjective, and existing artificial-intelligence tools typically assess stenosis in individual frames or videos and do not integrate the full multiview angiographic study. Here we show that DeepCORO-CLIP, trained on 203,808 angiographic videos and reports from 28,117 patients, interprets whole multiple-video angiograms at once. It detects obstructive stenoses (≥70%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89 internally and externally, and identifies chronic total occlusion (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.95), intra-coronary thrombus and calcification (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.91). It also predicts 1-year cardiovascular events (AUROC = 0.79, 95% CI of 0.74 to 0.84, versus 0.65 for a model derived using clinical variables) and left ventricular ejection fraction (mean absolute error 7.3% versus 8.8% for a previous model), both achieved using coronary angiography alone. In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, its reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists, with comparable false positives (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38); residual missed stenoses reflected an adjustable threshold rather than an absent signal.

recs.title: Pilot Randomized Trial of 2 Food Purchasing Interventions in Individuals With Hypertension in New Orleans: An American Heart Association Food Is Medicine Initiative.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consuming fruits and vegetables daily is linked to improved health in individuals with hypertension. Voucher incentives have been shown to improve healthy food purchasing. The objective of this study was to compare the effects of an online versus in-store voucher intervention on food purchasing and health outcomes in hypertensive individuals. METHODS: In this randomized pilot trial, 98 participants with uncontrolled hypertension received a $100 monthly food voucher to either an online grocery platform or an in-store local grocery. Both groups received educational materials. The primary outcome was change in self-reported fruit and vegetable consumption. Secondary outcomes were voucher use, engagement with educational materials, and changes in blood pressure, weight, and body mass index. Generalized estimating equations for repeated measures were used to assess changes in food-group consumption over 5 months. RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 57 years, and 65% were women. No difference was detected between arms for self-reported fruit and vegetable consumption. There was an overall 20% (interquartile range, -17% to 93%) increase in fruit and vegetable consumption within both arms. Voucher use was significantly higher in the in-store arm (>90%) than the online arm (<64%). Engagement with educational materials was greater in the in-store arm. No significant changes in weight, body mass index, or blood pressure were observed. CONCLUSIONS: No difference was detected between in-store and online vouchers for fruit and vegetable consumption. Higher engagement and voucher use were observed in the in-store arm than the online arm. Future interventions should be conducted in larger populations and address technological barriers to enhance program effectiveness and assess long-term health impacts. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06214806.

recs.title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest: Is the Catheterization Laboratory Ready to Rescue?
Combined Associations of Glycoprotein Acetylation With Lipoprotein (a) and hs-CRP (High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein) on Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in MESA.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Higher plasma glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) concentrations are associated with an increased risk for incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). We investigated the combined associations of GlycA with lipoprotein (a) (Lp[a]) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) with incident CVD. METHODS: We followed 6676 MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) participants, aged 45 to 84 years, without baseline CVD. Lp(a), GlycA, and hs-CRP were evaluated categorically using standard cut points (Lp[a]: 50 mg/dL; GlycA: 400 μmol/L; hs-CRP: 2 mg/L). We used multivariable-adjusted Cox hazards models to evaluate individual and combined associations of these 3 biomarkers with incident CVD, coronary heart disease, and stroke. RESULTS: Compared with those with low GlycA and low Lp(a) levels, an increase in both incident CVD and coronary heart disease risk was observed for those participants with high levels of either or both of these biomarkers. Risk was highest for those with both high GlycA and high Lp(a) levels (CVD hazard ratio [HR]=1.55 [95% CI: 1.15-2.10) and coronary heart disease (HR=1.92 [95% CI, 1.33-2.77). A similar pattern was not observed for individuals with high levels of both GlycA and hs-CRP. Compared with participants with low levels of GlycA, Lp(a), and hs-CRP, those with high levels of all 3 biomarkers had a 1.98-fold higher CVD risk (95% CI, 1.39-2.82), a 2.23-fold higher coronary heart disease risk (95% CI, 1.45-3.44), and a 2.51-fold higher stroke risk (95% CI, 1.24-5.08). CONCLUSIONS: Routine assessment of GlycA in addition to Lp(a) and hs-CRP may help to identify individuals at particularly increased CVD risk who may benefit from more aggressive preventive therapies.

Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.
recs.abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

Identifying the High-Risk Arrhythmic Mitral Valve Prolapse Phenotype by Imaging.
recs.abstract: Within arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP), a distinct subset of mitral valve prolapse (MVP), there is a small group that carries a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death called malignant MVP. The malignant MVP phenotype is over-represented in young women with unexplained sudden cardiac death on autopsy. AMVP is defined by myxomatous, often bileaflet MVP with mitral annular disjunction, abnormal valvular-myocardial mechanics, complex ventricular ectopy, and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Excessive mechanical force from systolic annular expansion, papillary muscle traction, and basal inferolateral "curling" promotes focal replacement and diffuse interstitial fibrosis, creating an arrhythmogenic substrate. Premature ventricular contractions act as triggers, whereas autonomic modulation influences the timing of ventricular arrhythmia initiation and progression to ventricular fibrillation or sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Baseline evaluation with an electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography is necessary to identify AMVP, exclude severe mitral regurgitation, and identify high-risk markers. If no premature ventricular contractions are found on a resting electrocardiogram, exercise stress testing and extended rhythm monitoring can help bring out ventricular premature contractions, which are triggers of ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance provides incremental prognostic value with late gadolinium enhancement reflecting replacement fibrosis and T1 mapping identifying diffuse fibrosis, even in those with no late gadolinium enhancement. Machine-learning analysis may further refine risk stratification by integrating high-risk features such as mitral annular disjunction, fibrosis extent, and location that outperform symptom-based assessment. As transcatheter and surgical mitral interventions expand, accurate phenotyping of AMVP is increasingly important, as hemodynamic correction of mitral regurgitation alone does not eliminate the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate. Comprehensive multimodality imaging and integrated rhythm assessment are therefore central to individualized risk stratification and management in this vulnerable population.

recs.title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information. METHODS: In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed. RESULTS: Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P<0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis. CONCLUSIONS: Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.
