Calprotectin Accelerates Pathogenic Calciprotein Particle Maturation to Promote Vascular Calcification in Chronic Kidney Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular calcification is a hallmark of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder and a major determinant of cardiovascular mortality. Secondary calciprotein particles (CPP2) are key mediators of vascular calcification; however, the mechanisms regulating their maturation and pathogenic properties remain incompletely understood. CPT (Calprotectin, S100A8/A9), a myeloid-derived inflammatory mediator, is elevated in CKD and predicts cardiovascular events and mortality, particularly under high-phosphate conditions, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: We investigated the role of CPT in vascular calcification using CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice with myeloid-specific CPT deletion. Aortic calcification was assessed by ex vivo imaging, histology, and calcium quantification. Serum calciprotein particle (CPP) fractions were determined by flow cytometry. Mechanistic studies were performed in vascular smooth muscle cells exposed to CPP2 in the presence or absence of macrophage-derived CPT. Calcification propensity was evaluated using the T50 assay, and CPP2 elemental composition was analyzed by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy-energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. RESULTS: Myeloid-specific CPT deletion significantly attenuated aortic calcification and osteogenic gene expression in CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice without altering renal function or systemic mineral parameters. These changes were accompanied by an increased circulating immature CPP fraction. Macrophage-derived CPT markedly enhanced CPP2-induced vascular smooth muscle cell calcification by accelerating CPP maturation, reflected by a shortened T50, and by altering CPP2 composition to be enriched in calcium and phosphate. Although no direct interaction between CPT and CPPs was detected, CPT modified the physicochemical milieu, including ionized calcium and pH. Consistently, CPP2 from CPT-deficient serum exhibited substantially reduced calcification potency, indicating that CPT shapes CPP pathogenicity by modulating particle quality rather than quantity. Importantly, CPT-mediated CPP maturation occurred in a cell-free milieu, indicating a TLR4-independent mechanism distinct from its known receptor-mediated actions. CONCLUSIONS: CPT is a previously unrecognized regulator of pathogenic CPP maturation and composition, thereby promoting vascular calcification in CKD-mineral and bone disorder. Targeting CPT may represent a novel therapeutic strategy to attenuate vascular calcification in CKD.

recs.title: The Impact of Statin Therapy on Postoperative Short- and Long-term Mortality and Morbidity After Non-Cardiac Surgery.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Statins' anti-inflammatory and endothelial-stabilising effects suggest perioperative value, but trials of de novo initiation were discredited following research misconduct. Whether established preoperative statin therapy lowers postoperative mortality dose-dependently remains unclear. METHODS: We studied 56,362 patients aged ≥45 years undergoing non-cardiac surgery at two university hospitals (2016-2023). Preoperative statin exposure was assessed as status (any vs none), intensity (high vs low/intermediate), and regimen (high vs low/intermediate vs none). Primary outcomes were 30- and 365-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting, using random forest-estimated propensity scores targeting the average treatment effect in the treated, was applied to balance measured confounders. Associations were estimated with weighted Cox regression. RESULTS: Overall, 372 patients (0.6%) died within 30 days and 3,735 (6.6%) within 365 days. After weighting, all covariates were balanced. Statin therapy showed a directionally consistent but non-significant association with lower 30-day mortality (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.57-1.07), and was associated with lower 365-day mortality (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.73-0.90; ARD -1.2 percentage points; number needed to treat 83). A dose-response relationship was evident: versus no statin, high-intensity therapy showed a 29% lower hazard (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.60-0.83; ARD -2.3 points) and low/intermediate-intensity a 16% lower hazard (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.74-0.96). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults undergoing non-cardiac surgery, established preoperative statin therapy was associated with dose-dependent lower 365-day mortality. These findings suggest perioperative statin continuation as a preventive strategy and warrant confirmation in a randomised trial.

recs.title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes. METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

recs.title: Anticoagulation strategies during peripheral ultrafiltration in diuretic-resistant congestive heart failure.
recs.abstract: Introduction and objectives Peripheral ultrafiltration (UF) is an effective strategy for the management of diuretic-resistant congestion in patients with decompensated heart failure. However, extracorporeal circuit clotting remains one of the main technical limitations of the procedure, and the optimal anticoagulation strategy during UF has not been clearly established. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different anticoagulation strategies during UF. Methods This prospective, nonrandomized, single-center study included 87 consecutive patients who underwent UF between January 2021 and November 2025. The anticoagulation strategy was tailored according to the patients' baseline anticoagulant therapy: unfractionated heparin (UFH), n = 8; low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), n = 41; vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), n = 12; and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), n = 26. Procedural efficacy was defined as successful completion of the UF session without premature interruption due to extracorporeal circuit dysfunction or clinical complications. Results Baseline characteristics and UF technical parameters were comparable among groups (P > .1). Procedural efficacy was highest with intravenous heparin (UFH = 100%, LMWH = 48.7%, VKAs = 66.6%, and DOACs = 65.4%; P = .048). Extracorporeal circuit clotting was more frequent with subcutaneous heparin (UFH = 0%, LMWH = 31.7%, VKAs = 25%, and DOACs = 27%; P = .018). Conclusions UFH was associated with a lower rate of extracorporeal circuit clotting and a higher rate of successful UF completion. Complications were infrequent. Given the observational design and the small sample size, these findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

recs.title: ST3GAL1-mediated α-2,3 sialylation restrains CD105-TGFβRII signaling to attenuate EndMT-driven atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) contributes to atherosclerotic plaque progression. Although endothelial sialylation is essential for vascular homeostasis, its role in EndMT remains poorly understood. This study investigated the role and underlying mechanism of α-2,3 sialylation in EndMT and atherosclerosis. METHODS: We investigated endothelial α-2,3 sialylation and its regulation during TGF-β-induced EndMT using endothelial cell models. ChIP-qPCR and promoter analyses were performed to determine SMAD2/3-dependent transcriptional regulation of ST3GAL1. IP-MS combined with biochemical validation was used to identify and characterize ST3GAL1 substrates. The functional role of the ST3GAL1-CD105 axis was further examined in vitro and in vivo. RESULTS: TGF-β-induced EndMT was accompanied by selective reduction of α-2,3 sialylation and downregulation of ST3GAL1. Mechanistically, TGF-β directly repressed ST3GAL1 transcription through SMAD2/3 binding to its promoter. ST3GAL1 overexpression restored α-2,3 sialylation and inhibited EndMT in an α-2,3-sialyltransferase activity-dependent manner. CD105 was identified as a major substrate of ST3GAL1, and its α-2,3 sialylation was reduced during EndMT. ST3GAL1-mediated α-2,3 sialylation limited CD105-TGFβRII association, thereby restraining SMAD2/3 activation. In vivo, endothelial-specific ST3GAL1 overexpression or CD105 knockdown inhibited EndMT and attenuated atherosclerotic lesion development. CONCLUSIONS: The ST3GAL1-CD105 sialylation axis is a key regulator of TGF-β-driven EndMT and represents a potential therapeutic target for atherosclerosis.

recs.title: How Pulmonary Embolism Burden Shapes Left Ventricular Strain and Recovery After Thrombectomy.
Heart Failure With Improved Ejection Fraction: What Does "Improved" Mean in Women vs Men?
Aldosterone-Producing Lesions Harboring ATP1A1 and ATP2B3 Mutations: An International Multicenter Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Somatic aldosterone-driver mutations are identified in >90% of patients with primary aldosteronism undergoing adrenalectomy, and they display distinct demographic clustering. ATP1A1 and ATP2B3 mutations, encoding the Na+/K+ ATPase α1 subunit and the Ca2+ ATPase 3, respectively, are relatively rare and are often grouped as ATPase mutations. Differences in their clinical and biochemical phenotypes remain understudied. METHODS: This international collaboration of 16 centers included patients with primary aldosteronism harboring pathogenic variants in ATP1A1 and ATP2B3. Clinical data were collected from medical records. Where available, we compared histopathologic features and steroid profiles (from peripheral and adrenal vein samples) by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. RESULTS: We included 300 patients (mean age, 57±11 years; 85% men) with aldosterone-producing lesions harboring ATP1A1 (204) and ATP2B3 (96) mutations. Age and sex distributions were similar. ATP2B3 mutations were associated with lower serum potassium, higher lateralization indices, and stronger contralateral suppression. Postoperative biochemical cure was achieved in 96% of patients with ATP2B3 mutations versus 83% of those with ATP1A1 mutations (P=0.02). Multiple CYP11B2-positive lesions were observed in 47% of ATP1A1 versus 27% of ATP2B3 cases (P=0.03). Baseline peripheral steroid profiling was available in 126 patients (84 with ATP1A1 and 42 with ATP2B3) and showed higher aldosterone concentrations in the ATP2B3 group (median [interquartile range], 31 ng/dL [20-43] versus 23 ng/dL [11-38]; P=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: ATPase mutations are most common in middle-aged men with lateralized primary aldosteronism. Compared with ATP1A1, ATP2B3 mutations are associated with a more severe primary aldosteronism phenotype, stronger lateralization, and higher rates of single aldosterone-producing lesions and postoperative biochemical cure.

recs.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
recs.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

recs.title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. METHODS: In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. RESULTS: The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSIONS: Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

Genetic Association of Aldosterone Synthase Inhibition With Cardiac Structure, Function, and Heart Failure.

The 'ten commandments' for the 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines on myocarditis and pericarditis.
Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0-42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P<0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm2, regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm2, regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

recs.title: Associations of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 Activity With Markers of Endothelial Dysfunction and Oxidative Stress in Young Healthy Adults: The African-PREDICT Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system plays a major role in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease through, among others, endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Circulating ACE2 (angiotensin-converting enzyme 2) is emerging as a biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk; however, its role in younger populations is not well-established. This study aimed to investigate sex differences in serum ACE2 activity and associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers in young, apparently healthy men and women. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we included 1134 young (aged 20-30 years) men (n=557) and women (n=577). Serum ACE2 activity was measured using a validated fluorometric assay. We analyzed markers of endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and antioxidant capacity. We performed a 2-sample t test and Mann-Whitney U test. We applied multivariable-adjusted Tobit regression analysis to account for left truncation. RESULTS: Men had higher ACE2 activity than women (P<0.001). After multiple adjustments for covariates, ACE2 activity was positively associated with von Willebrand factor (P=0.006), and a disintegrin-like metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motif type 1 member 13 (P=0.019) in men. Among women, ACE2 activity was negatively associated with asymmetric dimethylarginine (P=0.043) and superoxide dismutase (P=0.004). CONCLUSIONS: Serum ACE2 activity was higher in men than women and showed sex-specific associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers. Our results suggest an association between ACE2 shedding and pathophysiological processes associated with alterations in endothelial integrity and early endothelial dysfunction, which may be influenced by sex. This highlights the role of circulating ACE2 as a potential early biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk in young adults. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03292094.

recs.title: Multivariate Genomic Analysis Reveals Shared Genetic Architecture and Potential Therapeutic Targets for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide and comprises multiple clinical phenotypes, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and carotid plaque using genomic structural equation modeling to derive a multivariable ASCVD common factor. We applied fine-mapping, multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation, transcriptome-wide association studies, Mendelian randomization, colocalization, mediation analysis, and virtual screening. RESULTS: We identified 289 linkage disequilibrium-independent lead single-nucleotide polymorphisms mapping to 177 genomic risk loci; 13 lacked corresponding genome-wide significant signals in the input genome-wide association studies. Eleven had prior genome-wide association study catalog association records, whereas no relevant records were identified for the loci represented by rs2294777 near SASH1 and rs4843053 near AKAP13. Fine-mapping prioritized 26 putative causal variants. Integrated functional summary-based imputation, multi-tissue transcriptome-wide association study, and multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation analyses implicated 123 genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted endothelial cells and H3K27ac-marked regulatory regions. Lipidomic analyses linked higher triacylglycerols and sterol esters to increased multivariable ASCVD common factor risk. Protein Mendelian randomization analyses in deCODE and Fenland prioritized aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), phosphodiesterase 5A (PDE5A), HtrAserinepeptidase 1 (HTRA1), and transcription elongation factor A2 (TCEA2) as candidate targets. Colocalization supported a shared causal variant between TCEA2 and multivariable ASCVD common factor. Mediation analyses suggested partial mediation by diastolic blood pressure for ALDH2, PDE5A, and TCEA2 and by triglycerides for TCEA2. Virtual screening identified candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to PDE5A and ALDH2. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating multivariate genome-wide association study with multi-omics and causal inference analyses identified shared genetic signals associated with ASCVD susceptibility and prioritized candidate protein targets, informing future functional studies and target validation.

recs.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026. INTERVENTION: Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics. RESULTS: There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this large, pragmatic clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of 2 hospital-level strategies for second-line vasopressor management in septic shock, a strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower dose of other vasopressors did not reduce 28-day mortality compared with a strategy recommending vasopressin initiation at a higher dose of other vasopressors. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06217562.

recs.title: Impact of Continuous Baseline and Discharge Blood Pressure on Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence linking pre- and post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) blood pressure (BP) with cardiovascular outcomes is scarce. This study investigated the associations of pre- and post-TAVI BP and their changes as a continuous variable with cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI at a tertiary university hospital between 2011 and 2025 with office BP available before and after TAVI were included. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at 1 year. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models incorporating restricted cubic splines for continuous variables were fitted. RESULTS: Among 1191 patients, BP remained relatively stable from pre-TAVI to 1-year follow-up. Both discharge systolic BP and absolute changes therein from pre- to post-TAVI were significantly associated with MACE at 1 year (P<0.001 for both), whereas baseline systolic BP showed no significant association. BP values <115 mm Hg or >143 mm Hg were associated with a higher risk of MACE 1 year after TAVI. A decrease in systolic BP of -5 to -25 mm Hg was also associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with no change. CONCLUSIONS: While BP remains generally stable in the year following TAVI, both very low and high systolic BP at discharge were associated with higher 1-year MACE. Furthermore, moderate decreases in systolic BP from baseline to discharge appear to be protective. These findings highlight the potential prognostic value of BP optimization during TAVI follow-up and support the role of BP measurements as a clinically translatable, independently associated with long-term outcomes after TAVI.

recs.title: Genetic Variants in Intracranial Atherosclerotic Disease: A Systematic Review and Targeted Meta-Analysis Highlighting the RNF213 rs112735431.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) is a leading cause of ischemic stroke and premature mortality, with higher prevalence in specific ethnic groups. Multiple studies have evaluated the association of ICAD and genetic variants. This study aims to systematically review and summarize the current genetic contributors of ICAD. METHODS: Systematic review was performed following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from inception to September 2025 for human studies examining single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) associations and ICAD. Three independent reviewers extracted data on study characteristics, SNVs, alleles and P values. SNVs reported in >1 study were pooled using a fixed-effects model. Expression quantitative trait loci analysis evaluated the regulatory effects of identified SNVs across brain and arterial tissue. Functional enrichment analysis was conducted to identify relevant biological pathways. RESULTS: Fourteen studies met inclusion criteria, comprising a total of 15 535 individuals, of whom 3638 had ICAD. Across these studies, 35 SNVs were identified, mapping to 26 unique genes. In the pooled analysis, ICAD was associated with RNF213 rs112735431 (odds ratio, 18.61 [95% CI, 11.84-29.25]). Other SNVs were found in genes including ADIPOQ, INSR, and NTNG1. Functional enrichment highlighted lipid metabolism and triglyceride homeostasis pathways as key contributors to ICAD risk. CONCLUSIONS: This review consolidates current evidence on SNVs associated with ICAD, highlighting RNF213 rs112735431 as a major genetic contributor, particularly in East Asian populations. Further research is needed to clarify the functional roles of these variants and their potential as therapeutic targets.

recs.title: Cardiovascular Risk in SELECT-Eligible MI Patients With Overweight or Obesity: The Western Denmark Heart Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In the SELECT (Semaglutide Effects on Cardiovascular Outcomes in People with Overweight or Obesity) trial, treatment with semaglutide reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with cardiovascular disease, overweight or obesity, and no diabetes. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to estimate cardiovascular risk in first-time myocardial infarction (MI) patients meeting the SELECT-eligibility criteria and the preventive potential for treatment with semaglutide. METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study applying the SELECT trial's inclusion and exclusion criteria to patients with first-time MI recorded between 2010 and 2021 in the Western Denmark Heart Registry. Five-year incidence of second MI, MACE, and all-cause death was estimated for SELECT-eligible patients with a body mass index (BMI) ≥27 kg/m2. In an assumption-dependent scenario analysis the preventive potential for semaglutide was estimated as the postponement of MACE incidence. RESULTS: In 21,777 first-time MI patients without diabetes, 10,768 patients were SELECT-eligible with BMI ≥27 kg/m2. Median age at first-time MI was 65 years for the SELECT-eligible MI patients and 69 years for normal-weight (BMI 20-26 kg/m2) comparisons. Five-year incidence of second MI (n = 544), MACE (n = 975), and all-cause death (n = 914) was 5.9% (95% CI: 5.4%-6.4%), 10.7% (95% CI: 10.1%-11.4%), and 10.3% (95% CI: 9.7%-11.0%) in SELECT-eligible MI patients, respectively. Among these, treatment with semaglutide was estimated to postpone a 5% MACE incidence by 12 months. CONCLUSIONS: In SELECT-eligible first-time MI patients with overweight or obesity and no diabetes, the cardiovascular risk was substantial with 1 in 10 having a MACE event within 5 years after first-time MI. Based on the SELECT trial results, semaglutide may markedly postpone MACE incidence in these patients.

recs.title: Advancing Heart Failure Classification Beyond Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction: Unsupervised Machine Learning Insights From the Japanese Nationwide Acute Decompensated Heart Failure Cohort: JROADHF.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) classification based on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) inadequately captures HF heterogeneity, limiting phenotype-specific therapies. While machine learning (ML) has been applied to HF with preserved ejection fraction, comprehensive approaches across the full LVEF spectrum remain scarce. This study aimed to identify HF phenogroups across the entire LVEF spectrum using unsupervised ML, moving beyond the LVEF-centric and fragmented understanding of HF. METHODS: We analyzed 13 238 patients with acute HF from a nationwide, multicenter Japanese cohort (JROADHF [Japanese Registry of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure]). Unsupervised latent class analysis identified phenogroups from 46 clinically important admission variables. The primary end point was the 5-year composite of cardiovascular death or HF readmission. RESULTS: Three ML-based phenogroups emerged: (1) "HF with congestion and lower output" (n=2638), (2) "HF with afterload mismatch" (n=3462), and (3) "HFpEF-like HF" (n=7138). ML-derived groups stratified risk for the primary end point (P<0.001), whereas LVEF-based classification did not (P=0.267). Compared with phenogroup 3, phenogroup 1 had a higher age-adjusted risk by Cox regression model (hazard ratio [HR], 1.60 [95% CI, 1.49-1.71]) and phenogroup 2 had a lower risk (HR, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.60-0.70]). Notably, variable-importance analysis by discriminative power for phenogroup assignment indicated that total bilirubin, left ventricular diastolic diameter, and hemoglobin rather than LVEF principally drove classification. CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised ML identified novel HF phenogroups with distinct 5-year outcomes. This framework moves beyond an LVEF-centric paradigm, deepens understanding of HF pathophysiology, and may facilitate phenotype-specific therapeutic development.

recs.title: Comparison of Unfractionated Heparin and Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin in Acute Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Subanalysis of the CLOT-VENUS Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal anticoagulation in acute cerebral vein thrombosis remains uncertain. We compared unfractionated heparin (UFH) and enoxaparin, and identified predictors of functional recovery and UFH responsiveness. METHODS: This retrospective 2-center study from the multicenter international CLOT-VENUS (Collaboration on Cerebral Venous Thrombosis) registry included adults with acute cerebral vein thrombosis treated with UFH or enoxaparin (2004-2024). Baseline clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected. UFH response was measured via a composite responsiveness index (Unfractionated Heparin Composite Response Index) based on partial thromboplastin time. The primary outcome was 6-month functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]), and secondary outcomes included discharge mRS and death. RESULTS: Among 359 patients (median age, 40 [interquartile range, 28-54] years; 68.5% women), 220 (61.3%) received UFH and 139 (38.7%) enoxaparin. Only 64% of partial thromboplastin time values fell within the therapeutic range. UFH was associated with worse outcomes at discharge (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.89; mRS score, 2-6: adjusted odds ratio, 1.90; ordinal mRS score, adjusted odds ratio, 1.56) and at 6 months (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.63). Poor recovery was independently linked to the UFH composite responsiveness index and frequent infusion adjustments. Notably, in the sensitivity analysis limited to patients on UFH with ≥50%, ≥67%, and ≥79% therapeutic partial thromboplastin time values, the outcome differences diminished. Age was independently associated with UFH responsiveness, and female sex, body mass index, and NLR with the number of UFH infusion-rate adjustments. CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with UFH was associated with worse clinical outcomes compared with enoxaparin, largely attributable to suboptimal and inconsistent anticoagulation. However, when UFH achieves consistent therapeutic levels, the outcomes are comparable. Early predictors may help guide individualized anticoagulation strategies.

recs.title: Baseline invasive haemodynamics and treatment response to transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair: an exploratory analysis of the TRI-FR randomised trial.
A Thousand Lesions Before We Understood.
Blood proteome-wide Mendelian randomization reveals molecular pleiotropy in coronary artery disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a common cardiovascular disease characterized by the development of atheromatous plaques. Recent large-scale association study (GWAS) offers an opportunity to better understand the underpinnings of this pathology. METHODS: To investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms of CAD, we interrogated genetic association data for the blood proteome (216,063 cases and 1,246,152 controls for GWAS data and 53,480 individuals for pQTLs datasets). Data were analysed by using Mendelian randomization, inference of ligand-receptor interactions, molecular phenome-wide analysis of genetic variants and tissue-specific protein expression analysis. Pharmacological repositioning study on prioritized proteins was conducted. RESULTS: Using a two-tier replication MR approach with strong instrumental variables (PpQTL<5E-08) we identified 29 blood proteins associated with the risk of CAD, which were common to at least 2 exposition cohorts. Among those proteins, 17 are newly associated with CAD and were not previously reported or mapped in CAD-GWAS. CAD-associated proteome was enriched in ligands whose cognate receptors were expressed in cardiac macrophages and endothelial cells. Molecular phenome-wide association study (MolPheWAS) revealed a group of 10 blood proteins forming a pleiotropic network enriched in functions pertaining to cell migration-differentiation, inflammation and lipid metabolism. Mediation analysis identified TIMD4-APOC3, KLKB1-APOB and COLEC11-ANGPTL4 as strong putative candidate pairs involved in CAD risk. Pharmacological repositioning and tissue-specific protein expression analyses have highlighted 15 possible targets for follow-up investigations, a subset of which is specifically expressed in the liver. CONCLUSIONS: Integrative analyses presented here provide evidence for the involvement of 29 blood proteins in CAD. Those candidate proteins take part directly or through pleiotropic effects in functions pertaining to cell migration-differentiation, inflammation and metabolism.

recs.title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
recs.abstract: AIMS: The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR. METHODS AND RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE. CONCLUSIONS: In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

recs.title: Diagnostic Yield of a Systematic IWT Score-Guided Echocardiographic Pathway for Cardiac Amyloidosis in Patients with Increased Left Ventricular Wall Thickness: A Prospective Multicentre Study.
Conduction System Pacing After TAVR: Promise Meets Evidence.
Occupational Disparities in Cardiovascular Risk and Management in Contemporary China.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although occupational disparities in cardiovascular health are increasingly recognized, a comprehensive understanding of cardiovascular health across contemporary occupational contexts-particularly in rapidly transitioning economies-remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterize geographic and occupational patterns of cardiovascular risk, risk-factor management, and potential prevention opportunities among employed adults in contemporary China. METHODS: In this nationwide cross-sectional study, we analyzed 1,421,390 employees aged 20 to 65 years who underwent health examinations at 167 centers across 24 provinces in China between 2021 and 2023. Eighteen occupations were defined based on participants' employer registration and industry affiliation, and were classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, with the tertiary sector further subclassified into modern, public, and life services. Age- and sex-standardized prevalence of coronary heart disease (CHD) and cardiometabolic risk factors was estimated, along with age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control for hypertension and diabetes, and treatment for hypercholesterolemia and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) control. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk was calculated using the Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China model. We then assessed changes in the proportion of individuals classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk under simulated scenarios that set elevated blood pressure and total cholesterol to target levels and current smoking to noncurrent smoking and compared these reductions across occupations. RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 33.8 years, and 53.4% were male. Overall, the age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD was 1.33% (95% CI: 1.29%-1.37%) and demonstrated a pronounced north-south gradient (P < 0.001), with the highest in the North and the lowest in the South. Cardiometabolic risk factors also exhibited a similar geographic distribution. Employees in modern service sectors exhibited the lowest age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD and cardiometabolic risk factors, particularly those in "information transmission, software, and information technology," whereas the highest burdens were concentrated in the secondary sector, especially in "production and supply of electricity, heat power, gas and water." The age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control were 29.5% and 20.8% for hypertension, 36.6% and 21.9% for diabetes, and 17.0% and 9.5% for hypercholesterolemia treatment and LDL-C control, respectively. Modern services in the tertiary sector had the lowest treatment rates for all 3 cardiometabolic conditions and the lowest control rates for hypertension and LDL-C. Among individuals aged ≥35 years without prior ASCVD, 23.3% were classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk, with marked occupational variation, highest in "agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery" (30.4%) and lowest in "service to advanced manufacturing" (14.7%). Simulated control of elevated blood pressure, hypercholesterolemia, and current smoking revealed substantial occupational variation in potential ASCVD risk reduction. CONCLUSIONS: Occupational context may provide a practical framework for identifying patterns of cardiovascular risk, management gaps, and prevention opportunities among China's working population. Despite lower observed disease burden, modern occupational sectors showed suboptimal risk-factor management, whereas simulated ASCVD risk reductions varied across occupations, highlighting distinct prevention needs and opportunities across occupational contexts.

Substrate Comprising Fibrosis and Epicardial Adipose Tissue-Associated Electrophysiological Remodeling Can Sustain Atrial Fibrillation Drivers: Insights from Image-Personalized Computational Simulations.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computational models of atrial fibrillation (AF) help clarify arrhythmia mechanisms, but the contribution of left atrial (LA) epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is rarely included. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether incorporating EAT-associated effects into fibrosis-based atrial models alters reentrant arrhythmia inducibility, and to characterize the pro-arrhythmic properties of EAT-affected tissue. METHODS: LA fibrosis and EAT were quantified by LGE and Dixon MRI in 19 patients with persistent AF. For each patient, three anatomically identical image-personalized models were built (fibrosis only; fibrosis plus half-epicardial EAT effects, 0.5 mm; fibrosis plus full-epicardial EAT effects, 1.0 mm), yielding 855 simulations. In EAT regions, inward rectifier K+ current was reduced by 35%, intracellular K+ by 50%, and conduction velocity by 25%. RESULTS: Sustained reentry occurred in 370 simulations (43.3%), of which 306 had a functional (rotor-driven) component. Functional reentry inducibility rose from 22.8% (fibrosis only) to 41.4% (half-EAT) and 43.2% (full-EAT). At least one functional reentry was inducible in 12/19 fibrosis-only models, 18/19 half-EAT models, and 19/19 full-EAT models. Median inducible simulations per patient increased from 4 to 6 (p=0.004) and 7 (p=0.003), without significant difference between half- and full-EAT (p=0.895). Fibrosis/EAT overlap regions comprised only 2.1% of the LA wall but were the most arrhythmogenic, with a median 65.5% of their volume harboring reentry versus 8.8% (non-substrate), 37.3% (fibrosis), and 42.8% (EAT) (all p<0.001). In an exploratory analysis of PVI-only ablation patients (n=13), fibrosis-EAT overlap outside the PVI region was associated with 1-year recurrence (log-rank p=0.007). CONCLUSION: Adding EAT effects to fibrosis-based models increased sustained functional reentry, with transmural depth contributing only modestly. Reentry anchored preferentially where fibrosis and EAT effects coexisted.

recs.title: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes.
recs.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

recs.title: U.S. Trends in 10-Year Cardiovascular Risk Scores Over 2 Decades.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equations estimate 10-year risk of total cardiovascular disease (CVD), atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD), coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, and heart failure (HF). OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to describe the trends in PREVENT-based 10-year CVD risk among U.S. adults. METHODS: We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (1999-2023) to estimate 10-year risk of total CVD, ASCVD, CHD, stroke, and HF among adults aged 30 to 79 years. Crude and age-standardized risk scores were calculated for each survey cycle, and orthogonal polynomial coefficients were used to test for trends across 10 continuous 2-year cycles (1999-2018) overall and according to sociodemographic characteristics. RESULTS: Among 26,980 adults, 10-year CVD risk increased 24.4%, from 4.9% in 1999 to 2000 to 6.1% in 2017 to 2018 (P < 0.01). After age standardization, 10-year CVD risk remained stable at 5.4% in both periods. Age-standardized ASCVD risk declined from 3.5% to 3.3% (P = 0.04), driven by a 10% decline in CHD risk from 2.0% to 1.8% (P = 0.01), whereas stroke risk remained stable at 1.7%, and HF risk increased 7.1%, from 2.8% to 3.0% (P = 0.01). Reductions in CHD risk were more pronounced and increases in HF risk more modest among non-Hispanic White adults, those with higher educational attainment, and those with a higher income-to-poverty ratio. CONCLUSIONS: Among U.S. adults, 10-year total CVD risk increased over time due to population aging. Age-adjusted total CVD risk remained stable, with declining ASCVD risk driven by reductions in CHD risk offset by rising HF risk. Socioeconomic disparities in both CHD and HF risk widened overtime.

recs.title: Preventive cardiology: translating the European framework into Dutch practice.
Algorithmic Guardrails for Echocardiography AI: Deep Feature Representations for Error Slicing and Selective LVEF Estimation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Automated echocardiography analysis using artificial intelligence (AI) currently lacks effective guardrails or oversight mechanisms to ensure its safe and reliable deployment. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated whether deep feature representations can identify echocardiograms at risk of misinterpretation by echocardiography AI-based left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) estimation models. METHODS: We retrospectively validated 2 state-of-the-art models for LVEF estimation, EchoNet (single-task model) and PanEcho (multitask foundation model), on 4,010 apical-4-chamber videos from 1,353 studies (n = 1,208) with biplane LVEF measurements in the MIMIC-IV-ECHO database (2017-2019). We extracted 4 deep feature representations from a view classifier, a left ventricle segmentation model, and the 2 validated LVEF estimation models. These features were evaluated for their ability to identify systematic misinterpretations (error slicing) and automatically exclude AI estimates for high-risk inputs (selective estimation). RESULTS: While PanEcho performed better relative to EchoNet (EchoNet minus PanEcho [Δ], Δmean absolute error: 0.31 [0.07, 0.55]; ΔR2: -0.07 [-0.11, -0.03]), both models systematically overestimated LVEF at lower values (proportional bias slope, EchoNet: -0.33 [-0.39, -0.28], P < 0.001, PanEcho: -0.31 [-0.36, -0.26], P < 0.001). All investigated deep feature representations identified error slices for both models. Shared error slices between the models revealed 2 common failure modes: contrast-enhanced echocardiograms and poor-quality apical-4-chamber views. Selective estimation using intermediate features from EchoNet achieved the best performance across both estimation models (area under risk-coverage curve, EchoNet: 5.04 [4.45, 5.66]; PanEcho: 5.21 [4.54, 5.92]). CONCLUSIONS: Deep feature representations can be leveraged to identify and automatically flag misinterpretation-prone echocardiograms, enabling promising guardrail mechanisms for the reliable deployment of echocardiography AI.

recs.title: Left Atrial Enlargement Identifies Risk of Stroke Independent of Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) enlargement has been proposed to increase stroke risk independent of atrial fibrillation (AF), but evidence accounting for AF over time is limited. We tested whether the association between LA enlargement and stroke persist independent of new-onset AF. METHODS: In this observational study, participants from the Copenhagen General Population Study underwent cardiac computed tomography from 2010 through 2018 and were followed until December 2022. LA volume was indexed to body surface area. LA enlargement was defined using sex-specific cutoffs. The primary outcome was incident stroke. Secondary outcomes were incident AF, heart failure, dementia, and all-cause mortality. Individuals with baseline AF were excluded. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using cause-specific Cox models with AF modeled as a time-varying covariate. RESULTS: Among 10 024 individuals (mean age 60 years, 57% women), 684 (6.8%) had LA enlargement. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years stroke occurred in 356 individuals (3.6%). LA enlargement was associated with a higher absolute risk of stroke (11.1% versus 4.6%, risk difference 6.5% [95% CI, 2.4-10.6]) and an increased hazard (adjusted HR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.09-2.05]; P=0.013), which remained similar after adjustment for incident AF, and in separate models using the CHA2DS2-VA score and P-wave terminal force in lead V1. LA enlargement was also associated with higher risk of AF (HR, 3.77 [95% CI, 3.00-4.73]) and heart failure (HR, 3.59 [95% CI, 2.54-5.06]) but not with dementia or all-cause mortality. CONCLUSIONS: LA enlargement was associated with incident stroke independent of incident AF, supporting LA enlargement as a marker of thromboembolic risk.

recs.title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings. METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses. RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62). CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

Left Ventricular Filling Pressure Classification by Electrocardiogram, Echocardiography, and Catheterization: Prognostic Implications.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular diastolic filling pressure (LVFP) is a hallmark of heart failure. Although pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) measured during right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard, echocardiography is more commonly used in practice. OBJECTIVES: The authors previously developed an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) algorithm, trained on echocardiographic assessment, to classify LVFP. The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic implications of LVFP classification by AI-ECG, echocardiography, and PAWP among patients undergoing temporally proximate testing. METHODS: Adults who underwent echocardiography with electrocardiography within 14 days and RHC within 30 days were included. Elevated LVFP was defined as PAWP ≥15 mm Hg, grade 2 or 3 diastolic dysfunction by echocardiography, or elevated LVFP as classified by AI-ECG. Associations with all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed. RESULTS: Among 4,168 patients (median age: 64 years; 47.7% women), elevated LVFP was classified by AI-ECG in 2,383 patients, by echocardiography in 1,643, and by PAWP in 1,841. AI-ECG showed good discrimination for echocardiographic LVFP (AUC: 0.879; 95% CI: 0.867-0.891) and moderate discrimination for PAWP (AUC: 0.711; 95% CI: 0.695-0.727). Over 7.7 years, 1,433 deaths occurred. Elevated LVFP classification by AI-ECG (adjusted HR [aHR]: 1.80; 95% CI: 1.55-2.09) and echocardiography (aHR: 1.74; 95% CI: 1.51-2.02) showed stronger associations with mortality than PAWP (aHR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.31); in discordant cases, AI-ECG better predicted survival. Similar associations were observed for major adverse cardiovascular events. CONCLUSIONS: Despite moderate agreement with PAWP, echocardiography and AI-ECG showed stronger associations with clinical outcomes, suggesting they capture prognostically relevant myocardial information beyond resting hemodynamic status.

recs.title: CAD Complexity in TAVR Patients: Who Benefits From PCI?
Differences in Tricuspid Valve Insufficiency, Mechanical Synchrony, and Cardiac Remodeling Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Right Ventricular Pacing.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac implantable electronic device-induced tricuspid regurgitation (CIED-induced TR) involves primary (lead-induced) and functional etiologies. The impact of left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) versus right ventricular pacing (RVP) on these mechanisms remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and mechanisms of TR among pacing modalities, and evaluate the prognostic significance of these mechanisms. METHODS: We analyzed 225 patients with first-time RV apical pacing (RVAP, n=97) or RV septal pacing (RVSP, n=78) using stylet-driven leads, and LBBAP (n=50) using lumenless leads. Echocardiography and electrocardiography were performed at baseline and 2 years post-implantation. Three-dimensional echocardiography assessed lead interference. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared event-free survival between lead-induced (LITR) and functional TR (FTR) groups. Cox regression identified predictors for adverse outcomes. RESULTS: Despite a higher baseline heart failure burden than RVP (P< .001), LBBAP showed the lowest TR progression rate (20.0% vs RVAP 43.3% vs RVSP 35.9%, P=.020) over 25.8 months. Mechanistically, LBBAP shortened QRS duration (vs RVP widening, P< .001) and demonstrated less lead interference than RVAP (28.0% vs 50.5%, P= .009). Furthermore, LBBAP showed greater left-heart reverse remodeling and improvement in mitral regurgitation, while preserving right-heart structure and function better than RVP. Over 37.4 months, LITR showed worse outcomes than FTR (P= .03). LITR, pulmonary hypertension, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and elevated creatinine were independent predictors for adverse outcomes. CONCLUSION: LBBAP was associated with less CIED-induced TR than RVP, likely through reduced mechanical interference, superior electrical synchrony, and favorable cardiac remodeling. Furthermore, LITR was associated with a worse prognosis than FTR.

Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Class I Obesity: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity may increase the technical complexity of robotic mitral valve (MV) repair, but comparative outcomes with sternotomy remain poorly defined. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic vs sternotomy MV repair in patients with class I obesity. METHODS: A total of 880 patients with class I obesity (body mass index 30-34.9 kg/m2) underwent MV repair at our clinic between 2008 and 2025. After excluding those with mitral stenosis, active endocarditis, prior sternotomy, or concomitant procedures, 429 patients remained. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 132 patients in each group who underwent either robotic or conventional sternotomy MV repair. RESULTS: Median age was 59 years (IQR: 52-66), and 81% were male. Cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were longer in the robotic group than in the sternotomy group (86 vs 65 minutes and 60 vs 48 minutes, respectively; P < 0.001). Robotic MV repair was associated with shorter hospitalization (3.5 vs 5 days; P < 0.001) and a lower postoperative transfusion rate (1.5% vs 10.6%; P = 0.002). There were no operative deaths in either group. No sternal wound infections occurred. Thirty-day readmission was numerically higher after robotic repair (12.8% vs 4.3%; P = 0.064). Ten-year survival was 92% (95% CI: 87% to 97%) with no significant difference between groups (P = 0.83). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with class I obesity, the robotic approach in comparison to sternotomy was associated with lower transfusion rates, shorter hospitalization, and comparable operative mortality and long-term survival relative to sternotomy. Although 30-day readmission was numerically higher among robotic patients, most events were minor and managed without intervention.

recs.title: Endothelial Piezo1 Hyperactivity Drives Neurovascular Dysfunction in Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major driver of neurovascular dysfunction and cognitive decline, yet the molecular mechanisms linking elevated arterial pressure to impaired cerebral blood flow remain poorly defined. Piezo1, a mechanosensitive cation channel enriched in the brain endothelium, is a candidate mediator of cerebral blood flow deficits during hypertension. METHODS: Using 2 distinct mouse models of hypertension-BPH/2J mice (genetically hypertensive strain) and angiotensin II-infused C57BL/6J mice-we assessed brain endothelial Piezo1 activity using patch-clamp electrophysiology. Endothelial-specific Piezo1 deletion models were used to evaluate the role of the channel in hypertension-associated cerebrovascular impairment. Cerebral blood flow responses were measured in vivo by laser speckle contrast imaging, and super-resolution nanoscopy was used to quantify Piezo1 nanoscale organization. Behavioral testing was used to assess cognition. RESULTS: Genetic manipulation of endothelial Piezo1 had minimal impact on baseline blood pressure. However, cerebral endothelial Piezo1 activity was markedly elevated in different hypertension models. Deletion of endothelial Piezo1 protected against hypertension-induced cerebrovascular deficits, including impaired vasomotion, reduced functional hyperemia, and blunted CO2-evoked hyperemia. Super-resolution imaging revealed that hypertension increased Piezo1 clustering, consistent with electrophysiological findings of enhanced channel coupling and open probability. Mechanistically, Piezo1 hyperactivity was PKC (protein kinase C)-dependent, and the PKC-Piezo1 spatial association was enhanced during hypertension. Importantly, PKC inhibition normalized brain endothelial Piezo1 activity, restored cerebral blood flow responses, and rescued cognitive performance. CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension increased the gain of Piezo1 function in brain endothelial cells, promoting dysfunctional neurovascular signaling and cognitive impairment. Targeting Piezo1 or PKC signaling selectively restored cerebrovascular regulation. This work identifies a mechanosensitive pathway that could be leveraged to protect the hypertensive brain.
