Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
recs.abstract: AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo. METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers. RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

recs.title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025. INTERVENTION: Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention. RESULTS: Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

recs.title: Preoperative Angiographic Washout and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Patency.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) failure occurs in 3% to 30% of grafts by 1 year. Because graft flow depends on distal outflow, elevated microvascular resistance may predispose target vessels to graft failure. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to determine whether quantitative target-vessel contrast washout from standard preoperative coronary angiography is associated with subsequent CABG patency. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 107 patients undergoing CABG from 2021 to 2024 with preoperative coronary angiography and postoperative graft imaging by invasive angiography or computed tomography angiography. A total of 201 bypassed target vessels were analyzed. Preoperative angiograms were segmented using a validated neural network, and contrast intensity profiles (CIPs) were generated after isolating each target-vessel runoff territory. CIP downslope was the primary washout variable. The primary outcome was graft failure, defined as graft occlusion or stenosis. RESULTS: Among 201 bypassed target vessels, 152 remained patent and 49 met the criteria for graft failure. Each 1-SD shift toward a shallower CIP downslope was associated with higher odds of graft failure on univariable generalized estimating equations analysis (OR: 1.71; 95% CI: 1.19-2.47; P = 0.004) and after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, and current smoking (OR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.22-2.57; P = 0.003). Model discrimination was modest (area under the curve: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.62-0.78). A downslope threshold of -3,158 stratified graft patency, with faster washout associated with lower failure hazard (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.28-0.90; log-rank P = 0.0193). CONCLUSIONS: Automated quantification of preoperative angiographic contrast washout is feasible and associated with CABG patency, supporting CIP downslope as a potential angiography-derived marker of target-vessel outflow.

recs.title: Coexistance of Carotid Sinus Hypersensitivity and Orthostatic Hypotension in Patients with Unexplained Syncope.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid sinus hypersensitivity (CSH) and orthostatic hypotension (OH) are established causes of syncope but are often considered separate entities. However, evidence suggests that CSH and OH may coexist and jointly contribute to syncope. This study investigates the relationship between CSH and OH in patients with unexplained syncope. METHODS: A total of 1,908 patients aged ≥40 years (age, 63.7 ± 13.0 years; men, 45.3%) with unexplained syncope underwent carotid sinus massage (CSM) and head-up tilt testing (HUT). Occurrence of CSH in classical and delayed OH, including asystolic CSM responses was analysed. RESULTS: Six-hundred-and-eighteen patients (32.4%, 68.9 ± 11.3 years) had OH, while CSH was present in 320 patients (16.8%, 72.2 ± 9.9 years), and was more common in patients with OH than without OH (24.1% vs. 13.3%, p < 0.001). Among patients with CSH, 46.6% also had OH. CSH occurred equally in both classical OH (62/275, 22.5%) and delayed OH (87/345, 25.2%). Among OH patients, CSH was associated with older age, male sex, lower supine diastolic blood pressure, hypertension, and syncope-related hospital admission. An asystolic CSM response was observed more often in OH patients (n = 42; 6.8%) compared with non-OH patients (n = 44, 3.4%, p < 0.001) and was associated with older age and lower resting heart rate. CONCLUSIONS: CSH and OH frequently coexist in adults over 40 years evaluated for syncope. CSM may reveal a clinically relevant cardioinhibitory reflex in a subgroup of OH patients, supporting comprehensive cardiovascular autonomic testing in unexplained syncope.

recs.title: Learning From NATURE: A Second Chance for Thrombectomy in STEMI.
Correction to: Outcomes of simplified left atrial appendage occlusion using the WATCHMAN FLX device: the ROSE-FLX study.
Machine-Learning Prediction of Tumor Comorbidity and Cancer-Associated Mortality in Patients With Coronary Heart Disease: A 2-Stage Modeling Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary heart disease (CHD) with concomitant tumors is increasingly prevalent and is associated with a higher mortality. We aimed to develop 2 predictive models to enable early identification of tumor risk in patients with CHD and mortality risk in those with CHD and cancer. METHODS: We analyzed 134 141 patients with CHD treated at Tongji Hospital (Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, Hubei, China) during 2001 to 2023. Data collected from the First Hospital of Peking University (Beijing, China) were used for external validation. We developed and evaluated 6 machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting, light gradient boosting machine, random forest, neural network, decision tree, and logistic regression). Model explainability was improved using Shapley additive explanation, and an online prediction platform was subsequently implemented. RESULTS: For the model of predicting tumor risk in patients with CHD, extreme gradient boosting showed the best performance in the test set (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve =0.935), achieving the lowest Brier score (0.080). Its sensitivity, accuracy, and F1 score were 0.740, 0.882, and 0.751, respectively. Meanwhile, light gradient boosting machine performed well for in-hospital mortality prediction in the test set (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve =0.965), achieving the lowest Brier score (0.019), and the highest sensitivity (0.677), and F1 score (0.599). The 2 models also showed good performance in the external validation, suggesting a degree of generalizability. CONCLUSIONS: We constructed 2 predictive models to assess the risk of tumor and cancer-associated mortality in patients with CHD. The web platform assists clinicians in decision-making and patient management.

recs.title: Error in Author Name.
The Polypill: The Unmet Need and Great Hope for Heart Failure Patients.
Temporal Dynamics of Complement Activation and Outcome in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated inflammatory responses exacerbate brain injury and affect the prognosis in acute ischemic stroke. METHODS: We characterized longitudinal complement activation after acute ischemic stroke using serial plasma samples from 10 patients and 8 controls. Initial markers of classical (C1q), lectin (mannose-binding lectin), and alternative (complement factor Bb) pathways, as well as regulatory (complement factor H) and downstream markers (C3a, C5a, and C5b-9) were measured by ELISA at 9 time points. RESULTS: Patients with stroke showed broad complement activation, with increased C1q, mannose-binding lectin, complement factor Bb, C3a, C5a, and C5b-9, and reduced complement factor H compared with controls. Complement components showed distinct temporal patterns during follow-up. Complement factor Bb levels were lower in patients with unfavorable functional outcome and in those with moderate-to-severe stroke. C1q and C3a trajectories differed according to functional outcome, whereas C3a trajectories also differed according to stroke severity. C1q trajectories differed according to age group and infarct volume. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest dynamic, pathway-specific complement activation after acute ischemic stroke and highlight the need for larger studies to clarify its prognostic and therapeutic relevance.

recs.title: Impact of Early Atrial Tachyarrhythmia Within the Blanking Period on Late Recurrence After Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early atrial tachyarrhythmias (ERAT) occurring during the first 3 months after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation were not traditionally considered a treatment failure, and this defined the blanking period after thermal energy ablations. More recent data suggest that the blanking period after pulsed field ablation (PFA) is shorter. We hypothesized that the traditional concept of "blanking period" does not apply to PFA for AF. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether ERAT during the 3 months after PFA for AF predicts late recurrence and whether or not the timing of ERAT affects late recurrences. METHODS: All consecutive patients undergoing PFA for AF at our institution (Feb 2024- March 2025) were enrolled in a prospective registry and followed to assess arrhythmia recurrences. ERAT was defined as atrial fibrillation or flutter lasting ≥30 seconds within 90 days. Late arrhythmia recurrences (LRAT) were defined as recurrences after 90 days. RESULTS: Among 1,608 patients followed for 1 year, 334 (20.8%) experienced ERAT and were more likely to experience LRAT than those patients without ERAT (68.4% vs 20.3%, P < 0.001). In multivariable Cox analyses, ERAT was independently associated with LRAT (HR: 4.89; 95% CI: 4.04-5.93; P < 0.001). The risk of LRAT was consistently elevated using 30-day and 60-day ERAT timing cutoffs: ERAT ≤30 vs 31-90 days (LRAT = 70.4% vs 65.5%; P = 0.41; adjusted HR: 5.40 vs 4.34 respectively compared with no ERAT) and ERAT ≤60 vs 61-90 days (LRAT = 68.6% vs 67.1%; P = 0.88; adjusted HR: 4.91 vs 4.83 respectively) compared with no ERAT. In secondary analyses, LRAT rates were similar in ERAT patients with or without cardioversion (73% vs 66.7%, P = 0.29). Interaction testing showed no significant differences in these HRs across ERAT-timing or cardioversion subgroups (all P > 0.05). Moreover, ERAT was associated with a higher need for cardioversion (25.1% vs 7.2%, P < 0.001; HR: 1.49; 95% CI: 1.10-2.02; P = 0.008) and late arrhythmia recurrences compared with patients without ERAT. CONCLUSIONS: After PFA for AF, atrial tachyarrhythmias at any time within the first 3 months, regardless of timing or need for cardioversion, strongly predict late recurrence and warrant increased monitoring intensity in the early postablation period.

recs.title: TRPC1 Promotes Thoracic Aortic Dissection Through Inducing Proinflammatory Phenotype of Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a life-threatening vascular disease that lacks effective pharmacological treatment. Canonical transient receptor potential (TRPC) channels are involved in regulating various cardiovascular functions, yet their roles in TAD have not been elucidated. METHODS: Three-week-old male mice were administered β-aminopropionitrile dissolved in drinking water for 28 days to induce TAD formation. The effects of TRPCs on TAD were explored in vitro and in vivo. RNA sequencing of thoracic aortas was performed to investigate the mechanism by which TRPCs regulate TAD progression. RESULTS: Among the TRPC family members, TRPC1 expression was markedly increased in aortas from β-aminopropionitrile-induced TAD mice along with the downregulation of the vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) contractile markers smooth muscle α-actin and smooth muscle 22. Compared with control littermates, SMC-specific TRPC1 deficiency in mice alleviated β-aminopropionitrile-induced TAD formation characterized by decreased aortic rupture, reduced maximal thoracic aortic diameters, and less elastin degradation. Conversely, SMC-specific knock-in of TRPC1 exacerbated TAD development in mice. Unbiased RNA sequencing showed that TRPC1 knockout in vascular SMCs inhibited the expression of inflammatory factors and chemokines in thoracic aortas during the early stage of β-aminopropionitrile administration. Mechanistically, TRPC1 induced the proinflammatory phenotypic transition of vascular SMCs by activating the calcineurin/nuclear factor-κB pathway, thereby contributing to vascular inflammation and TAD development. CONCLUSIONS: Our study identified TRPC1 as a novel endogenous pathogenic factor for vascular SMC inflammatory phenotypic transition and TAD formation and provided new insights for a comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms during TAD. Blocking the TRPC1/calcineurin/nuclear factor-κB signaling suppressed TAD progression, which may be a promising strategy to address TAD.

recs.title: Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention: The CAUGHT-CAD Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA. METHODS: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes. RESULTS: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium. CONCLUSIONS: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C. (Coronary Artery Calcium Score: Use to Guide Management of Hereditary Coronary Artery Disease [CAUGHT-CAD]; ACTRN12614001294640).

recs.title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
recs.abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

recs.title: Human adult and pediatric multimodal transcriptomic atlas of progression from pressure-loaded to failing right ventricle.
recs.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) independently predicts mortality in heart failure, yet its pathophysiology is poorly understood. Here we present a multi-modal atlas of human right ventricular pressure loading and failure, including bulk (n = 142), single-nucleus (n = 11) and Xenium spatial (n = 9) transcriptomics in adults, plus pediatric (n = 14) and mouse pulmonary artery banding cohorts. Subclustering resolved 34 cell subtypes across 12 lineages along a two-phase trajectory. Phase 1 (non-failing to pressure-loaded) accounts for most of the transcriptional change detectable by bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing and is marked by loss of resident macrophage identity, fibroblast activation, endothelial expansion and erosion of tissue-protective programs. Phase 2 (pressure-loaded to RVF) produces little change in bulk RNA sequencing but is resolved by spatial transcriptomics, engaging multi-lineage fibrotic, endothelial-activation and cardiomyocyte-reactivation programs, with a gain of extracellular matrix (collagen, laminin, thrombospondin) signaling over a stable cell contact adhesion baseline. Mitochondrial respirometry revealed respiratory dysfunction in adult and mouse RVF but not pediatric RVF. Multi-lineage remodeling of the cardiac microenvironment emerges as the central molecular program of RVF, meriting further study as possible disease-modifying targets.

recs.title: Regulatory Considerations for Generative AI: The FDA Asks for Help.
Direct oral anticoagulants vs dual antiplatelet therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion: a meta-analysis of trials.
Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Versus Angiography-Guided Coronary Stent Implantation: An Updated Meta-Analysis.
Long-COVID Associated With Incident Hypertension: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long COVID has been linked to persistent autonomic and vascular abnormalities, but its impact on hypertension among non-hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents remains unclear. Given the link between blood pressure and cardiovascular morbidity, understanding how long COVID modifies the risk of incident hypertension is clinically important. METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal population-based study using MIRACLE-S (Multimorbidity Integrated Registry Across Care Levels in Stockholm). Adults aged 18 to 65 years without prior hypertension or hospitalization for acute COVID-19 were followed from October 2020 to January 2025. Long COVID was defined by a physician-assigned U09.9 diagnosis. The outcome was new-onset hypertension (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] I10). Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs), adjusted for age, socioeconomic status, comorbidities, mental health, and pre-pandemic health care utilization. Analyses were stratified by sex. RESULTS: Among 1 221 570 adults, 8365 (0.7%) were diagnosed with long COVID, and 18% developed incident hypertension during follow-up. Individuals with long COVID (women: n=5578, 16%; men: n=2787, 24%) showed an early and consistently higher cumulative incidence than unexposed individuals (P<0.0001). Long COVID was associated with increased hypertension risk overall (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.09-1.20; P<0.001), and in women (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.05-1.22; P=0.001) and men (HR 1.15, 95% CI 1.05-1.27; P=0.002), with stable estimates across models. CONCLUSION: Long COVID was associated with elevated risk of incident hypertension in non-hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents. These findings suggest SARS-CoV-2 infection may contribute to vascular and autonomic dysregulation affecting blood pressure, supporting structured monitoring and risk management in individuals with persistent post-COVID symptoms.

recs.title: When Universal Is Not Uniform: Sex and the Definition of Myocardial Infarction.
Optimizing Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Women: Pacing Implementation with Scientific Discovery.
Adult Attention Deficit-Hyperactivity Disorder.
recs.abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

recs.title: Unmasking the phenotype in newly diagnosed dilated cardiomyopathy.
In-Stent Restenosis in Transition: Interpreting the Rise of Adjunctive Therapy.
Evaluating Standard Shielding Versus Novel Enhanced Radiation Protection Devices in the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Enhanced radiation protection devices (ERPDs) have the potential to reduce occupational risks in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. We aimed to investigate scatter radiation exposure to various cardiac catheterization laboratory members using 2 ERPDs. METHODS: We prospectively allocated cases to 3 different shielding conditions: standard shielding (group 1), EggNest Protect ERPD (group 2), and EggNest Complete ERPD (group 3). Real-time dosimetry was used to measure radiation exposure at 3 positions: primary operator (position 1), assistant (position 2), and circulating nurse (position 3). Effective dose equivalent was estimated (annualized to 300 cases/y). RESULTS: A total of 135 patients were included in the study (mean age, 68±11 years; 73% men). For position 1, annualized effective dose equivalent -1 doses were 51.4 (19.1-101.3), 7.0 (2.3-21.5), and 2.4 (0.9-6.2) mRem for groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively (P<0.001) standard shielding versus Protect ERPD: 33.1 (95% CI, 11.1-62.9), standard shielding versus Complete ERPD: 41.4 (20.5-71.9). For position 2, annualized effective dose equivalent -1 doses were 2.8 (2.0-6.3), 1.1 (0.6-6.4), and 0.8 (0.3-2.7) mRem for groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively (P<0.001) standard shielding versus Protect ERPD: 33.1 (95% CI, 11.1-62.9), standard shielding versus Complete ERPD: 41.4 (20.5-71.9). For position 3, annualized effective dose equivalent -1 doses were 1.5 (0.6-4.0), 1.5 (0.3-2.4), and 0.8 (0.2-2.5) mRem for groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively (P=0.003) standard shielding versus Protect ERPD: 0.3 (-0.4 to 1.2), standard shielding versus Complete ERPD: 0.4 (-0.1 to 1.4). With the use of the EggNest Complete ERPD without a lead apron, annualized total effective doses are ≤1% of the recommended annual maximum for all positions. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with standard shielding, ERPDs significantly lowered scatter radiation exposure to all members of the cardiac catheterization laboratory.

recs.title: Arrhythmia and dementia: time to think beyond atrial fibrillation.
Diagnostic Accuracy of NT-proBNP thresholds in Dyspneic Patients in the Emergency Department according to patients' characteristics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Concentrations of N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is central to acute heart failure (AHF) diagnosis in dyspneic emergency departments (ED) patients, but optimal thresholds remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of various NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF, across the general population and these key subgroups. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including studies published up to August 28, 2025, that reported the diagnostic performance of NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF in dyspneic ED patients. RESULTS: The analysis included 31 studies comprising 26,948 patients. To exclude AHF, a fixed threshold of ≤300 ng/L yielded an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.73 (0.69-0.77), with high sensitivity of 97.9% (96.9-98.5) and lower specificity of 46.2% (36.4-56.2); the negative predictive value of this threshold was 97.0% (96.5-97.4). Age-dependent thresholds (≥450 ng/L for patients aged <50 years, ≥900 ng/L for those aged 50-75 years, and ≥1,800 ng/L for those aged ≥75 years), evaluated in 14,410 patients, achieved an AUC of 0.84 (0.83-0.85) with a more favorable balance between sensitivity of 85.9% (85.0-86.7) and specificity of 82.0% (81.2-82.9). In patients with CKD (N=2,271), all fixed thresholds yielded AUC <0.80; age-dependent thresholds showed an AUC of 0.77 (0.75-0.78) with specificity of 62.6% (59.4-65.7). In patients with obesity (body mass index ≥30), only age-dependent thresholds were assessed, in 3,562 patients; AUC was 0.82 (0.81-0.84) and sensitivity was 81.2% (79.2-83.1), broadly comparable to the overall population. CONCLUSION: A threshold ≤300 ng/L provides excellent rule-out performance for AHF, while age-dependent NT-proBNP thresholds offer superior diagnostic performance for ruling in AHF in the ED compared to fixed thresholds, and demonstrate consistent accuracy across subgroups. However, evidence in patients with CKD and obesity remains limited, both in terms of sample size and the range of thresholds evaluated.

recs.title: Extended DAPT for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease.
Joint Impacts of Ambient Air Pollution and Temperature on Cardiovascular Disease in West Florida.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature and fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) are well-established contributors of acute cardiovascular events, but their joint short-term effects in subtropical coastal regions have not been well characterized. We evaluated their joint associations with major cardiovascular outcomes in West Florida. METHODS: We analyzed daily hospital admissions for myocardial infarction, heart failure, and stroke within the BayCare Health System from 2017 to 2024. Daily mean temperature and PM2.5 were obtained from national monitoring networks. Joint exposure-response relationships were estimated using distributed-lag generalized additive models with tensor-product interactions across lags 0 to 7 days, adjusting for temporal trends, day of week, and copollutants. Effect modification by age, sex, and race was examined. RESULTS: Temperature showed stronger short-term associations with cardiovascular risk than local PM2.5. Among adults aged ≥65 years, myocardial infarction risk was higher at lower temperatures, compared with higher temperatures (relative risk comparing the 75th versus the 25th percentile of the exposure distribution [RR75/25], 0.92 [95% CI, 0.89-0.95]). Heart failure exhibited a U-shaped temperature-risk relationship, with greater heat-related risk observed among younger adults (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]) and Black patients (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]). In contrast, PM2.5 showed weaker overall associations, with only a modest elevation in stroke risk among Black patients (RR75/25, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.96-1.08]). Joint exposure surfaces revealed outcome-specific nonlinear patterns, particularly for heart failure at higher temperature and PM2.5. CONCLUSIONS: Temperature and PM2.5 jointly influence short-term cardiovascular risk through nonlinear and subgroup-specific pathways, highlighting the need for integrated climate and air-quality strategies to reduce cardiovascular disparities.

recs.title: Lipoprotein(a) in Disaggregated South Asian Groups: An Analysis of MASALA and the UK Biobank.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: South Asian individuals have a high prevalence of elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], but little is known about the variation between disaggregated South Asian subgroups. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to evaluate Lp(a) levels, nongenetic influences, and the association with incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in South Asian populations using data from the Meditators of Atherosclerosis in South Asians Living in America (MASALA) and the UK Biobank (UKB) studies. METHODS: Lp(a) levels were assessed by South Asian country of origin and by state among Indian-origin participants. The association between nongenetic factors and Lp(a) levels was evaluated in multivariable linear regression models. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated the association between Lp(a) and ASCVD events in UKB participants. RESULTS: Among 2,074 MASALA participants born in the South Asian subcontinent (mean age: 56.7 ± 9.6 years), median [Q1-Q3] Lp(a) was 20.7 [10.5-43.0] mg/dL with significant variation by country of origin (P = 0.035). Median Lp(a) was 23 [11-48], 19 [10-37], 22 [11-47], and 17 [10-34] mg/dL in participants from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, respectively. Vegetarian diet, statin use, postmenopausal status, and fewer years in the United States were associated with higher Lp(a) levels while alcohol consumption was associated with lower Lp(a) levels. However, these associations were all very modest. Among 6,845 UKB participants (mean age: 55.1 ± 8.7 years; median Lp(a): 31 [13-65] nmol/L), the associations between Lp(a) and ASCVD did not vary by country of origin or South Asian ethnicity (P interaction > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: There is modest variation in Lp(a) levels, but no difference in the association between Lp(a) and ASCVD outcomes, across South Asian subgroups.

recs.title: Regional Adipose Distribution Reveals Differential Genetic Risk Patterns for Cardiometabolic Diseases.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic risk associated with obesity is increasingly recognized to be strongly influenced by the anatomical distribution and ectopic deposition of adipose tissue, yet the genetic mechanisms linking adipose depots to cardiometabolic diseases remain incompletely understood. METHODS: Using large-scale genome-wide association summary statistics, we systematically characterized shared genetic architecture between 7 magnetic resonance imaging-derived regional and ectopic adipose traits and 20 cardiometabolic diseases, including major cardiovascular outcomes and type 2 diabetes. Genetic overlap was assessed at genome-wide, regional, and variant levels, followed by functional annotation, cell-type enrichment, and phenotype enrichment analyses. Protein-protein interaction networks and molecular docking analyses were further applied to prioritize disease-relevant genes and potential therapeutic compounds. RESULTS: We identified widespread yet heterogeneous genetic overlap, including 109 adipose-cardiometabolic diseases pairs with genome-wide overlap, 92 pairs showing regional concordance across 423 genomic regions, and 146 pleiotropic loci supported by colocalization. Shared variants were enriched in regulatory elements and connected to pleiotropic genes involved in metabolic and inflammatory pathways, including insulin signaling, ion homeostasis, and cellular stress responses. Cell type enrichment analyses highlighted immune, endothelial, and metabolically active parenchymal cells as key contributing cell types. Network and docking analyses further prioritized cardiometabolic disease-related genes such as MMP9, PPARG, and TM6SF2, along with candidate compounds exhibiting favorable binding properties. CONCLUSIONS: This study delineates differential genetic risk patterns linking adipose distribution to multiple cardiometabolic diseases and reveals interconnected metabolic, immune, and vascular mechanisms, providing a genetic framework for cardiometabolic and cardiovascular risk assessment and the prioritization of potential therapeutic targets.

recs.title: Meet the First Authors.
Differences in cardiovascular risk factor prevalence in premenopausal and postmenopausal women compared with age-matched men.
Validating ECG-Based Artificial Intelligence Models for Cardiomyopathy Detection in Obstetric Patients: A Multisite International Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy significantly impacts maternal health worldwide. Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiograms (AI-ECG) have shown effectiveness in detecting left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) in adults and limited obstetric cohorts; however, broad validation in diverse obstetric populations remains unexplored. OBJECTIVES: Our primary objective was to validate the performance of 2 versions of an AI-ECG model for detecting cardiomyopathy in an international obstetric cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multisite study of pregnant or postpartum women (≤12 months) across 11 institutions in 4 countries (Israel, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the United States). Two AI-ECG models (Food and Drug Administration-cleared v2.5.0 and refined v3.0.0) were evaluated against echocardiography. LVSD was defined as left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40% in keeping with the model's training target. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC). RESULTS: We included 1,820 women with paired ECG-echocardiogram data, of whom 7.3% had LVSD. Model 1 (v2.5.0) demonstrated strong discriminative performance with an AUROC of 0.865, sensitivity of 46.1%, and negative predictive value of 95.8%. Model 2 (v3.0.0) showed significantly improved performance, with an AUROC of 0.925, sensitivity of 64.1%, and negative predictive value of 97.2% (P < 0.001) for LVSD detection. CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG models demonstrated strong external validity in a global obstetric cohort, with significantly improved performance in the refined model trained on expanded data. These findings support the potential role of AI-ECG for a scalable LVSD screening tool in obstetric populations, while underscoring the importance of population-specific validation prior to clinical implementation.

Targeting Transmural Substrate: Noninvasive Radioablation for Refractory Chagasic VT.

Pulse pressure in heart failure - easy to assess, not so easy to understand.
Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12, P=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (P=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39, P<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11; P=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23; P=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60; P=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106, P=0.524). CONCLUSIONS: Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.

recs.title: Transcatheter reclosure for residual shunting with incomplete degradation of a biodegradable patent foramen ovale occluder.
Risk-weighted apoB and lipoprotein-associated coronary risk across ethnic groups.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects the number of circulating atherogenic lipoproteins but does not account for differences in particle atherogenicity. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), which incorporates triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), may better capture lipoprotein-driven coronary risk, but its performance across diverse populations remains uncertain. We assessed whether the prespecified triglyceride - and Lp(a)-weighted information captured by RW-apoB was associated with coronary events beyond apoB and compared the discrimination of RW-apoB and measured apoB across ethnicities. METHODS: We analyzed 40,132 participants with 4,509 coronary events from ARIC, CARDIA, MESA, the Framingham Offspring Study, and China Kadoorie Biobank. RW-apoB was calculated using a prespecified equation. Mutually adjusted Cox estimates were pooled within ethnic groups using random-effects meta-analysis. Separate single-marker models compared discrimination. Sensitivity analyses included age and sex adjustment, standardized exposures, hard-events, truncated follow-up, and CKB-specific logistic regression. RESULTS: Mean RW-apoB exceeded apoB by approximately 8 mg/dL in African American and Chinese participants, reflecting higher lipoprotein(a) and triglycerides, respectively. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events conditional on apoB in White, African American, Chinese, and Hispanic participants: hazard ratios per 10 mg/dL were 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.18), 1.11 (1.08-1.15), 1.08 (1.05-1.11), and 1.10 (1.01-1.21), respectively. C-indices for RW-apoB versus apoB were 0.630 versus 0.617 in White (P<0.001), 0.606 versus 0.595 in African American (P=0.085), 0.567 versus 0.554 in Chinese (P=0.014), and 0.540 versus 0.535 in Hispanic participants (P=0.756). CONCLUSION: RW-apoB captured lipoprotein-associated risk beyond measured apoB, with discrimination gains statistically demonstrable in the larger White and Chinese groups.

recs.title: Serbia's national initiative on asymptomatic valvular disease.
Increased Heart Failure Risk After Low-Voltage-Area Ablation in Patients With Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Extensive atrial ablation may impair atrial function; however, its impact on long-term heart failure (HF) risk remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between low-voltage area (LVA) ablation and HF outcomes after catheter ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: This was a long-term follow-up analysis of the Volatile Coronary Lesion and Obstructive Nodal Atrial Fibrillation trial. A total of 398 patients were followed for up to 7 years and classified into 3 groups: no LVAs (group A), LVAs with LVA ablation (group B), and LVAs without LVA ablation (group C). The primary outcome was HF hospitalization. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1,660 (735-2,555) days, HF hospitalization occurred in 21 patients. Sinus rhythm was maintained in 96% of patients, with no differences among groups (P = 0.26). Patients with LVAs had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those without (18% vs 3%; P < 0.001). Among patients with LVAs, HF hospitalization occurred more frequently in those undergoing LVA ablation (30% vs 6%; P = 0.01). In a competing-risk analysis accounting for all-cause death, the cumulative incidence of HF hospitalization remained significantly higher in patients undergoing LVA ablation (Gray's test, P = 0.042). Among patients who experienced HF hospitalization, most events occurred during documented sinus rhythm. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with paroxysmal AF and LVAs, LVA ablation was associated with a higher incidence of HF hospitalization despite a high rate of sinus rhythm maintenance. Given the limited sample size and number of events, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies.

recs.title: Combined Effect of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry on Cardiovascular Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap syndrome has been linked to worse cardiovascular outcomes. Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) is recognized as an early stage of chronic obstructive pulmonary diseas. However, whether the coexistence of OSA and PRISm confers increased cardiovascular risk remains unknown. METHODS: Using data from the Sleep Heart Health Study, participants were categorized into 4 groups according to OSA and PRISm status. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. The secondary outcome was cardiovascular disease mortality. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to evaluate the association of these groups with the risk of cardiovascular outcomes. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.45 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events was 17.00% in non-OSA with normal lung function, 27.52% in non-OSA with PRISm, 25.28% in OSA with normal lung function, and 49.40% in OSA with PRISm. After multivariable adjustment, compared with non-OSA with normal lung function, the adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events were 1.20 (95% CI, 0.82-1.75) in non-OSA with PRISm, 1.04 (95% CI, 0.89-1.21) in OSA with normal lung function, and 1.52 (95% CI, 1.08-2.12) in OSA with PRISm. Corresponding HRs for CVD mortality were 2.02 (95% CI, 1.26-3.24), 1.05 (95% CI, 0.81-1.35), and 2.17 (95% CI, 1.41-3.34), respectively. A significant sex interaction was observed (P for interaction=0.009), with the association present only in women. CONCLUSIONS: The coexistence of OSA and PRISm is independently associated with increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This association is observed predominantly in women.

Toward Targeted Population-Level Screening for Heart Failure.

Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty. RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk. CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

recs.title: Cardiovascular health in transgender and gender diverse individuals: an expert opinion on gender-affirming hormone therapy, risk assessment and clinical management.
recs.abstract: Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) individuals represent a growing population with specific cardiovascular health needs. Current cardiovascular prevention strategies are largely derived from cisgender populations and may not adequately account for the combined effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) and other determinants. This expert opinion summarizes current evidence regarding cardiovascular health in TGD individuals, focusing on the cardiovascular effects of GAHT, population-specific cardiovascular risk factors, practical approaches to cardiovascular risk assessment, and future research priorities. Available evidence indicates that GAHT is associated with changes in cardiometabolic risk factors, haemostasis, vascular function, and cardiac physiology. Feminizing GAHT is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, whereas masculinizing GAHT is associated with adverse lipid changes, erythrocytosis, and a potentially increased risk of major cardiovascular events. However, causal inference is limited by the predominance of observational studies, relatively young study populations, heterogeneous GAHT regimens, short follow-up, and the absence of randomized study evidence. Population-level cardiovascular disparities in TGD should not be attributed to GAHT alone and smoking, obesity, physical inactivity, minority stress, socioeconomic disadvantage, and unequal access to healthcare may independently or interactively influence cardiovascular risk. Current cardiovascular risk prediction tools have not been validated or calibrated in TGD populations and do not account for GAHT exposure or TGD-specific psychosocial and structural determinants. Cardiovascular risk assessment in TGD individuals should integrate conventional risk factors, transgender-related cardiovascular risk factors, and patient involvement regarding individual goals. A coordinated multidisciplinary approach may facilitate personalized cardiovascular prevention while supporting access to gender-affirming care. Future research should prioritize long-term prospective studies and development of risk prediction models tailored to TGD populations.

recs.title: Correction to: Implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy in patients with heart failure and obesity: European Journal of Heart Failure expert consensus document.
Steatotic liver disease phenotypes and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The updated nomenclature of steatotic liver disease (SLD) recognizes distinct phenotypes, including Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). Although cardiovascular risk may differ across SLD phenotypes, their association with stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between SLD phenotypes and ischemic stroke risk in AF patients. METHODS: AF patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Korean health insurance database. According to SLD phenotype, patients were categorized into No-SLD, MASLD, MetALD, and ALD. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke. Subgroup analyses were conducted by CHA2DS2-VA score. RESULTS: Among 196,242 patients (No-SLD: 101,308; MASLD: 77,715; MetALD: 8,678; ALD: 8,541), median follow-up was 5.9 years. Compared with No-SLD, MASLD was not associated with stroke risk (adjusted hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval; 1.00, 0.97-1.04), whereas MetALD and ALD were associated with higher risk (1.09, 1.00-1.18 and 1.16, 1.08-1.26, respectively). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the higher risk associated with alcohol-related phenotypes appeared more apparent at lower CHA2DS2-VA scores; however, the 6-year absolute risk differences were approximately 1% or less, and these findings are regarded as hypothesis-generating. CONCLUSION: In patients with AF, stroke risk was significantly higher in the alcohol-related SLD phenotypes, MetALD and ALD, whereas MASLD was not associated with stroke risk. These findings are consistent with the current recommendations for comprehensive risk-factor management in AF, with particular attention to alcohol intake in patients with alcohol-related SLD phenotypes.

recs.title: Global Prevalence of Adherence to Antihypertensives and Associated Moderating Factors Among Adults With Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a significant public health issue affecting over a billion adults worldwide with adherence to antihypertensives being crucial for achieving sustained blood pressure control and reducing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. To extend previous evidence, we conducted a meta-analysis on global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives among adults. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL. Pooled prevalence of antihypertensive medication adherence was estimated using generalized linear mixed-effects model in R software version 4.4.3. Cochran's Q, τ2, and I2$$ {I}^2 $$ statistics examined statistical heterogeneity with moderator analysis exploring sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis was analyzed using exact fixed-effects model. RESULTS: A total of 123 studies with 1 052 445 adults with hypertension were included. Pooled global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives was estimated at 58% (95% CI, 52%-63%), with 39% for high adherence, 29% for moderate adherence, and 35% for low adherence. Results for sensitivity analysis were 57.91% (95% CI, 57.81%-58.01%) with δ̂ being 24.3%. Prevalence across continents was 67% for Europe, 65% for South America, 60% for Africa, 56% for Asia, and 45% for North America. Adherence to antihypertensives was similar across low-income countries (61%), high-income countries (58), upper-middle-income countries (57%), and lower-middle-income countries (56%). In multivariate model, age and assessment tool only were significantly associated with medication adherence. CONCLUSIONS: Globally, a large proportion of adults with hypertension exhibit moderate to low adherence to antihypertensive medications. Future studies should prioritize establishing consensus-based operational definitions and cutoff values to enhance adherence.

recs.title: Heart Failure Risk in Hypertension: Beyond Left Ventricular Hypertrophy.
Lipoprotein (a) Concentrations Across a Global Cross-Sectional Registry of Patients With Established Coronary Artery Disease.
Lp(a) reduction with PCSK9 inhibitors: How does real-world data stack up?

Antithrombotic Therapy for Secondary Stroke Prevention in Patients With Symptomatic Large-Artery Atherosclerosis and Atrial Fibrillation: A Multicenter Experience.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy for ischemic stroke due to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis in patients with atrial fibrillation remains uncertain. We describe real-world prescribing patterns and outcomes across antithrombotic regimens. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation and ischemic stroke related to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis (intracranial or extracranial or both) at 4 US comprehensive stroke centers. Patients were grouped by discharge regimen: single anticoagulant, single antiplatelet (sAP), single anticoagulant+sAP, dual antiplatelet therapy, or triple therapy (single anticoagulant+dual antiplatelet therapy). Outcomes were recurrent ischemic stroke, symptomatic hemorrhage, and death at 90 days and 1 year. RESULTS: Among 191 patients (median age 75 years [interquartile range [IQR], 68-83]; 40% women; 36% prior stroke/transient ischemic attack), single anticoagulant+sAP was the most common discharge regimen (33%), followed by single anticoagulant (25%), whereas triple therapy was uncommon (4%). More than half of patients switched regimens within 1 year, mostly as the planned duration ended (71%) or following an outcome event (12%). During follow-up (median 68 days [IQR, 28-120]), 21 patients (11%) had recurrent ischemic stroke, and 26 (14%) had symptomatic hemorrhage, over half of each within 90 days; 25% of deaths occurred within 90 days. Ninety-day stroke/death rate was 24%, with single anticoagulant versus 8% with single anticoagulant+sAP; symptomatic hemorrhage rate was 0% and 12%, respectively. At 1 year, stroke/death was 27.3% with sAP, 11.1% with single anticoagulant+sAP, 4.5% with single anticoagulant, and 0% with dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic hemorrhage was similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with atrial fibrillation and symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis, recurrent ischemic events and mortality were common, and antithrombotic management varied substantially. The combination of single anticoagulant+sAP was associated with lower observed short-term stroke/death than single anticoagulant; however, bleeding remains a concern with prolonged therapy. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal regimen and duration for this high-risk population.

recs.title: Coming Full Circle in Transcatheter Mitral Valve Intervention in MAC: Lessons From the ENCIRCLE Registry.
Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models. METHODS: We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially. CONCLUSIONS: Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.
