CardioPharmaGENET: a new European network for pharmacogenomics-driven cardiovascular care.
Associations of Physical Activity and Diet Quality With Mortality and Cardiovascular Disease in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) and diet are cornerstones for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, yet their associations with CVD within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework remain unexplored. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the independent and joint associations of PA and/or diet quality with mortality and incident CVD across CKM stages. METHODS: Our study included 339,074 UK Biobank participants (51.3% women, mean age 56.4 years) with CKM syndrome stage 0 to 4. PA was categorized as high (≥150 min/wk of walking or moderate-to-vigorous activity) or low using self-reported and accelerometer-measured data. Diet quality was classified as low/median/high. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations with incident CVD, cause-specific CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality across CKM stages. RESULTS: High PA was associated with lower risks of all-cause mortality (HR: 0.76 [95% CI: 0.74-0.79]), composite CVD mortality (0.74 [0.70-0.77]), and incident composite CVD (0.90 [0.88-0.92]); for high diet quality, corresponding HRs (95% CIs) were 0.81 (0.77-0.85), 0.81 (0.75-0.88), and 0.87 (0.84-0.90). PA showed nonlinear associations with these outcomes, plateauing at approximately 2,500 metabolic equivalent min/wk. High PA combined with high diet quality showed stronger inverse associations with all-cause mortality (0.64 [0.60-0.68]), composite CVD mortality (0.61 [0.54-0.68]), and incident composite CVD (0.83 [0.79-0.88]). Significant multiplicative interactions between PA and diet quality were observed for stroke mortality, composite CVD, and heart failure. The joint associations with these outcomes were stronger at more advanced CKM syndrome stages. CONCLUSIONS: Beyond individual benefits, joint PA-diet modification was associated with lower risk of mortality and CVD across CKM stages, highlighting the value of integrated behavioral strategies.

recs.title: Evaluating the Role of Lower Extremity Elastic Bandage in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity compression therapy has been proposed as an adjunct to mitigate diuretic resistance during acute decompensation of heart failure (ADHF). We evaluated the effect of lower leg compression with elastic bandages on diuretic efficiency in patients with diuretic-resistant ADHF. METHODS: Historical cohort study enrolling adult cardiac ICU admissions with ADHF who used elastic bandages (EB) at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota from 2007 to 2017. The diuretic efficiency before and after applying EB was the primary outcome. RESULTS: A total of 176 patients with heart failure who received elastic bandages were included. The in-hospital mortality rate, the median hospital length of stay, and 30-day hospital readmission were 9.7%, 11.4 days (IQR 7.1-19.0), and 11%, respectively. When EB was applied, the average daily loop diuretic dosage was decreased by a mean difference of 1.19 mg per 40 mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: 0.22 to 2.2; p = 0.016). The average post-EB diuretic efficiency was 1,355 mL (IQR 1,119, 1,590) per 40-mg furosemide, which was significantly higher than before EB application, with a mean difference of 340 mL per 40-mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: -554, -125; p = 0.002). A higher diuretic efficiency led to lower diuretic doses. Average daily urine output before and after EB application was not different (2,642 pre-EB vs. 2,792 post-EB mL/day; 95% CI: -455 to 154; p = 0.33). CONCLUSION: EB use enhances diuretic efficacy during ADHF. Further studies are needed to determine the potential clinical benefits and risks of applying EB compression treatment in ADHF.

recs.title: Stroke Risk-Based Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: ALONE-AF Post-Hoc Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Discontinuation of oral anticoagulant (OAC) in patients without recurrent atrial arrhythmia after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has been demonstrated to reduce composite outcomes of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with continued OAC. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the optimal OAC strategy according to baseline stroke risk and AF recurrence. METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of the Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation after Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF) trial, patients were stratified according to CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 and ≥3. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared between the OAC discontinuation and continuation subgroups. The cumulative incidence of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding at 2 years was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with competing risk analysis accounting for AF recurrence. RESULTS: Among 840 patients, 584 and 256 had a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 (mean age 62.0±7.5 years, 15.9% female) and ≥3 (mean age 68.9±7.3 years, 45.3% female), respectively. In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≤2 stratum, the primary outcome occurred in one patient (0.4%) in discontinuation subgroup vs. six (2.4%) in continuation subgroup (absolute difference -1.9 percentage points, P=0.066). In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 stratum, two events (1.8%) occurred in the continuation subgroup only (absolute difference -1.8 percentage points, P=0.172). All major bleeding events (n=5) occurred in the continuation subgroups. Competing risk analysis yielded consistent results. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were observed between OAC strategies when stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc score, though event numbers were limited. Larger prospective trials are needed to confirm these observations. TRIAL REGISTRATIONS: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04432220.

recs.title: Transpulmonary Gradient vs Pulmonary Vascular Resistance for Post-Transplant Risk Stratification.
Refining Care Pathways for MINOCA: Lessons from the DOMINO Registry.
Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Risk-Factor Burden in Patients Presenting With Premature ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
One-Year Systolic Blood Pressure and Subsequent Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights from a Swiss Prospective Cohort.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Current guidelines recommend targeting systolic blood pressure (SBP) below 130 mmHg in patients at high cardiovascular risk, including after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), although evidence specific to the post-ACS setting remains limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of SBP measured 1 year after ACS on subsequent cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: The ELIPS cohort prospectively enrolled ACS patients across four Swiss tertiary-care centers (2009-2017). Patients alive at 1 year with available SBP measurements were included. The association between SBP at 1 year and 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke/transient ischemic attack, or non-fatal myocardial infarction) was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for age, sex, renal function, cardiovascular risk factors, index-event type, coronary revascularization, cardiac rehabilitation, heart-failure history, and antihypertensive medication classes. RESULTS: Among 2,074 patients (age 63±12 years; 82% male; 53% STEMI), 229 MACE events occurred over a median follow-up of 4.0 years (2.7 per 100 patient-years). The SBP-MACE relationship was nonlinear and J-shaped (P-non-linearity=0.007), with lowest risk between ∼130 and 140 mmHg (formally estimated nadir 138 mmHg [95%CI 116-152]). Above 140 mmHg, each 5-mmHg increase was associated with a borderline increase in MACE risk (adjusted HR 1.08; 95%CI 1.00-1.17). The pattern was broadly consistent across sex, age and hypertension status, with a possible interaction with diabetes that could not be excluded (P-interaction=0.08). CONCLUSIONS: In this large, predominantly male, well-characterized post-ACS cohort, SBP measured 1 year after ACS showed a J-shaped association with cardiovascular risk, with lowest risk at 130-140 mmHg.

recs.title: Unipolar Electrograms at the Pulmonary Vein Antrum: Spatial and Directional Heterogeneity with Distinct Postablation Morphologies.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Disappearance of the near-field S-wave in the unipolar electrogram (U-EGM) is commonly used to assess lesion formation during pulmonary vein (PV) isolation; however, interpretation of U-EGMs in anatomically complex atrial regions remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize spatial, directional, and postablation changes in antral PV U-EGMs, and evaluate the limitations of conventional waveform interpretation. METHODS: In 15 patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation, U-EGMs were recorded at 116 antral PV sites during sinus rhythm and distal coronary sinus (CS) pacing before and after ablation. U-EGM morphology and R- and S-wave amplitudes were analyzed. RESULTS: Baseline U-EGMs showed spatial heterogeneity, with a small r and deep S in the right anterior PV antrum transitioning to a positive-dominant morphology (Rs) in the left-lower PV antra. Distal CS pacing altered the activation sequence, causing direction-dependent changes, most prominently in the right PV antrum. After ablation, overall S-wave amplitude decreased from -0.94 ± 0.70 to -0.08 ± 0.55 mV (P<0.001). Residual negative deflections ≥0.5 mV persisted in 18.1% (21/116) of recordings, frequently in association with direction-dependent far-field activity. Newly developed positive deflections ≥1.0 mV were observed in 17/116 sites (14.7%; mean 1.42 ± 0.42 mV), predominantly in the right-sided antra. CONCLUSIONS: Antral PV U-EGMs frequently represent composites of near- and far-field signals with spatial heterogeneity and direction-dependent variation. Postablation responses are diverse, including S-wave disappearance, residual negativity, often reflecting contributions from overlapping far-field components, and newly developed positive deflections. PV-antral U-EGMs should be interpreted in the context of their composite nature.

recs.title: Monopolar biphasic pulsed field ablation and coronary endothelial function: the Vasc-PFA study.
Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group. CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

recs.title: Association of Non-Cytochrome P450 3A4-Metabolized Statins Versus Atorvastatin With Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Cancer Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Propensity Score-Matched Target Trial Emulation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often undergo CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4) metabolism. Atorvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate, whereas rosuvastatin and pitavastatin largely bypass this pathway. We evaluated whether statin choice was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in TKI-treated patients with cancer. METHODS: Using TriNetX, we conducted an active-comparator, new-user target trial emulation among adults with cancer receiving their first TKI. The index date was the first statin dispensation; outcome ascertainment began on Day 30 and continued up to 3 years. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons included rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin (primary; 2215 per group), pitavastatin comparisons, and a pooled non-CYP3A4 statin comparison. RESULTS: Among 10 843 eligible patients (mean age, 66.7 years; 60.7% male), rosuvastatin was associated with a lower major adverse cardiovascular events rate than atorvastatin (624 versus 769 events; hazard ratio [HR], 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.93]). The proportional-hazards assumption was violated (P=0.042), so the HR was interpreted as a time-averaged association. The pooled comparison was concordant (HR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.96]). The early-persistence Day-180 estimate was imprecise (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.09]). CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin use was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events than atorvastatin in TKI-treated patients with cancer. This observational finding is compatible with, but does not establish, a CYP3A4-mediated interaction. Residual confounding, nonaligned TKI and statin timing in part of the primary cohort, and lack of individual-level event-time data require prospective confirmation.

recs.title: Do Extracellular Vesicles and the Biochemical Microenvironment Contribute to Amyloid Transthyretin Cardiomyopathy?
Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI. METHODS: Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified. RESULTS: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA. CONCLUSIONS: IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

recs.title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications. OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes. METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events. RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157). CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.

recs.title: Pulmonary Embolism-Attributable Mortality in Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in the United States from 2010 to 2023.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) are at increased risk of pulmonary embolism (PE) and related mortality, yet contemporary US trends remain incompletely defined. We examined PE-attributable mortality from 2010 to 2023 among patients with ASCVD, stratified by age, sex, race, ethnicity, urbanization, and region. METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research data (2010-2023) to assess PE-attributable mortality among patients with ASCVD aged ≥15 years using age-adjusted mortality rates. Concurrent trends in age-adjusted ASCVD prevalence and risk factors were evaluated using NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey). Age-adjusted mortality rates were analyzed with Joinpoint regression to estimate average annual percentage change (95% CI), and trends in NHANES were assessed using linear models. RESULTS: From 2010 to 2023, 152 386 US patients with ASCVD aged ≥15 years (80 015 male, 72 371 female) died from PE. PE-attributable AAMR rose from 3.62 to 4.96 per 100 000 (annual percentage change +3.1%; P<0.001), with a modest increase from 2010 to 2018 (annual percentage change +0.7%, P=0.003) and a sharp rise from 2018 to 2023 (annual percentage change +12.8%, P<0.001). Age-adjusted mortality rate was highest in non-Hispanic/non-Latinx Black American individuals, and American Indian/Alaska Native and Hispanic/Latinx populations had the steepest increases. Adults <65 years, rural areas, and the Western United States showed disproportionate rises, whereas the South had the highest absolute deaths. Such trends paralleled increasing ASCVD prevalence, which was driven by hypertension, obesity, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease. CONCLUSIONS: PE-attributable mortality among US patients with ASCVD rose from 2010 to 2023 particularly among young-to-middle-aged adults, socioeconomically isolated ethnic and racial groups, and Western residents.

Sedentary Behavior, Physical Activity, and Sleep During Pregnancy and Offspring Health: Protocol for the Pregnancy 24/7 Offspring Multi-Site Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a major public health concern that increases cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease theory posits that obesity and CVD risk is, in part, programmed in utero. A greater understanding of modifiable maternal factors that associate with offspring obesity and CVD risk in childhood could inform primordial prevention interventions during pregnancy. Maternal sedentary behavior, physical activity, and sleep during pregnancy are modifiable and plausible determinants of offspring obesity and CVD risk yet remain insufficiently studied. This protocol describes the design of the Pregnancy 24/7 Offspring Study (NCT07172880), developed to address this gap in knowledge. METHODS: This study examines associations between device-based maternal 24-hour movement behavior (sedentary behavior, physical activity, and sleep) measured in each pregnancy trimester and analyzed via trajectories and as compositions with offspring obesity and CVD risk through 24 months of age. Maternal 24-hour movement behavior data and birth outcomes were previously collected in the Pregnancy 24/7 Cohort Study (N=500, Iowa, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia). The Offspring study extends this cohort by enrolling up to 450 maternal-offspring dyads and collecting new measures in the offspring, including body mass index z-score from birth through 24 months obtained via medical record abstraction, anthropometry, indicators of CVD risk, and maternal questionnaires. The primary outcome is body mass index z-score trajectory; secondary outcomes include adiposity, blood pressure, and brachial-femoral pulse wave velocity. CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this study will advance understanding of how maternal 24-hour activity associates with early-life obesity and CVD risk, informing primordial prevention strategies during pregnancy.

American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals. RESULTS: Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.

Lipoprotein(a) and Coronary Artery Disease Polygenic Risk Scores Do Not Improve Secondary Manifestations of Arterial Disease Score Prediction of Coronary Events After Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Survivors of ischemic stroke are at high risk for coronary artery disease (CAD), but individual risk varies. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and CAD polygenic risk scores (CAD-PRS) improve risk prediction in primary prevention; however, their prognostic value after stroke remains uncertain. We assessed whether Lp(a) and CAD-PRS add predictive value to the Secondary Manifestations of Arterial Disease (SMART) secondary prevention score. METHODS: We analyzed 1202 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry with prior ischemic stroke and no CAD at baseline (2006-2022). Baseline clinical characteristics, Lp(a), and CAD-PRS were recorded. The primary outcome was incident CAD, identified from hospital, primary care, and death records. Competing-risk models compared SMART alone with SMART plus Lp(a), CAD-PRS, or both. Ten-year model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and Brier score. Prespecified subgroup analyses examined age, sex, diabetes, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.4 years, 155 participants (12.9%) developed CAD. SMART alone provided moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.64-0.75]) and a Brier score of 0.08. Adding Lp(a), CAD-PRS, or both did not improve prediction (change in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, ≤0.002; all P>0.6; continuous net reclassification improvement, ≤0.03; all P>0.20). Results were consistent across subgroups, with no significant interactions after correction for multiple comparisons. CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors of ischemic stroke without CAD, neither Lp(a) nor CAD-PRS improved prediction of incident CAD beyond the SMART score. These findings do not support their incremental use for coronary risk stratification in this population.

recs.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).
